records.requirement: `Auth.Builder.build()` shall throw `AuthConfigException` when `.apiKeyScheme(String)` is empty, contains a character outside the RFC 9110 `token` set (including space or comma), or equals `Bearer`, `Basic`, `Digest`, `DPoP` or `Negotiate` ignoring case, and shall accept exactly one scheme name with no aliases.
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R47 (1) (22nd edition scheme rules, 23rd edition added DPoP and Negotiate); §7 row `.apiKeyScheme(String)`; §6.4 row "R47 × 스킴 설정 검사".
records.research: - Decisive facts: the forbidden names are the standard HTTP schemes a client or proxy could already send (`Bearer` would collide with JWT verification). Only RFC 9110 token characters are allowed so the scheme fits the `credentials` grammar. One scheme only: a key is never accepted under two names, which keeps the 401 challenge list (`Bearer, <scheme>`) unambiguous.
records.implementationNotes: - Validate in `Auth.Builder.build()`; compare reserved names with `String.equalsIgnoreCase` (no locale-sensitive lower-casing). `AuthConfigException` is defined by scope AUTH.

records.title: Versioned common HTTP contract and retained legacy routing profile

acceptanceCriteria.text: FR-ROUTE-018/019/020/021 and FR-APP-021/022 govern common HTTP string/Pattern/alternative matching, stack order, duplicates, Route identity, mounts and hooks. The strict segment grammar, priority and conflict rules of FR-ROUTE-003/005/006/007/008 remain contracts for retained routing.Router/RoutePattern/RouterPolicy and the separate WS profile, not the new HTTP default stack.

FR-HTTP-027 governs common HTTP current raw path/URL/parameter views instead of FR-HTTP-009's historical decoded-path checkpoint; existing rawPath/scalar/numeric conveniences and shared strict capture decoding remain available. Root/traversal/symlink/file boundaries and malformed capture errors are not weakened.

FR-APP-021/022/023 and FR-HTTP-028 replace the historical universal HTTP freeze/single-use/no-async/automatic-empty-response/405/default-method constraints in FR-HTTP-008/021/024/026, FR-APP-003/004, CON-APP-002 and IR-APP-002. Server/configuration/service/WS lifecycle guards and the legacy middleware/upgrade profile remain separately tested.

FR-APP-021/024 and FR-HTTP-028 govern common HTTP static/error layer position and method/final outcomes instead of the historical static-fallback order in FR-STATIC-001/002. File access safety, conditional/Range semantics, stream ownership and explicitly configured static/error convenience behavior remain regression obligations.

Each affected current-runtime test is updated only with the relevant new requirement and positive/negative evidence for the changed behavior; existing direct legacy/WS tests are retained or explicitly relocated to the preserved profile. No test is weakened or disabled to obtain green.

The host records a per-requirement old-to-new conflict matrix and independent review. Old verified checkpoint status/evidence is left historical; all new requirements require their own TDD/coverage/commit evidence before verified. Raw transport restrictions not resolved by existing dependencies remain an explicit local decision and are not silently waived.

The explicit typed CORS extension retains FR-DX-010 AC-6: error fallback clears ordinary application headers and preserves only tracked framework CORS grant/Vary metadata, including credentials, without grant override by application/HttpException headers. Common HTTP final handling without that CORS extension preserves ordinary app headers as Express does. Both policies have separate positive/negative runtime tests; the existing CORS privacy assertions are not weakened.

records.research: - Allowed JDK surface (00 §2): javax.crypto.Mac, java.security (SecureRandom, Signature, MessageDigest), java.net.HttpURLConnection, java.text.Normalizer, java.util.concurrent, FileDescriptor.sync. Forbidden because above API 21: java.time (API 26, replaced by TimeSource and epoch-ms long), java.util.Base64 (API 26, use internal Base64Url), java.nio.file (API 26), CompletableFuture and java.util.function (API 24; UserMutator is its own SAM, 00 §7). Pitfall: JCA algorithms requested by name (e.g. PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 via SecretKeyFactory) are not statically checked by animal-sniffer, which is why PBKDF2 is implemented in-house over Mac (TOKEN scope). acceptanceCriteria.text: com.snoworca.naruserve.utils, utils.auth and each public subpackage (jwt, password, user, group, rbac, audit, apikey, spi and testing, all in the NaruServe-api main jar; testing per IR-AUTH-005 AC-7) have a package-info.java annotated @org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked, and ApiJarClasses.PUBLIC_PACKAGES lists every one of them.

The FR-KT-001 nullability check passes over those packages, utils.auth.testing included: every public method return type and parameter that may be null carries @Nullable (for example Auth.userOrNull, Auth.loadUser, AuthEventContext.getOrigin, AuthRejection.getRetryAfterSeconds, AuthPrincipal.getApiKeyId), every other reference type is non-null through the package's @NullMarked default without an annotation, and, as FR-KT-001 AC-3 requires, no org.jspecify.annotations.NonNull appears on any type, member, parameter or type use in those packages. Where another 0.11.0 requirement or 00 writes a position as @NonNull, that means non-null by this default, never the @NonNull annotation.
The FR-KT-002 keyword check passes: no public method name in those packages is in, is, object, fun, when, val or var.

A callback interface in this AC is exactly what the FR-KT-003 AC-1 inventory (CallbackInventory.inventory) counts: a public interface in those packages that is the parameter type of a public method or constructor of a type in those packages and has exactly one abstract method after dropping Object methods and default methods. Every such interface (for example TimeSource, UserMutator, AccessRule) is annotated @FunctionalInterface, is listed in CallbackMatrix.CALLBACK_TYPES so the FR-KT-003 AC-4 exact-equality test stays green, and is used as a Kotlin lambda in CallbackMatrixKotlinTest (a trailing lambda for a callback parameter, or a Kotlin lambda implementation for an SPI type, as FR-KT-003 AC-3 does for ExchangeHandler) that a request through the in-memory harness reaches (for UserMutator, a route handler calling auth.users().update(id) { ... }), so the FR-KT-003 AC-3 test 'z every CALLBACK_TYPES interface was exercised' stays green. Interfaces with no abstract method or with more than one are outside this rule and need neither @FunctionalInterface nor a Kotlin lambda: store and SPI interfaces with required abstract methods (for example UserStore with its five required methods, GroupStore, ApiKeyStore and PasswordHasher) keep them (00 §5, 00 §6.3 ApiKeyStore table, CON-AUTH-006 AC-4), and AuthEvents, whose methods are all default no-ops, is covered by CON-AUTH-006 AC-3. The root `build.gradle` declares, per module, exactly these main dependencies: `NaruServe-api` none; `NaruServe-servlet` `NaruServe-api`; `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` `NaruServe-api`, `com.snoworca:tinyhttpd-core` and `com.snoworca:tinyhttpd-websocket` at the pinned TinyHttpd version of CON-BUILD-018; `NaruServe-gson` `NaruServe-api`, `com.google.code.gson:gson:2.14.0`; `NaruServe` `NaruServe-api` and `NaruServe-gson` in `api` and `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` in `implementation`; `NaruServe-kotlin` `NaruServe` and `org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib` in `api`; `NaruServe-slf4j` `NaruServe-api`, `org.slf4j:slf4j-api:1.7.36`; `NaruServe-filelog` `NaruServe-api`; `NaruServe-logcat` `NaruServe-api`; `NaruServe-proxy` `NaruServe-api` only; `NaruServe-android` `NaruServe` and `NaruServe-logcat` in `api`.

records.research:
- Why reopened: FR-ENGINE-008 chose Express `trust proxy = true` semantics (left-most XFF) and rejected trusted-address lists and hop counting with "reopen if a deployment needs hop counting". 00 §8 reopens that decision because the left-most value is client-chosen (06 S4 (b): with `trustProxy` on, a client rotates the left-most value and IP limits never trigger), which is a Core-wide defect, not an auth detail.
- Decision: keep the method and its behaviour (binary and behavioural compatibility for 0.10.0 apps) and warn in Javadoc and docs; the safe modes are new methods, not a behaviour change of the old one.
- Rejected alternative: changing `trustProxy(true)` to mean `trustProxyHops(1)`. It silently changes `remoteAddress()` for existing apps behind multi-hop proxies and breaks FR-ENGINE-008 AC-2; reopen at a major version.
- Rejected alternative: `@Deprecated` now. 00 does not ask for it, and deprecation warnings would hit every 0.10.0 user before the replacement is proven; reopen when hop/CIDR modes have shipped one release.
- Pitfall: docs tests pin exact text (OPS-ENGINE-002 AC-4 `WaveFiveDocsTest.appAndRequestNameServerTrustProxyAndKeeper`); add the warning without removing the asserted facts, or re-point the assertion in the same change.

records.requirement: The system shall not use `runBlocking` as an asynchronous adapter: no class of a published module references `kotlinx.coroutines`, no published module has a `kotlinx-coroutines` artifact on its `compileClasspath` or `runtimeClasspath`, and the build check `checkNoCoroutines` fails the build when either appears.
records.rationale: Covers D-356. Measured (2026-10-20): `grep -rn "runBlocking\|kotlinx.coroutines"` over `NaruServe*/src` and `src` finds no match; `docs/api/kotlin.md` documents that `suspend` handlers are unsupported in v1 and that `runBlocking` holds the request thread. Decision: the check is separate from the wave 1 `checkClassReferences` and `checkDependencyRules` tasks, because `BuildLayoutTest` pins the exact `prefixes += [...]` list of `build.gradle`; the new check scans constant pools of the main output of the nine published modules for `kotlinx/coroutines/` and reads each module's resolved `compileClasspath` and `runtimeClasspath` for group `org.jetbrains.kotlinx`, artifact `kotlinx-coroutines-*`. Pitfall: the existing prefix `kotlin/` does not match `kotlinx/` because of the slash. Rejected alternative: adding a coroutine adapter in `NaruServe-kotlin` with `runBlocking`; it would hold a request thread per suspend call and hide the cost behind a friendly signature; reopen when a separate non-blocking coroutine module is designed (post-v1).

records.requirement: The reference DDL of `JdbcApiKeyStore` shall define, for SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL, the key table with all `StoredApiKey` fields, a case-sensitive unique index on prefix (MySQL `utf8mb4_bin` or `ascii_bin` collation), an index on `(owner_user_id, expires_at, owner_ver)` and an index on `(expires_at)`, and, for MySQL and PostgreSQL, the lock table `naru_api_key_owner(owner_user_id PRIMARY KEY)` whose rows are never deleted; the SQLite DDL need not include the lock table because SQLite issuance takes a database-wide write lock with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (REL-APIKEY-007).

records.research: - Decisive facts: the lock table exists so the API key store can lock per owner without locking the user table, which may not be JDBC at all; its rows stay after user deletion (one small row, ids are never reused, §4.3). MySQL's default `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` treats base62 upper and lower case as equal, raising collisions and returning other keys' rows; PostgreSQL default collation and SQLite `BINARY` already compare case-sensitively. auth still re-compares the returned prefix byte-wise. The owner index serves limit counting, `listByOwner`, `deleteStaleByOwner` and `deleteFutureByOwner`; the `(expires_at)` index serves `deleteExpired`. The key table's name and exact column names are not given in 00 (name not final).

records.title: API key expiry judged without leeway on the evaluating node's clock, and scheduled deletion of expired keys

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a fixed `TimeSource` where `nowMillis()` equals the key's `expiresAt`, a key request gets 401 `invalid_api_key`.
With `nowMillis()` equal to `expiresAt - 1`, the same key authenticates.
A key issued through `auth.apiKeys().issue(owner, name, null, scopes)` (expiresAt null) still authenticates with `nowMillis()` set to `Long.MAX_VALUE - 1`.
`ApiKeyStore.deleteExpired(nowMillis)` removes keys whose non-null `expiresAt` is less than or equal to `nowMillis` and keeps keys with null `expiresAt`.

Scheduled cleanup (00 R47 (6) "dead keys": expired keys are deleted by the R42 10-minute cleanup scheduler; §6.3 ApiKeyStore table, `deleteExpired` row, used by the R42 cleanup scheduler at a 10-minute interval): with `.apiKeys(store)` set, a fixed `TimeSource` past key K's `expiresAt` and a non-expiring key N, after one run of the same 10-minute daemon cleanup scheduler that calls `RefreshTokenStore.purgeExpired` (FR-TOKEN-002 AC-5), `deleteExpired` has been called once with that `nowMillis`, `findByPrefix(K's prefix)` returns null and N remains; without `.apiKeys(store)` the scheduler makes no `ApiKeyStore` call; after onStop no further `deleteExpired` call happens. An exception from `deleteExpired` leaves request responses unchanged (IR-APIKEY-004 AC-6).

records.research: - Decisive facts: unlike JWT, no leeway, because key lifetimes are in days and a few seconds of skew do not matter. `expiresAt` is absolute; under `MULTI_INSTANCE` issuing and evaluating nodes may differ, so expiry moves by the clock skew between nodes; operators keep clocks in sync with NTP (doctor clock check, §4.4). records.title: Personal access token endpoints under /auth/me/apikeys

acceptanceCriteria.text: `POST /auth/me/apikeys` with a correct `password`, `name` `ci`, `scopes` `["posts:read"]` returns 201 with the plaintext key in the body; a following `GET /auth/me/apikeys` lists the key with `status` `active` and no secret or hash field.

`POST /auth/me/apikeys` with a wrong `password` returns the same 401 as a wrong current password on `/auth/password` and counts toward the R34 (7) per-user-id limit (15 minutes, 5 attempts); the 6th wrong attempt in 15 minutes gets 429 `too_many_attempts` with `Retry-After`.
`POST /auth/me/apikeys` by a user whose `passwordHash` is null (SSO) returns the same 401 as a wrong password.
A user holding only `posts:read` requesting `posts:write` gets 403 `insufficient_scope`.
`DELETE /auth/me/apikeys/:id` with another user's key id or an unknown id returns 404 `NOT_FOUND`; with an own key id it deletes the key without a password.
`POST /auth/me/apikeys` with `"password": null` or no `password` returns 400 `BAD_REQUEST`.

An access token whose JWT is expired on `POST /auth/me/apikeys` gets 401 `invalid_token` and the handler does not run (principal-required credential endpoint); because keys are on, the challenge is `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", ApiKey` (the configured scheme name; header owned by SEC-FLOW-003 AC-4 and IR-FLOW-001 AC-4).

Constant-work password confirmation (00 R38, editions 21 and 24): on `POST /auth/me/apikeys` and on `POST /auth/admin/apikeys` (FR-APIKEY-004 AC-10), a wrong password and a caller whose `passwordHash` is null each take one hash slot and run exactly one target-cost PBKDF2 (a dummy for the null hash, counted through an instrumented hasher), and the 401 is sent no earlier than the SEC-TOKEN-009 floor max(1.25T, elapsed) plus 0-50 ms jitter (with HashCost.calibrate(250 ms), so T = 250 ms per PERF-TOKEN-001 AC-6, a measurement stub, a fast fake hasher that records one verify at the target iteration count (so the elapsed time stays below 312.5 ms on any machine) and an injected scheduler: scheduled at 312.5 ms plus jitter, never earlier, as in SEC-TOKEN-009 AC-2); a correct password is not delayed by the floor.
A PAT issued by user u1 through `POST /auth/me/apikeys` is stored with `issuedByUserId` = u1 (owner and issuer are both u1), and the issue audit event names u1 as the issuer (00 R47 (3), 24판).

CSRF and Origin on the key-issuing subject-required endpoints (rule owned by SEC-FLOW-006 and SEC-FLOW-007, same outcome as SEC-FLOW-014 AC-9): in COOKIE, and in BOTH with no Authorization header, a valid `naru_at` of family F and a correct `password`: `POST /auth/me/apikeys` and `POST /auth/admin/apikeys` without `X-CSRF-Token` (same-origin `Origin`) -> 403 `csrf_failed`; with F's `X-CSRF-Token` and `naru_csrf` but `Origin` `https://evil.example`, not in trustedOrigins -> 403 `csrf_failed`; in each case no key is inserted and no password hash runs.

records.title: Admin API key endpoints under /auth/admin/apikeys and their check order

acceptanceCriteria.text: `GET /auth/admin/apikeys` without `ownerUserId` gets 400 `BAD_REQUEST`; `?ownerUserId=u1` returns u1's keys with `status`, including when u1 is disabled; an unknown `ownerUserId` gets 404 `NOT_FOUND`.

`POST /auth/admin/apikeys` with an unknown `ownerUserId` gets 404 `NOT_FOUND`; with a disabled owner that passes R31 gets 400 `BAD_REQUEST`; with a disabled owner protected by R31 target protection gets 403 `insufficient_scope`; none of the three runs the password hash or counts toward the R34 (7) limit.

`POST /auth/admin/apikeys` with empty `scopes` and an unknown `ownerUserId` gets 400 `BAD_REQUEST` (body check first); `"ownerUserId": null`, a body without `ownerUserId`, `"ownerUserId": 7`, missing `name` and `"name": 7` each get 400 `BAD_REQUEST` before any owner read or password check.

With a stolen access token: no `password`, and separately `"password": null`, each get 400 `BAD_REQUEST` before any owner read or password hash, and neither counts toward the R34 (7) limit; a wrong `password` gets 401 and counts toward the R34 (7) per-user-id limit (00 R47 (5) JSON null 25판, R47 (10), §6.4 rows "R47 × JSON null 비밀번호" and "R47 × 관리 발급 비밀번호").
Admin A issues a key for service account S: the stored key's `issuedByUserId` is A and the issue audit event names A; `ownerUserId` equal to the caller is allowed with the same password check.
A delegated admin deleting admin's key with `DELETE /auth/admin/apikeys/:id` gets 403 `insufficient_scope`; an unknown key id gets 404 `NOT_FOUND`.
A caller whose `passwordHash` is null gets the same 401 as a wrong password on `POST /auth/admin/apikeys`.

A delegated admin holding `auth-apikeys:write` and `posts:*` issuing a `posts:read` key for an enabled owner holding `*` gets 403 `insufficient_scope` (R31 target protection on the owner although the new key scope is covered); no key is inserted and no password hash is run.

`POST /auth/admin/apikeys` is registered with methodAsync and its password check uses the shared hash slot (REL-TOKEN-001): with all hash slots taken, a pending request holds no worker thread. The same registration for `POST /auth/me/apikeys` is owned by IR-FLOW-002 AC-5.

The password check is last so rejected requests do not spend the hash slot or the R34 (7) budget. Disabled owners are refused because disabling raises `ver` but enabling does not (R37), so a key minted on a disabled account would work the moment it is re-enabled. Revoking another user's key needs R31 (2) target protection; the key row is read by id to find the owner. No list of all keys in v1.

records.title: Key count limit, lifetime bound and issuance body validation

acceptanceCriteria.text: An owner with 20 live keys: PAT issuance gets 409 `api_key_limit`; app `issue` throws `AuthRejection(409, "api_key_limit")`; admin issuance gets 409 `api_key_limit`.

With the off-request stale-key deletion held (an injected executor that does not run queued tasks, so `deleteStaleByOwner` has not run; REL-APIKEY-002), an owner with 5 expired keys and 15 keys made stale by `?all=true` (0 live keys): PAT issuance gets 201, and the list shows those keys with `status` `expired` and `stale`.
PAT or admin issuance with `expiresInDays` 400 (above the default 365), 0, 1.5, or the string `"30"` each gets 400 `BAD_REQUEST`.
PAT issuance without `expiresInDays` stores `expiresAt` equal to the issuance time plus 365 days in milliseconds (31536000000 ms).
PAT issuance with empty `scopes`, missing `name`, `"name": null` or a non-string `name` gets 400 with body `code` `BAD_REQUEST`, produced through Core `HttpException(400)` (not `AuthRejection`).
With `.maxKeysPerUser(2)` and `.maxApiKeyDays(30)`, a third live key gets 409 `api_key_limit` and `expiresInDays` 31 gets 400 `BAD_REQUEST`.

Scopes that break the R46 grammar (FR-IAM-005 AC-1), `["Posts:Read"]` and, separately, `["po*"]`, from a caller holding `*` with the correct `password`: `POST /auth/me/apikeys` gets 400 with body `code` `BAD_REQUEST` through Core `HttpException(400)`, not 403 `insufficient_scope`, and no key is inserted; `POST /auth/admin/apikeys` with the same scopes gets the same 400 `BAD_REQUEST`, also when `ownerUserId` names no user (not 404), and runs no owner read and no password hash (00 R47 (10); R47 (6) 29th edition: the body check comes before the owner checks and the password check).

Exception in MULTI_INSTANCE: invariant-violating keys still count (see the status requirement).

records.title: Service accounts without passwords

acceptanceCriteria.text: `POST /auth/login` with a service account's name returns the same 401 as a wrong password, takes the same dummy-hash time, and counts toward the R34 login counters.
Admin `PATCH` A4 that sets `password` on a service account gets 400 `service_account_no_password`.

A2 with the service-account flag and a `password` gets 400 `service_account_no_password` when the actor is a JWT admin (a key actor gets 403 `api_key_not_allowed` first, whatever its scopes: SEC-APIKEY-008 AC-7, AC-9).
Recovery (R31 (6)) whose target is a service account gets 400 `service_account_no_password`.
A `UserMutator` that changes the service-account flag of an existing user throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

A service account created through `auth.users().create` with the flag round-trips `isServiceAccount()` true through `InMemoryUserStore` and `FileUserStore`, and the `UserStore` Javadoc states that an app-provided store must persist the service-account flag (Javadoc test).
Audit events for actions by a service account mark the actor as a service account.

records.title: RestApp.create() looks up the bootstrap AppFactory through ServiceLoader

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp.create()` is a `public static` method of the `RestApp` interface returning `RestApp`, and `RestApp` declares no other `create` overload. [D-110; residual: class-loader overload]

Through the internal lookup helper and a dedicated class loader that exposes exactly one fake provider at `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory`, the helper returns the app the provider's `create()` returned. [D-226; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: the lookup uses `ServiceLoader.load(AppFactory.class, loader)` where `RestApp.create()` passes `RestApp.class.getClassLoader()` and never the thread context class loader.

With a class loader that exposes no provider, the helper throws `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `com.snoworca.naruserve:naruserve` and mentions `RestApp.builder()`; `RestApp.create()` itself throws that exception in the `NaruServe-api` test run, where no provider is on the class path. [D-227]
With a class loader that exposes two providers, the helper throws `IllegalStateException` whose message names both provider class names. [wave decision: RestApp.create()]

The fake providers live in the `NaruServe-api` `test` source set, not in its `testFixtures`, so no other module's tests see a provider, and `NaruServe-api` main has no compile-time reference to TinyHttpd or Gson. The provider classes are compiled in `src/test/java`, but their `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory` file is not on the test class path: the test writes it into a temporary directory that only the dedicated class loader sees. [D-226; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: the dedicated class loader is a `URLClassLoader` over the temporary directory whose parent loader holds the nested fake provider classes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-15]

records.title: Per-app state isolation and the NEW-state guard

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two apps built in one JVM with different routes, middleware, loggers and `onStart` registrations each answer only their own routes, run only their own middleware, log only to their own logger and expose only their own services and attributes. [D-113]

A reflection scan finds no non-`final` static field and no static field of a mutable collection type in the classes of `com.snoworca.naruserve` and `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` other than compile-time constants and `private static final` arrays that are never written after class initialisation (such as `MethodSet` `METHODS` and `DefaultResponse` `EMPTY`). [D-113]

In each of the states `STARTING` (called from an `onStart` callback), `RUNNING`, `STOPPING` (called from an `onStop` callback) and `TERMINATED`, each of `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `options`, `route(Method, ...)`, `route(MethodSet, ...)`, their route-middleware overloads, `use(mw)`, `use(prefix, mw)`, `accessLog`, `logger(l)`, `onStart`, `onStop`, `onError`, `routerPolicy` and the `get`/`use` methods of a `RouteBuilder` obtained in `NEW` throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the method and the current state, and the refused call changes nothing. [D-114; wave-4 carried: NEW-state rule]

Every guarded method calls one internal guard method, so a test that lists by reflection all non-static `RestApp` methods returning `RestApp` (including `logger(Logger)`) and the registration methods of a `RouteBuilder` obtained from `route(String)` finds each one rejected in `RUNNING`, while `logger()`, `state()` and `route(String)` itself are not guarded. [D-114] Decision: the one guard is the internal `AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable`, called first by every guarded method. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-3 SDS-AC-4]

The after-freeze rejection of verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5 still holds, because the one guard rejects when the state is not `NEW` or the route table is frozen (the harness and the FR-HTTP-008 tests freeze while the state is still `NEW`); FR-HTTP-008 AC-6 states the wave 3 situation that D-111 ends, and its wave 3 test is re-pointed to assert that `RestApp.builder()` and `RestApp.create()` are the only public static methods of `com.snoworca.naruserve` that return a `RestApp` or its builder. records.title: Middleware scope and pipeline order in the dispatcher

acceptanceCriteria.text: With global middleware `g1`, `g2`, prefix middleware `p1` on `/api` registered before `g2` and `p2` on `/api`, and `app.route("/api/users").use(r1).use(r2).get(h)`, a `GET /api/users` records `g1, g2, p1, p2, r1, r2, h`, and `app.get("/b", r3, h2)` makes `GET /b` record `g1, g2, r3, h2`. [D-120; D-119; T35] Decision: all global middleware run first in registration order, then all matching prefix middleware in registration order, however the two kinds of registration interleave. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-1] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

Prefix `/api` runs for `/api` and `/api/users` and not for `/apix` or `/ap`; prefix `/api/` behaves as `/api`, and prefix `/` runs for every path. [D-118; T35] Decision: a trailing `/` of a prefix is ignored and `/` covers every path. User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

With `RouterPolicy.builder().caseInsensitive(true)` the `/api` prefix middleware runs for `/API/users`, and with `mergeSlashes(true)` it runs for `//api//users`, so every path that reaches a route under the prefix runs the prefix middleware. [D-118] Decision: the prefix comparison uses the same case and slash normalisation that the router applies under the app's `RouterPolicy`. User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

Inside prefix middleware and the handler, `req.path()` still returns the full decoded path (for example `/api/users`, not `/users`). [D-118; D-137] Decision: NaruServe does not strip the mount prefix from `req.path()` and has no `baseUrl`. User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

A request that matches no route runs global and matching prefix middleware and then receives the `404` of the fallback point; route middleware of other routes does not run. [D-121; D-117] Decision: for a lookup result other than `MATCHED` the dispatcher builds the `Request` with the parsed `Method` and empty params and runs the global and matching prefix middleware with an empty route middleware list and the fallback answer as the terminal step. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-6] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

A recording global middleware runs once each for a `405` (method mismatch), a `426` (WebSocket-only route without upgrade), an automatic `OPTIONS /r` `204`, a `501` for `TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and a `501` for `CONNECT /`, before the automatic response is written. [D-117; wave decision: Pre-request rejections] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

A global middleware does not run for the pre-request rejections (unrecognised method token `501`, raw path not starting with `/` `400`, `PathValidator` rejection `400`, `OPTIONS *` `204`) nor for the lifecycle-gate `503`s of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.
For a matched route all middleware and the handler run on the adapter thread that called the dispatcher, one after the other. [D-128]

records.title: next.run() contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: A middleware that calls `next.run()` twice gets `IllegalStateException` from the second call, and the downstream middleware and handler ran once. [D-122; T35]

A middleware that calls `next.run()` after `res.send("x")` completed the response gets `IllegalStateException` and no downstream middleware runs; a `Next` kept and called after the request ended (from the test thread after the in-memory exchange finished) throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-123] Decision: `next.run()` throws when the response is `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` or the request has ended, and no downstream step runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-10]

A middleware that records a marker after `next.run()` returns sees the handler's marker already recorded and `res.isCommitted()` true for a handler that called `res.send(...)`. [D-124] Decision: an exception thrown downstream propagates out of `next.run()` unchanged and the dispatcher hands it to the error path once, so a middleware may wrap `next.run()` in `try`/`catch`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-11]
A middleware that writes `res.status(401).send("no")` and returns without `next.run()` delivers `401` with body `no`, and the later middleware and the handler record no call. [D-125; T36]

Calling `next.error(e)` after `next.run()` in the same invocation, or `next.run()` after `next.error(e)`, throws `IllegalStateException`; `next.error(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-122; D-116] Decision: `next.run()` and `next.error(e)` together count as the single continuation of one invocation. Decision: `next.error(null)` throws before the continuation is consumed. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-12]
`next.run()` runs the downstream chain on the calling thread, and no middleware or handler runs after the dispatcher returned to the adapter for a non-streaming response. [D-128]

records.title: Unified error path and onError chain

acceptanceCriteria.text: With one recording `onError`, a `RuntimeException` thrown by a middleware, a checked `IOException` thrown by a handler and `next.error(e)` from a middleware each reach the handler once with the same `Throwable` instance and the request's `Request` and `Response`. [D-127; D-129; T36] Decision: a thrown `java.lang.Error` is not routed to `onError`; it aborts the response and is rethrown, as in wave 3. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-1]

An `HttpException(400)` thrown by a handler, an `HttpException(413)` and an `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` each reach `onError` with `status()` readable, and the malformed query `?x=%zz` raises an `HttpException` with status `400` that reaches `onError` after the middleware ran and before the handler. [D-129; D-130; wave-4 carried: malformed query]

With two `onError` handlers, the second runs only when the first returned with the response `NEW`, and receives the same error; when the first responded, the second records no call. [D-137] Decision: `onError` registrations form one chain in registration order that stops at the first handler that starts the response. Decision: the first `onError` handler runs whatever the response state was when the error arrived; a later one runs only while the response is still `NEW`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-2]

When every `onError` handler returned with the response `NEW`, or none is registered, the response is the standard error response of FR-APP-006 for the error. [D-132; D-137] Decision: the standard error response drops the status and headers the app set before the error. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-3]

An `onError` handler that throws makes the framework log the thrown exception at `ERROR` through the app logger and answer the standard `500` error response if the response is still `NEW`; no later `onError` handler runs. [D-129; D-133]

When a handler throws while the response is `STREAMING`, `onError` is still called once, no error body is written, and after the error path the response is `ABORTED` with the in-memory exchange closed abnormally; when the response is `COMPLETED`, it stays `COMPLETED` with the sent bytes unchanged. [D-131; T37]

A recording `onError` records no call for the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` and `OPTIONS` responses and for the pre-request and lifecycle-gate rejections. [residual: onError scope; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

An error that ends in a standard `500` response is logged once at `ERROR` with its `Throwable` through the app logger; an `HttpException` with a `4xx` status is not logged at `ERROR`. [D-129; D-133] Decision: only `500`s are logged at `ERROR`, with the stack trace kept in the server log. Decision: a `500` is logged at `ERROR` whatever the response state, and no other status is logged at `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-6]

The error path decides by the response state at the time the error arrives (`NEW` gives the error response, committed but not completed gives an abort, `COMPLETED` stays unchanged), the rule that the `res.json` serialisation case of D-136 relies on; that case itself is asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists. [D-136; D-131] Decision: the error path reads the response state once, after the `onError` chain, under the response lock; because a response committed on arrival can only stay committed or end, this gives the same outcome as the arrival-state rule. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-7]

records.title: Standard error JSON body, status mapping and code values

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `new RuntimeException("secret com.example.Foo")` is answered `500` with exactly `{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal Server Error","requestId":"<id>"}}`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a matching `Content-Length`, and the body contains neither the exception message, nor `RuntimeException`, nor `at ` stack frames. [D-132; D-133] Decision: the body has no whitespace and exactly the fields `code`, `message` and `requestId` in that order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-8]

The `code` values are `400` `BAD_REQUEST`, `404` `NOT_FOUND`, `405` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `413` `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `415` `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, `422` `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, `426` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, `500` `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `501` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and `503` `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and any other `HttpException` status uses `HTTP_<status>`. [D-134; D-137] Decision: these are the `code` values per status.

The `message` is the status reason phrase (for example `Not Found`), except for an `HttpException` created with a message, whose message is used; a `500` always uses `Internal Server Error`. [D-133; D-137] Decision: only an app-supplied `HttpException` message reaches the client.

The automatic `404`, `405` (with its `Allow` header), `426` (with `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade`), `501`, the pre-request `400`s and `501` and the lifecycle-gate `503`s carry the standard body with their `code`; the `204` answers keep no body. [D-134; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave-4 carried: standard error body]
For a `HEAD` request the standard error response carries the headers and the `Content-Length` of the body it would have had and no body. [D-132; FR-HTTP-017]
The `requestId` of a standard error body equals the request id field of the access log line of FR-APP-015 for the same request, also for the pre-request rejections. [D-135]

The body is generated by the core without the app's `JsonCodec`, escapes `"`, `\` and control characters of the `message` per RFC 8259, and is identical with any codec. [D-132] Decision: the core writes the standard error JSON itself. Decision: non-ASCII characters stay literal UTF-8 and are not escaped. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-13]
No API replaces the automatic `404`/`405` bodies in v1; an app answers custom `404` pages with a route of its own. [D-137] Decision: custom `404`/`405` bodies are not configurable in v1.

expiredAcceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a handler throwing `HttpException(400)`, `HttpException(422)`, `HttpException(413)` and `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` is answered `400`, `422`, `413` and `415` with the standard body, and any other exception `500`. [D-134; wave decision: 415]

records.title: Service registration, frozen registry and the single application context

acceptanceCriteria.text: A `UserService` registered in `onStart` is returned with identity by `req.service(UserService.class)` and `req.application().get(UserService.class)` in an HTTP handler; the WebSocket and SSE cases of D-142 are asserted in wave 7. [D-142; T41; wave decision: Services for long connections]

`ctx.register` and `ctx.registerExternal` called from `onStop`, and `req.application().register(...)` called from a handler in `RUNNING`, throw `IllegalStateException`, and the registry is unchanged. [D-139; D-141; T42] Decision: `register`, `registerExternal` and `own` throw `IllegalStateException` naming the method and the state whenever the state is not `STARTING` or the registry is frozen, before the registry or the close list is touched. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-2]

A second `ctx.register(UserService.class, other)` in `onStart` throws `IllegalStateException` naming the key, so `listen()` fails with it, and `getOrNull(UserService.class)` read from a failing-start close hook still returns the first instance. [D-140; T42] Decision: the configuration error is `IllegalStateException`. Decision: the message contains the class name of the key, the first instance stays registered and the second is not tracked for closing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-3]

In `RUNNING` sixteen threads calling `req.service(UserService.class)` concurrently all receive the registered instance, and the registry seen in `RUNNING` is an unmodifiable snapshot taken before the state became `RUNNING`. [D-141]
Two `onStart` callbacks run in registration order, each exactly once for one successful `listen()`, and neither runs again on `shutdown`. [D-143; D-154; T41]

`ctx.attribute` set in `onStart` is read by handlers in `RUNNING` and by `onStop` in `STOPPING`, and eight threads writing and reading distinct keys concurrently during `RUNNING` lose no write, and `onStop` writes `ctx.attribute("k2", v)` and reads it back. [D-144] Decision: attributes live in a concurrent map that the lifecycle gate does not guard. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-7]

`ctx.logger()` in `onStart` and `onStop` returns the same instance as `app.logger()`, also after `app.logger(l)` replaced it before `listen`. [D-145] Decision: `ctx.logger()` returns `app.logger()` read at call time, the logger as set and not the framework's failure-isolating wrapper. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-8]
The `ctx` passed to `onStart`, the `ctx` passed to `onStop` and `req.application()` in every request are the same instance. [D-146]

records.title: Owned and registered resources close once in reverse order

acceptanceCriteria.text: `ctx.own(db)`, then `ctx.register(UserService.class, users)` (an `AutoCloseable`) close as `users`, then `db` on shutdown. [D-147; D-149; T45]
One object registered under an interface key and under its implementation key and also owned is closed exactly once, at the position of its first `own` or `register` call. [D-148; T45]

When the second of three resources throws from `close()`, the first and third are still closed; on shutdown the failure is logged at `ERROR` through the app logger, and on start failure it is added as a suppressed exception to the exception `listen()` throws. [D-150; D-158] Decision: close failures are logged on shutdown and attached as suppressed on start failure.

An object registered only with `registerExternal` is not closed on shutdown or start failure, while `get` returns it like any service; an object passed to both `registerExternal` and `own` is closed once. [D-151]
A non-`AutoCloseable` service is registered and returned normally and nothing is closed for it. [D-149]

records.title: Shutdown sequence, deadline and shutdown participants

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recording test adapter, participants in all three phases, an `onStop` callback, an owned resource and a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger record the order: before-wait participants, `adapter.stop`, force-close participants, `onStop`, after-`onStop` participants, owned resource `close`, logger `flush` and `close`, `adapter.release`, then `app.state()` is `TERMINATED`. [D-162; D-401; T46]

The timeout passed to `adapter.stop` is the time left until the one deadline computed when `shutdown` began, so a before-wait participant that sleeps 200 ms of a 1 s timeout leaves at most 800 ms for the adapter stop. [D-162; wave-4 carried: exchange lifetime] Decision: the deadline is `System.nanoTime() + unit.toNanos(timeout)`, computed once, and `adapter.stop` receives `max(0, deadline - now)` nanoseconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-7 SDS-AC-8]
The internal participant registry adds participants to a phase in order and runs them in that order; a participant that throws is logged at `ERROR` and the sequence continues. [D-401]
`onStop` reads every service registered in `onStart` through `ctx.get`, before any owned resource is closed. [D-163; T45]

Two threads calling `shutdown` on a `RUNNING` app: one runs the sequence; the other and any later call return without running any step again, and `onStop` ran once. [D-161; T46] Decision: the losing caller waits for `TERMINATED` up to its own timeout and then returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-7 SDS-AC-11]
A request in flight when `shutdown` begins completes normally while the adapter stop waits within the deadline. [D-162]
An app logger that is also owned is skipped at its owned position and closed once at the log-writer step; closing the console logger leaves `System.out` open. [wave decision: Logger shutdown; D-148]

An `onStop` callback that throws is logged at `ERROR`, the remaining `onStop` callbacks run and the sequence continues to `TERMINATED`. [D-162] Decision: `onStop` failures do not stop shutdown. An `Error` (not only an `Exception`) thrown by an `onStop` callback or a shutdown participant is handled the same way, so the owned-resource close, the logger flush and close and the adapter release still run; after `TERMINATED` the first such `Error` is rethrown from `shutdown`, as on the start-failure path. [wave-4 loop P issue w4-S2-001]

`shutdown(timeout, unit)` called from a route handler or middleware of a `RUNNING` app runs the sequence on a separate non-daemon thread named `naruserve-shutdown` and returns at once, and that request's response is sent in full; called from a handler while another shutdown is already `STOPPING`, it returns at once; when the shutdown thread cannot be started, the sequence runs on the calling thread and still reaches `TERMINATED`. [D-161; D-162; wave-4 loop P issue w4-P1-001] Decision: in-request shutdown does not wait for itself, because the sequence waits for in-flight requests.

records.title: shutdown in NEW, STARTING, FAILED and TERMINATED, and listen after termination

acceptanceCriteria.text: `shutdown` on a `NEW` app sets `TERMINATED`, runs no `onStart` or `onStop` callback, never calls the adapter's `bind`, and closes a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger once. [D-164; residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED]

With `onStart` blocked on a latch inside `listen()` on thread A, `shutdown(5, SECONDS)` on thread B, then the latch released: `onStart` finishes, no `bind` happens, `listen()` throws `AppStartException`, no `onStop` runs, owned resources close in reverse order and observe `FAILED`, `app.state()` ends `TERMINATED`, and `shutdown` returns after `listen()` ended, and a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger is flushed and closed once after the resources closed and before `TERMINATED`. [D-426; T46; residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED] Decision: a start ended by a pending stop throws `AppStartException` with a message saying shutdown was requested while starting. Decision: with a pending stop recorded during `onStart` callback k, the callbacks registered after k do not run; the latch test registers a second callback and asserts it never ran.

When the pending stop is recorded during `bind`, the socket bound by it is released (`stop` and `release` called) and `RUNNING` is never set, and a request that the test adapter dispatched during that `bind` is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body with no middleware, handler or `onError` run. [D-426; D-428]

With `onStart` blocked on a latch, `shutdown(100, MILLISECONDS)` returns normally without an exception before the latch is released, `app.state()` is then `STARTING` or `FAILED`, and once the latch is released `listen()` still passes through `FAILED` to `TERMINATED` and throws `AppStartException`. [D-438; T46]

A resource `close()` running during a failing `listen()` (state `FAILED`) starts thread B, which calls `shutdown(5, SECONDS)`, and then blocks 100 ms; B's `shutdown` returns after the state became `TERMINATED` and within its timeout; `shutdown` on a `TERMINATED` app returns at once with no callback or close run. [D-427]
`listen(0)` on a `TERMINATED` app throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-165; T46]

records.title: Requests reaching the dispatcher during STOPPING get 503 with Connection: close

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request sent through the in-memory adapter from a before-wait shutdown participant (after `STOPPING` began, before the adapter stop) is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and `{"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",...}}`. [D-166; D-134; wave decision: Keep-alive at shutdown]

For that request a recording global middleware, the route handler and a recording `onError` record no call, and the access log records exactly one line with status `503`. [wave decision: Lifecycle gate; D-173]

A request that was in flight when `STOPPING` began is not answered `503` and completes with its handler's response. [D-166; D-162] Decision: the gate reads the state once, when the request enters it. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-7 SDS-AC-23]

The lifecycle gate runs before the pre-request checks, so during `STOPPING` an `OPTIONS *`, an unrecognised method token and a raw path not starting with `/` are each answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body, and in `STARTING` they are held on the start gate like any request. [wave decision: Lifecycle gate; D-428] Decision: the lifecycle gate is the first check of the exchange handler that `listen()` passes to the adapter, which wraps the dispatcher (FR-APP-009 AC-8).

records.title: One access log line per HTTP request

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the defaults, `GET /users/7` answered `200` with a 5-byte body produces exactly one `info` line matching `GET /users/7 200 \d+ms in=0 out=5 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`. [D-173; D-181; T38] Decision: this is the line format, and the request id is 16 lowercase hex characters generated per request. Decision: the duration is the `System.nanoTime()` difference from request start to response end divided by 1 000 000, in whole milliseconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-4]

With `includeDuration(false)`, `includeBytes(false)` and `includeRequestId(false)` the line is `GET /users/7 200`, and with `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` it is written through `debug`. [D-172; D-173] Decision: a disabled part is dropped together with its leading space, and `level` selects the `Logger` method, `trace` to `error(String)` for `TRACE` to `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-5]

A response aborted after commit (handler throws while `STREAMING`) produces one line with its committed status followed by ` aborted`; a `404`, a `405`, a handler `500`, each pre-request rejection (`501` unknown token, `400` raw path, `400` validator, `204` `OPTIONS *`) and each lifecycle-gate `503` produce exactly one line. [D-173; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate]
For a streaming response the line is written once after the stream copy finished, with `out` equal to the bytes copied; for a `HEAD` response `out` is `0`. [D-173; D-177]

`in` counts the request body bytes the core read from the adapter's body stream (not the declared `Content-Length`): a dispatcher test whose handler reads 4 bytes of a 10-byte body through the internal `BodyState` stream logs `in=4`, and a handler that never reads gives `in=0`. [D-177]

After `exclude("/health")`, `GET /health` produces no line while `GET /health/x` and `GET /healthz` do; with `enabled(false)` no request produces a line. [D-174; D-172] Decision: `exclude` matches the raw path without the query exactly.
The `rid` value of the line equals the `requestId` of the standard error body of the same request. [D-135]

records.title: Logcat logger through reflection on android.util.Log

acceptanceCriteria.text: A JVM test in `NaruServe-logcat` with a test-scope fake `android.util.Log` that records calls shows `new LogcatLogger()` calling `v`, `d`, `i`, `w`, `e(tag, msg)` and `e(tag, msg, t)` with tag `NaruServe` for the six methods. [D-403] Decision: the default tag is `NaruServe`. Decision: the `android.util.Log` methods are resolved once, in the constructor, through `Class.forName("android.util.Log")`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-1]

`new LogcatLogger("MyApp")` uses tag `MyApp`, and `new LogcatLogger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-403] Decision: the `null` tag check runs before the class lookup. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-2]

Without `android.util.Log` on the class path, the `LogcatLogger` constructor throws `IllegalStateException` naming `android.util.Log`; an exception thrown by a reflective call is caught and not rethrown. The case without `android.util.Log` loads `LogcatLogger` through a dedicated class loader that sees the `NaruServe-logcat` and `NaruServe-api` main classes but not the test classes. [D-403; D-171] Decision: the dedicated class loader is a `URLClassLoader` over the `NaruServe-logcat` and `NaruServe-api` main class directories whose parent is the bootstrap loader. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-4]

The `NaruServe-logcat` main classes reference no `android.*` type in their bytecode; `android.util.Log` appears only as a string for reflection, and the fake class lives only in the test source set. [D-403; D-178]

records.title: Rotating file logger with a bounded queue

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RotatingFileLogger.builder().build()` uses directory `./logs`, `maxFileBytes` `5242880`, `maxFiles` `5`, `queueCapacity` `1024` and level `INFO`; `maxFileBytes`, `maxFiles` or `queueCapacity` below `1` throw `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-180; I-012] Decision: the queue capacity defaults to 1024 records and no value may be unlimited. Decision: an out-of-range value throws from the builder setter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-6]

Records are written to `naruserve.log` in the console line format of IR-APP-006; when the next record would exceed `maxFileBytes` the files rotate to `naruserve.log.1` up to `naruserve.log.<maxFiles-1>`, dropping the oldest, so a test with `maxFileBytes(200)` and `maxFiles(3)` ends with at most three files. [D-180] Decision: the file names are `naruserve.log` and `naruserve.log.<n>`.
With the writer blocked on a latch inside the test output stream and `queueCapacity(2)`, the third and later records are dropped without blocking the caller and `droppedCount()` counts them. [D-180]

With a directory that cannot be created, logging calls return normally and `droppedCount()` grows; no exception reaches the caller. [wave decision: File logger directory; D-171] Decision: a failed write is handled the same way: the writer thread drops and counts the record. `flush()` returns after every record queued before the call is written; `close()` writes the queued records, stops the writer thread so no thread of the logger remains, and later logging calls are dropped and counted. [wave decision: Logger shutdown; I-015] Decision: `flush()` and `close()` wait for a marker record queued behind the earlier records. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-10]
The module's main classes reference no SLF4J or `android.*` type and pass the API 21 animal-sniffer check. [D-179; C-02]

The tests of this requirement and the failed-`listen()` writer-thread check of FR-APP-010 AC-6 live in the `NaruServe-filelog` test source set, which declares `testImplementation testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api'))`; tests block the writer through a package-private constructor that takes the factory of the file output stream. [D-180; I-015]

When renaming `naruserve.log` fails during rotation, the logger keeps appending to the same file without deleting any line, the public `rotationFailureCount()` counts the failure, the next rotation is attempted only after the file grows by another `maxFileBytes`, and a backup is deleted only when no free backup number is left, so a rename that keeps failing deletes no further backup. [D-180; D-171; wave-4 loop P issue w4-P1-001] Decision: a failed rotation keeps logging and backs off instead of retrying on every record.

records.title: Access log: one line per HTTP request, the WebSocket handshake and close lines, and the SSE stream-end line (wave 7)

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the defaults, `GET /users/7` answered `200` with a 5-byte body produces exactly one `info` line matching `GET /users/7 200 \d+ms in=0 out=5 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`. [D-173; D-181; T38] Decision: this is the line format, and the request id is 16 lowercase hex characters generated per request. Decision: the duration is the `System.nanoTime()` difference from request start to response end divided by 1 000 000, in whole milliseconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-4] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC1

With `includeDuration(false)`, `includeBytes(false)` and `includeRequestId(false)` the line is `GET /users/7 200`, and with `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` it is written through `debug`. [D-172; D-173] Decision: a disabled part is dropped together with its leading space, and `level` selects the `Logger` method, `trace` to `error(String)` for `TRACE` to `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-5] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC2

A response aborted after commit (handler throws while `STREAMING`) produces one line with its committed status followed by ` aborted`; a `404`, a `405`, a handler `500`, each pre-request rejection (`501` unknown token, `400` raw path, `400` validator, `204` `OPTIONS *`) and each lifecycle-gate `503` produce exactly one line. [D-173; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC3

For a streaming response the line is written once after the stream copy finished, with `out` equal to the bytes copied; for a `HEAD` response `out` is `0`. [D-173; D-177] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC4

`in` counts the request body bytes the core read from the adapter's body stream (not the declared `Content-Length`): a dispatcher test whose handler reads 4 bytes of a 10-byte body through the internal `BodyState` stream logs `in=4`, and a handler that never reads gives `in=0`. [D-177] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC5

After `exclude("/health")`, `GET /health` produces no line while `GET /health/x` and `GET /healthz` do; with `enabled(false)` no request produces a line. [D-174; D-172] Decision: `exclude` matches the raw path without the query exactly. re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC6
The `rid` value of the line equals the `requestId` of the standard error body of the same request. [D-135] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC7

An accepted upgrade to `/ws` produces exactly one handshake line matching `GET /ws 101 \d+ms in=0 out=0 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`, written in the endpoint's `onOpen` after `101` was written and before the first frame is read, which a test asserts by reading the log before the client sends its first frame; an upgrade rejected before `onOpen` (`426` for `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 12`, `403` for a refused `Origin`, `503` beyond the limit) produces its ordinary line with the rejection status and no `101` line (T38). [D-430; D-325; T38] Decision: the handshake line is written in `onOpen` after the channel is stored and before the handler, with the duration measured from `req.startNanos()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-12 SDS-AC-1] Decision: when the response ends with `upgraded101()` true no line is written from `onDone`, and a refusal before `onOpen` never calls `upgraded`, so its ordinary line is written. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-12 SDS-AC-2]

When a session ends, one close line `WS /ws <closeCode> \d+ms rid=<id>` is written with the same `rid` as its handshake line, the close code chosen by FR-WS-006 AC-9 (`1000` for `ws.close()`, `1001` at shutdown, `1008` on queue overflow, each also when the client never answers the server's close frame; the client's code for a client close; `1006` for a session aborted without any close frame) and the duration from `onOpen` to the close, exactly once per session (T38). Decision: the close line form is `WS <path> <closeCode>[ <n>ms][ rid=<id>]`. [D-325; T38]

An SSE stream produces no line when it starts and exactly one line when it ends, matching `GET /events 200 \d+ms in=0 out=<n> rid=[0-9a-f]{16} sse start=\d+ cause=(client|app|overflow|shutdown|error)`, where the duration covers the whole stream, `out` equals the bytes written to the stream, `start` is the epoch milliseconds of the stream start, and `cause` is the first end reason the core recorded for the stream: `app` when `close()` is called, `overflow` when the overflow policy ends the stream, and `shutdown` when the closing participant marks the stream ended or the deadline force-close begins, each recorded before any `IOException` that the ending causes; `client` only when a drain write or heartbeat to the socket failed with an `IOException`, or the drain found the connection closed, on a stream with no earlier recorded reason (how a client disconnect is detected); and `error` when a failure that is not an `IOException` in the core or app code during the drain (for example a `RuntimeException` thrown by event serialisation or by the adapter's output stream) ends a stream with no earlier recorded reason; an in-memory test asserts `cause=client` for a drain write failed with `IOException`, `cause=error` for a drain write failed with a `RuntimeException`, `cause=app` when the drain write after `close()` fails with `IOException` and `cause=overflow` when the drain write after the overflow end fails with `IOException`, and a TinyHttpd test asserts `cause=shutdown` for the stalled stream force-closed at the shutdown deadline (FR-SSE-005 AC-5); a `HEAD` to an SSE route produces its ordinary line without the `sse` part (T38). Decision: the SSE line appends ` sse start=<epochMillis> cause=<cause>` to the D-173 line, and the first recorded end reason wins over a later `IOException` or failure. [D-338; D-343; T38] Decision: for a response with a non-null `sseClient()`, `writeSse` is called with status `200`, `out` = `bytesWritten()`, the stream's start millis and the client's `cause()`; a null cause cannot occur because `sseEnded` runs only after `endBy`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-12 SDS-AC-4] A Servlet stream aborted before drain startup still emits its terminal stream-end record once.

`exclude("/ws")` and `exclude("/events")` suppress the WebSocket handshake and close lines and the SSE line of those paths, `enabled(false)` suppresses all of them, and `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` writes them through `debug`. [D-325; D-338; D-174]

records.requirement: The system shall write through the app logger at the configured level exactly one access log line per HTTP request that reaches the dispatcher, when the response completes or is aborted, in the format `<method> <path> <status>[ aborted][ <duration>ms][ in=<bytesIn> out=<bytesOut>][ rid=<requestId>]`, where `path` is the raw path without the query, the optional parts follow the options of IR-APP-007, the byte fields count body bytes actually read from and written to the connection, and requests to an excluded path produce no line, except that an accepted WebSocket upgrade gets its line with status `101` when the connection opens plus a separate close line with close code and duration, and an SSE stream gets its one line when the stream ends, with its start time and closing cause.
records.rationale: Restates FR-APP-015 AC-1 to AC-7 unchanged for plain HTTP (D-173, D-174, D-177, D-135, D-181 and the pre-request and lifecycle-gate decisions of wave 4) and adds D-430 (the `101` handshake line written in `onOpen`), D-325 (separate WebSocket close line with close code and duration) and D-338 (one SSE line at stream end with start time, duration, bytes and closing cause), which change the "one line per request when the response completes" statement; test T38 (WebSocket and SSE parts). Measured: `internal/AccessLog.java:51-86` formats the D-173 line once per request when the response completes; `DefaultAccessLogOptions`, `BodyState` and `RequestIds` keep their roles. Decision: the WebSocket close line starts with the token `WS` instead of an HTTP method so log tools can tell it from request lines; the SSE line keeps the D-173 prefix and appends ` sse start=<epochMillis> cause=<client|app|overflow|shutdown|error>`. Decision (SSE cause, AC-10): the first end reason recorded wins. The core records `app` when `close()` is called, `overflow` when the overflow policy ends the stream and `shutdown` when the closing participant marks the stream ended or the deadline force-close begins, before any `IOException` that the ending causes (TinyHttpd's `stop` aborts every remaining socket at the grace deadline, so the stalled drain write of FR-SSE-005 AC-5 then fails with an `IOException`); `client` is recorded only when an `IOException` or a detected closed connection ends a stream with no earlier recorded reason, since a client disconnect is seen only as such a failure (FR-SSE-003 AC-7, FR-SSE-004 AC-2); `error` is kept for a failure that is not an `IOException` (a `RuntimeException` in the drain, serialisation or adapter stream) with no earlier recorded reason; the core tells `client` from `error` by exception type. Pitfall: writing the SSE line at `res.sse()` time would log `out=0` and no cause; it is written when the stream ends. Pitfall: an upgrade rejected before `onOpen` must not get a `101` line; it takes the ordinary error-path line (D-444). Rejected alternative: logging every WebSocket message; it would flood the log of a chat app, reopen on demand as an option. Tests to re-point to FR-APP-019: every `FR_APP_015_*` method of `NaruServe-api/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/AccessLogTest.java`, `AccessLogAcceptanceTest.java`, `internal/DispatcherTest.java` (pre-request rejection log asserts) and the access-log asserts of `internal/StoppingGateTest.java` and `internal/AppIsolationTest.java`; the `@req FR-APP-015` comments of `AccessLog.java`, `BodyState.java`, `DefaultAccessLogOptions.java`, `DefaultResponse.java`, `DefaultRestApp.java`, `Dispatcher.java` and `RequestIds.java` move to FR-APP-019.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `ShutdownParticipants` keeps `add(Phase, Runnable)` and gains an overload taking a participant that receives `long deadlineNanos`; participants of both kinds registered in one phase run in registration order, and a deadline participant receives the deadline that `shutdown(timeout, unit)` computed, which a test asserts by checking that `deadlineNanos - System.nanoTime()` at entry is at most the timeout and at least the timeout minus 100 ms. With a shutdown timeout of 500 ms and one WebSocket session whose client stopped reading, the WebSocket close wait ends within 500 ms plus 200 ms and `shutdown` returns within 500 ms plus the 3 s margin (T44 case with a timeout below 1 s). data: shutdown

` and the end of the body, the `onClose` listeners run once and `send` returns `false`; an upgrade that reaches the upgrade extension point after the flag receives `503` with `Connection: close` before any `101`; and every session or stream registered before the flag is in the snapshot, which an in-memory test asserts by setting the flag between two registrations. The before-wait participants run while the adapter still accepts connections, for at most 1 s plus 200 ms of slack: a plain request sent while the WebSocket close wait is held by a stalled session receives `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body from the stopping gate, and an upgrade sent in that phase is refused without `101`. A short request whose handler takes 300 ms and starts before `shutdown(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` completes with `200` and its full body, and the `onStop` callback runs only after that response completed, which a test asserts by recording both events in order (T44). [D-342]

A WebSocket session and an SSE stream whose clients stopped reading are force-closed by the deadline: both client sockets reach end of stream or reset within the shutdown timeout plus the 3 s margin. [D-343]

Decision: the D-344 margin is 3 s = TinyHttpd `stop(grace)` overrun up to 1.5 s (acceptor join up to 1000 ms plus worker wait up to 500 ms) + adapter release wait of D-107 up to 1 s + 0.5 s scheduling slack, recorded in `docs/api/lifecycle.md` and used as the T44 tolerance; W2-010: the bound covers the core and adapter waits of D-162 while `onStop`, resource close and logger flush return promptly, and `docs/api/lifecycle.md` keeps its statement that those steps run without a time limit. records.title: Ordered HTTP registration layers and persistent Route identity

acceptanceCriteria.text: Matching overlapping or duplicate HTTP registrations executes in registration order rather than specificity order and permits continuation to later registrations; duplicate HTTP routes are not freeze conflicts. Separate app registrations have distinct Route identities.

route(path) inserts one Route at creation time; handlers added through that builder append to the same identity in method/handler order. A route skip exits all remaining callbacks of that identity and does not skip a separately registered route.

Existing registration overloads, RouteBuilder.use, group middleware and convenience APIs remain available. Null/invalid registrations fail atomically before a layer is published, and a group retains its documented configuration/ownership contract.

Ordinary HTTP route/middleware/RouteBuilder handlers may be registered after listen using safely published stack snapshots/append state; an in-progress request does not see partial registrations. Lifecycle/configuration, WebSocket and server-policy guards remain separately enforced.

HTTP registration consumes the new string matcher and Java Pattern/alternative inputs; HTTP matching defaults are case-insensitive and non-strict trailing slash unless explicitly configured. Repeated slashes remain meaningful by default.

Existing WebSocket resolution/authentication/Origin/426/upgrade fallback and explicit legacy matcher tests remain intact; changing HTTP defaults does not silently recompile WS patterns or alter its conflict policy.

records.title: HTTP continuation cursor and route/router skip semantics

acceptanceCriteria.text: next.run advances to the next callback/layer using shared cursors; a handler that neither continues nor completes does not automatically enter the next layer. Same-thread next.run retains downstream-before-after-next ordering.

Route skip exits remaining callbacks of the current Route; the same operation in ordinary use middleware behaves as normal continuation. Router exit leaves the nearest mounted router and resumes its parent's next layer, with a top-level exit reaching fallthrough.

Explicit continuation after res.end/send and repeated continuation follow the pinned execution trace rather than the old single-use/completed-response guard, while response writes still enforce one response commit.

Error continuation skips normal callbacks until an applicable downstream error handler and may resume normal flow when handled; malformed input and callback exceptions do not restart an earlier layer or run final handling twice.

Nested synthetic router frames and actual mounts preserve parent cursors, request views and parameter scopes. Concurrency/off-thread calls do not corrupt cursor progress or hold a request-wide lock across user callbacks.
Existing synchronous middleware lambdas and route-handler lambdas compile unchanged. New skip operations have Java8/API21-compatible public representations and clear null/error validation.

records.title: Deferred HTTP continuation and request completion ownership

acceptanceCriteria.text: A middleware/handler that returns with an unfinished response and no continuation leaves the request pending; a later callback can next, send text/JSON, stream or start SSE. Fulfilled asynchronous work does not implicitly next/end; explicit rejection/throw follows the error path.
Deferred completion uses Java8/API21-compatible callbacks or an existing-type integration; CompletionStage/CompletableFuture, coroutines and extra dependencies are not mandatory core APIs.

Response completion/abort, disconnect, timeout and shutdown converge on exactly-once access logging, in-flight decrement, input/stream closure and upload/temp cleanup after active callbacks release their ownership. Body/attributes/parameter views remain the same request identity.

Callbacks re-enter and restore the lifecycle request context so shutdown from a deferred callback does not wait on itself. No request-wide monitor is held while executing user code; a handler that starts and joins a thread invoking Next cannot deadlock.

Queued continuations and synchronous nested next calls preserve their documented trace order; cross-thread/late calls after terminal abort/shutdown have a documented bounded outcome and cannot double-commit or resurrect closed resources.

Deferred success/rejection, multiple/repeated next, response-end-then-next, late stream/SSE start, disconnect, shutdown deadlines and callback/resource races are tested in core and actual Tiny/Servlet adapters. Existing long-lived WS/SSE resource bounds remain covered.

A pending Deferred returned by an asynchronous callback explicitly retains a request work lease even after response completion; each successful or rejected settlement releases its lease without implicitly continuing or ending. Deferred.onSettled(Runnable) observes first settlement exactly once, including late registration, outside internal locks and after rejection observers. Multiple leases delay cleanup until all settle or terminal cancellation revokes them; late work after cancellation cannot resurrect resources.

HttpExchange provides additive default Runnable retainRequest(), returning an idempotent release action and imposing no new abstract obligation on custom exchanges. The core acquires one transport request retention before user callbacks and releases it only after active callbacks, queued work and Deferred leases permit input/upload cleanup. Under normal completion, built-in Tiny/Servlet adapters may finish the wire response but must not recycle request input/container context while retained; an actual POST that responds before its first body read can still decode the original body in pending asynchronous work. Terminal abort, timeout and forced stop may revoke transport holds to meet existing deadlines; late releases are harmless, cancelled input cannot be reopened, and original immutable request metadata cannot become another request's data. A shared common RequestRetentions helper owns reusable counting/once logic; callbacks run outside its lock.

records.title: Every registration API is recorded once, in call order, with its C4 kind and the original registered object as target

acceptanceCriteria.text: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `options` (every `RouteHandler`, `Middleware` and `Middleware...` overload, with or without a leading `Middleware`), `route(Method, String, ...)`, `route(MethodSet, String, ...)`, `method(...)`, `methodAsync(...)`, `getAsync(...)` and each method of a `route(path)` builder each produce a `ROUTE` record whose `getPath()` is the registered string path; `ws(...)` produces one `WEBSOCKET` record; `use(Object, Router)` and `use(Router)` produce `ROUTER_MOUNT`; `group(prefix, configurer)` produces `GROUP`; `param(...)` produces `PARAM`. (00 §8 also lists Express `all`; Core has no `all(...)` method and 0.11.0 adds none.)

`staticFiles(...)` produces exactly one `STATIC` record and `cors(...)` exactly one `CORS` record; neither call adds a `MIDDLEWARE` or `PATH_MIDDLEWARE` record, although `cors` registers `options.middleware()` through `use(Middleware)` (`DefaultRestApp.java:827`) and `staticFiles` registers through `use("")`.

`use(Middleware)`, `use("", mw)`, `use("/", mw)`, `use((Object) "", mw)`, `useAsync(handler)` and `useAsync("/", handler)` each produce a `MIDDLEWARE` record; `use("/api", mw)`, `use(Pattern.compile("^/a"), mw)`, `use(new Object[]{"/a", "/b"}, mw)` and `useAsync("/api", handler)` each produce a `PATH_MIDDLEWARE` record.
`use(ErrorMiddleware)`, `use(Object, ErrorMiddleware)` and `onError(ErrorHandler)` each produce an `ERROR_MIDDLEWARE` record.

For an app that calls, in this order, `cors(...)`, `use(mw)`, `get("/a", h)`, `staticFiles("/", dir)`, `use("/api", mw2)` and `onError(eh)`, `registrations()` lists the kinds `CORS`, `MIDDLEWARE`, `ROUTE`, `STATIC`, `PATH_MIDDLEWARE`, `ERROR_MIDDLEWARE` in that order and nothing else.

records.title: Registrations inside mounted Routers and groups are expanded with the mount path, including later additions to a live mounted Router

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `Router r = Router.create(); r.get("/users", h); app.use("/api", r);`, `registrations()` holds a `ROUTER_MOUNT` record with path `/api` followed by a `ROUTE` record with path `/api/users`, and the watcher receives both. Decision: expanded records follow their `ROUTER_MOUNT` or `GROUP` record in the mounted router's own order.

With `app.group("/v1", g -> g.get("/x", h))`, `registrations()` holds a `GROUP` record with path `/v1` followed by a `ROUTE` record with path `/v1/x`. The `GROUP` record is made only after the configurer returns normally, and before the buffered inner registrations are replayed; it is validated, passed to the watcher and recorded before any of its inner registrations, and each inner route then yields exactly one `ROUTE` record through the normal validate → watcher → apply → record cycle (it is not recorded again by expansion); `registrations()` for this example holds exactly one `ROUTE` record for `/v1/x`. A configurer that throws leaves `registrations()` unchanged, the watcher is not called for the `GROUP`, and the exception reaches the caller of `group(...)` (FR-APP-021 AC-3, `DefaultRouteGroup.java:34-49`).
A router nested in a mounted router (`outer.use("/b", inner); inner.get("/c", h); app.use("/a", outer);`) is expanded with both prefixes: the `ROUTE` record path is `/a/b/c`.

After `app.use("/api", r)` and after `listen`, calling `r.get("/late", h)` invokes the app's watcher once with a `ROUTE` record whose path is `/api/late`, and `registrations()` then contains that record appended at the end in call order (the list stays in registration order, IR-APP-008 AC-1); the record exposes (name not final) the `ROUTER_MOUNT` record of `r` it was expanded under, so a reader such as IR-AUTH-002 AC-5 can count it at the mount position of `r` (00 §6.4 row "R30 × 마운트된 Router에 추가", 14th edition).

A mount or a mounted registration whose path is a `Pattern` or an array (for example `app.use(Pattern.compile("^/x"), r)` or `r.get(new Object[]{"/a", "/b"}, h)`) yields a record that a test distinguishes from a string-path record through the public record type alone, without parsing `toString()`. (protectOnly treats it as doctor FAIL or an IllegalStateException in R28.)

A watcher exception thrown for a registration made through a mounted `Router` (`r.get("/late", h)`) propagates out of `r.get(...)` unchanged and the route is neither recorded nor reachable (a request to `/api/late` is answered `404`).

When a `Router` that already holds registrations is mounted (before or after `listen`), the watcher receives the `ROUTER_MOUNT` record and then every expanded record before the mount is applied; if the watcher throws for any of them, the mount is not applied, no record is added to `registrations()`, none of the Router's routes is reachable under the mount path (`404`), and the exception reaches the caller of `use(...)` unchanged (00 §8 C4: a watcher exception stops the registration, also through a Router; R28 11th edition: a watcher called after apply bypasses protectOnly).
