records.research:
- Decisive fact: `DefaultRouter` sends every mutation straight to its `HttpRouter` registry with no parent link (`DefaultRouter.java:9-34`, `HttpRouter.java:40` mount), so today the app cannot see a later `r.get(...)` on a mounted Router; Core still serves it because the Router is live (`AppLifecycle.requireHttpRegistration` allows HTTP registration until STOPPING, L151-L157).
- Pitfall: without expansion, `.protectOnly("/api")` checks only `/api` mount paths and misses `r.get("/../x")`-style or regex routes inside the Router; S-9 made unexpandable entries a FAIL for this reason.
- Pitfall (AC-7): mounting a Router that already holds a `Pattern` route after start. If the mount were applied once the watcher had seen only the string-path `ROUTER_MOUNT` record, the inner `Pattern` route would go live before the protectOnly watcher could veto it, the bypass R28 11th edition forbids; so every expanded record reaches the watcher before the mount is applied.
- Decision (AC-2): the `GROUP` record is made after the configurer returns, matching the existing buffer-then-replay group code (`DefaultRouteGroup.java:34-49`), so a throwing configurer leaves no phantom `GROUP` record.
- Decision: the record carries the full prefixed path for string paths; for `Pattern` or array paths (at the mount or inside) it must be marked so a reader can refuse it. 00 does not fix the representation; choose one the public record exposes (for example a nullable string path plus the original path object).
- Pitfall: a Router mounted under two prefixes or into two apps. 00 is silent; listed as an open question, decide during implementation and document.
- Rejected alternative: expanding only at `freeze`. Post-start additions to a live Router would then be invisible to the watcher, which reopens the protectOnly bypass of T-5.
records.implementationNotes:

records.title: Audit event stream: AuditEvent, AuditSink and AuditSinks

acceptanceCriteria.text: AuditEvent exposes getTimestampMillis() (long), getType(), getOutcome(), @Nullable getActorId(), @Nullable getTargetId(), getAction(), @Nullable getSourceIp(), @Nullable getRequestId(), @Nullable getReason() and getDetails(); it contains no username, email or password field. [INFERRED:med:advisory]

A recording AuditSink set on the builder receives events for: recovery use, self-protection grant denial, security_write_conflict, API key issue and API key revoke. Issue and revoke events carry the key id and issuedByUserId (a key with no recorded issuer, such as one from auth.apiKeys().issue, omits it), and a revoke event names the key's owner as target. auth.apiKeys().revoke and DELETE /auth/me/apikeys/:id read the key row best effort before they delete: when that read fails, the revoke still succeeds and its event has no issuedByUserId, and the event of auth.apiKeys().revoke has no target either. Every audit event raised during a request authenticated by an API key (for example an admin write by a key actor, or a key revoke) carries that key id, and every event whose actor is a service account marks it as such; an ordinary API-key request that triggers no audited action produces no audit event. Decision (2026-11-06, narrowed 2026-11-09): the auth.apiKeys() forms without a request are outside the key id rule, because they cannot see the request: even when a route calls them, their event has no actor, request id, IP or apiKeyId of the calling request; the forms that take the request (IR-APIKEY-002 AC-9) follow the rule.

getRequestId() of an event raised during a request equals req.requestId() of that request, except an event of an auth.apiKeys() form without a request, which has no request id (AC-2); the forms that take the request carry it.
An AuditSink that throws does not change the HTTP response; the failure is logged.

No AuditEvent carries a token, cookie value, API key secret, password or Authorization value (covered by the SEC-AUTH-008 AC-1 marker test, whose COOKIE and BOTH runs put the cookie values on the code path).

NaruServe-api contains the public types AuditEvent, AuditSink and AuditSinks in package com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth.audit (00 §2 tree, audit [공개·구현]); AuditSinks offers at least one public static method returning an AuditSink (the factory set and its names are not final and are recorded in docs/api); a reflection test asserts the three types exist and are public.

AuditEvent is an immutable value object: the class is final, declares no public setter, and every instance field is final, so a sink cannot change an event that another sink also receives. [INFERRED:med:advisory]

records.title: res.addCookie serialises one Set-Cookie header per call

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Response` declares `Response addCookie(Cookie)` returning the receiver; `addCookie(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; two calls add two `Set-Cookie` header lines in call order and never merge them. [D-203; T33] Decision: `addCookie` returns the response for chaining like `status` and `header`.

A cookie `sid=abc` with path `/`, domain `example.com`, `maxAge` 3600, secure, httpOnly and `SameSite.LAX` produces exactly `Set-Cookie: sid=abc; Path=/; Domain=example.com; Max-Age=3600; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`; a cookie with only name and value produces `sid=abc`; `SameSite.STRICT` and `SameSite.NONE` produce `SameSite=Strict` and `SameSite=None`. [D-203; T33] Decision: attributes appear in the order `Path`, `Domain`, `Max-Age`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`.

A cookie with `maxAge` 0, path `/` and domain `example.com` produces `Set-Cookie: sid=; Path=/; Domain=example.com; Max-Age=0` when its value is empty, which deletes the cookie in browsers. [D-204; T33]

A cookie whose `maxAge` is negative (the default `-1`, or `-5`) produces no `Max-Age` attribute, and no cookie ever produces an `Expires` attribute. [D-208] Decision: v1 has no `Expires` support; a lifetime is set only through `Max-Age`.

A cookie built by the request-cookie parser with a value containing a space, `,`, `;` or a control character makes `res.addCookie(cookie)` throw `IllegalArgumentException` and adds no `Set-Cookie` header, and no `Set-Cookie` value the framework writes contains CR or LF. [D-205; I-017; wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently]
`addCookie` follows the commit rule of `res.header`: on a committed or completed response it throws `IllegalStateException` and adds nothing. [D-203; FR-HTTP-015; FR-HTTP-018]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `res.addCookie(Cookie("s", "").apply { maxAge = 0; path = "/" })` inside a route lambda. [D-204; C-03; I-010]

records.title: Lenient request-cookie parsing behind req.cookie and req.getCookies

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `Cookie: a=1; b=2; a=3`, `req.cookie("a").getValue()` is `1`, `req.cookie("zz")` is `null` and `req.getCookies()` holds `a=1`, `b=2`, `a=3` in that order. [D-206; T34] Decision: duplicate names are all returned in header order, `cookie(name)` returns the first, and several `Cookie` header lines are read in header order.
Without a `Cookie` header `req.getCookies()` returns an array of length 0, and every call returns a new array, so changing it does not change a later result. [D-206; T34]
Every parsed cookie has `getPath()`, `getDomain()` and `getSameSite()` `null`, `getMaxAge()` `-1`, `getSecure()` `false` and `isHttpOnly()` `false`. [D-207; T34]

For `Cookie: bad name=1; ok=2; =3; noeq; q="x y"; p=a%2Cb` no exception is thrown, the pairs `bad name=1`, `=3` and `noeq` are skipped, `ok` is `2`, `q` is `"x y"` with its quotes and `p` is `a%2Cb`; whitespace around each pair is trimmed and nothing inside a value is decoded. [wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; residual: Building request cookies]

A T34 test sets `x=a%2Cb` through `res.addCookie`, sends it back as a request `Cookie` header, reads `req.cookie("x").getValue()` as `a%2Cb` and sends it again with `res.addCookie(req.cookie("x"))`, which writes `Set-Cookie: x=a%2Cb`. [wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; T34]

`cookie(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; the parser builds cookies through the non-validating factory of IR-COOKIE-001 AC-6, so a value the public constructor would reject is returned without an exception. [D-206; residual: Building request cookies]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `val token: String? = req.cookie("session")?.value` and `val all: Array<Cookie> = req.getCookies()` without platform types. [D-206; C-03; I-010]

records.title: RestApp.start 정적 진입점: create, 설정 람다, listen을 한 호출로

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `RestApp` exactly one method named `start`, declared `public static ServerHandle start(int, Configurer<RestApp>)`, and finds on `RestApp` and `ServerHandle` no method named `run`, `startAsync`, `await` or `close`, no instance `start` and no `start` overload without a port; `ServerHandle` does not extend `AutoCloseable`; no class of `NaruServe-api` main outside `com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth` and its subpackages calls `System.getenv`, and inside those packages only `AuthMode.fromEnv()`, `KeySources.fromEnv(...)`, `AuthFileKey.fromEnv()` (the auth file master key of SEC-IAM-008, `NARU_AUTH_FILE_KEY`; names not final) and the `NARU_AUTH_RECOVERY` recovery switch read the environment (each an explicit call the app makes, 00 §3 and R41), so `start` itself still reads no environment variable.

`start(port, null)` throws `NullPointerException` before `create()` runs; otherwise `start` runs in this order, asserted with a recording app and adapter: the app is created, the lambda runs once with the app in state `NEW` (so `get`, `use`, `server`, `onStart`, `onStop` and `trustProxy` are accepted), then `listen(port)` runs, and the returned `ServerHandle` is the one of that `listen`.

With the real bootstrap module, `RestApp.start(0, app -> app.get("/x", (req, res) -> res.send("ok")))` returns a handle whose `port()` is the actual positive port and whose `state()` is `RUNNING`, and a client socket request `GET /x` to `127.0.0.1:<port>` returns `200` with body `ok`.

`start` returns as soon as `listen` returned: a child JVM whose `main` only calls `RestApp.start(0, ...)` and ends stays alive until the app is shut down (the FR-ENGINE-006 AC-5 scenario through `start`), and the call from the test thread does not block.

`start` does not change `listen`: without `app.server(...)` in the lambda `handle.address()` is `127.0.0.1`; `app.server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0"))` in the lambda binds the wildcard and produces the same one non-loopback warning as `listen`; port `-1` and `65536` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, a route conflict throws `RoutingConfigException`, and a bind failure throws `AppStartException` or the unchecked cause exactly as `listen` does, none swallowed or wrapped again by `start`.

When the lambda throws, `start` shuts the app down (state `TERMINATED`, logger flushed and closed, no thread or socket left) and rethrows the original exception instance unchanged; a `listen` that threw for a port outside `0..65535` while the app was still `NEW` leaves the app `TERMINATED` too.

When no `AppFactory` provider is on the class path, `start(0, routes)` throws the `IllegalStateException` of `RestApp.create()` unchanged, whose message names `com.snoworca.naruserve:naruserve`, and `routes` is never called (checked in the `NaruServe-api` tests, which have no provider, like FR-APP-001 AC-3).

A Kotlin test (T11) compiles and runs `RestApp.start(0) { app -> app.get("/x") { _, res -> res.send("ok") } }` with the trailing lambda and the chain as the last expression, with no platform type on the new signature (`@NullMarked` package), and the Kotlin callback matrix of FR-KT-003 still lists no new callback type because `Configurer` is reused.

records.requirement: The system shall provide the static interface method `ServerHandle start(int port, Configurer<RestApp> routes)` on `RestApp` that calls `RestApp.create()`, runs `routes` with the new app while it is still `NEW`, calls `app.listen(port)` and returns the resulting `ServerHandle` without blocking, so that `RestApp.start(3000, app -> app.get("/hello", (req, res) -> res.send("Hello World")))` is a complete server in one statement, and shall leave every rule of `listen` (default bind `127.0.0.1`, non-loopback warning, Host allowlist and the exception types) unchanged.
records.rationale: Spring Boot's SpringApplication.run(Class) scans classes, which NaruServe rejects (no auto scan, Android). Only the shape "one static call" is adopted. Rejected alternatives (docs/research/start-api/00-recommendation.md): a port-less overload, a PORT environment variable or system property (hidden input sources; the default port is 3000 in README but 8080 in object.md), the start(Class) scan form, an instance app.start (two names beside listen), a blocking run (no handle, ANR on Android; the non-daemon keeper thread of FR-ENGINE-006 already holds the JVM), startAsync, AutoCloseable and await() (out of v1 scope). LAN exposure stays explicit inside the lambda: app.server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0")). The method lives in the Core RestApp interface because create() already crosses the engine boundary through ServiceLoader, so no engine, Gson, android or servlet type is referenced.

records.title: ServerHandle.url과 shutdown으로 시작한 서버를 핸들만으로 확인·종료

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `ServerHandle` declaring exactly `int port()`, `String address()`, `AppState state()`, `String url()` and `void shutdown(long, TimeUnit)`, no other public method, and no `@Nullable` position; the handle of `listen` and the handle of `start` both implement all five.

`url()` returns `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` for the default bind, with `<port>` the bound port also after `listen(0)`; `http://localhost:<port>` when the bind address is `0.0.0.0`, `::`, `::0` or `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0`; `http://<address>:<port>` for another IPv4 address or host name; and `http://[<address>]:<port>` for an IPv6 literal, with a zone id written `%25<zone>` as RFC 6874 requires (`fe80::1%en0` gives `http://[fe80::1%25en0]:<port>`), asserted for each form.

`handle.shutdown(timeout, unit)` on a `RUNNING` app runs the `onStop` callbacks once and leaves `state()` as `TERMINATED` with the port closed; calling it again, after `RestApp.shutdown`, or from several threads returns without error; a negative timeout throws `IllegalArgumentException` and a `null` unit throws `NullPointerException`, as `RestApp.shutdown` does.

A Kotlin test (T11) reads `handle.url()` and calls `handle.shutdown(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` on the handle returned by `RestApp.start(0) { ... }`, and the Kotlin contract checks of FR-KT-001 and FR-KT-002 (nullability annotations, no keyword method name) still pass for `ServerHandle`.

records.rationale: Names are decided during implementation (they were absent from object.md): url() and shutdown(long, TimeUnit), the latter named like RestApp.shutdown so one contract serves both. A 5-second default shutdown, close() and AutoCloseable are not added: try (ServerHandle h = start(...)) on a long-lived server would stop it at the end of the block. Returning RestApp from start was rejected because the app is already RUNNING and every setter would throw IllegalStateException, and it would break FR-APP-002 AC-5 and FR-HTTP-008 AC-6. This requirement changes IR-APP-005 AC-3 (ServerHandle declared exactly port(), address() and state()).

records.title: start의 시작 로그 한 줄과 JVM 한정 shutdown hook 등록·제거

acceptanceCriteria.text: After a successful `start` the app logger receives exactly one start line at INFO that begins with `Listening on http://` followed by the real bound port (also for port `0`); for a loopback bind it is `Listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port> (this device only)`, for a wildcard bind `Listening on http://0.0.0.0:<port> - open http://localhost:<port> or http://<this-device-ip>:<port>`, for another address `Listening on http://<address>:<port>`; on a JVM the line ends with ` Press Ctrl+C to stop.` and on Android it does not.

`listen` logs no start line: the log lines recorded for `RestApp.builder()` apps that call `listen` are the same as before this requirement (the existing log-count tests pass unchanged), and `listen` registers no shutdown hook.

On a JVM `start` registers exactly one hook thread after `listen` returned (not before `listen`, so a failed start registers none); when the hook runs it logs one INFO line starting with `Stopping` and calls `app.shutdown(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`, which a recording hook registry and a child JVM that receives SIGTERM both show (`onStop` runs, the line `Stopping` is printed).

When `android.util.Log` is visible to the class loader of `RestApp`, detected only by reflection (no class of `NaruServe-api` main references `android.*`, the CON-BUILD-013 check stays green), `start` registers no hook and the start line has no `Press Ctrl+C` text; the detection is separated so a test with a class loader that exposes a fake `android.util.Log` shows both outcomes.

The registered hook is removed with `Runtime.removeShutdownHook` after `handle.shutdown(...)`, after `RestApp.shutdown(...)` called on the app captured in the lambda, and when the hook itself ran the shutdown (an `IllegalStateException` of the removal during JVM shutdown is swallowed); after a start whose lambda threw or whose `listen` failed no hook is registered; ten successive start and shutdown cycles through a recording registry leave zero registered hooks.
A hook that runs for an app that is already `TERMINATED` does nothing and does not throw, and removing a hook twice is harmless.

When the hook registry refuses the registration after `listen` returned (the JVM is already shutting down, or a security manager denies it), `start` shuts the app down (state `TERMINATED`, port closed) and rethrows the refusal exception instance unchanged, so no server is left running without a handle; asserted with a recording registry whose `add` throws.

records.rationale: Measured before this work (docs/research/start-api/03-tinyhttpd-and-junior-dx.md scenarios 2 and 5): a plain listen prints nothing, so the terminal looks stuck, and SIGTERM cuts an in-flight request (curl exit 52) and never runs onStop. start is the convenience path and listen stays pure; the difference is a table in docs/api/app.md. The hook is registered after listen succeeded, so a failed start leaves nothing to remove. records.title: TinyHttpd adapter implements HttpAdapter with confined engine types and per-feature classes

acceptanceCriteria.text: `TinyHttpdAdapter` is a public final class with a public no-argument constructor implementing `HttpAdapter`, and reflection finds no `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` type in any public or protected constructor, method or field signature of any public class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`. [D-209] Decision: the adapter class is `com.snoworca.naruserve.tinyhttpd.TinyHttpdAdapter`.

The adapter core class sets every TinyHttpd builder limit of FR-ENGINE-003 and FR-ENGINE-004, while the exchange bridge and the file-transfer, event-stream and upgrade paths of `HttpExchange` are separate classes of the module; in wave 5 the file-transfer, event-stream and upgrade classes throw `UnsupportedOperationException` naming the wave (6 or 7) that adds them. [D-210; D-404] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-5 SDS-AC-2]: in wave 5 the file-transfer, event-stream and upgrade paths of the exchange delegate to the module class `TinyHttpdFeatures`, which throws the `UnsupportedOperationException`.

No class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` references TinyHttpd's `TlsConfig` or calls the builder's `tls(...)` or a `listen(..., TlsConfig)` overload, which a class-reference test checks, and on the TinyHttpd adapter `req.isSecure()` returns `false` unless proxy trust of FR-ENGINE-008 reports `https`. [D-433; D-080]

Over a real socket, `GET /a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and a request without `?` has a `null` raw query, because the adapter reads `getRequestURI()` and `getQueryString()` and never `getPath()`. [D-399; I-021; wave-3 carried: TinyHttpd halves]

The adapter's request headers, method token, HTTP version and remote address reach the core unchanged, and the adapter's `boundPort()` throws `IllegalStateException` before bind like the SPI requires. [D-209; D-107]

records.title: Loopback default bind, explicit LAN binding with warning, Host allowlist and bind outcomes

acceptanceCriteria.text: Without `server(...)`, the adapter passes `InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1")` to TinyHttpd's `bindAddress` explicitly, the listening socket's local address is `127.0.0.1`, `ServerHandle.address()` returns `127.0.0.1`, and no class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` calls `InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress()`. [D-211; wave decision: The default bind address is IPv4 `127.0.0.1`; residual: D-211 wording]

With `server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0"))` the socket binds the wildcard address and `ServerHandle.address()` returns `0.0.0.0`; with a non-loopback local address `a` found through `NetworkInterface`, a connection to `a` is refused for the default app and accepted for an app bound to `0.0.0.0` (the case is skipped through JUnit `Assume` when the host has no such address). [D-212; T49; wave decision: The default bind address is IPv4 `127.0.0.1`] Decision: `ServerHandle.address()` returns the configured bind address after a LAN bind.

`listen()` with a bind address outside `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1` and `localhost` logs exactly one `warn` record through the app logger that names the bind address and says the app must add its own authentication, whether or not global middleware is installed, and logs no such record for the default bind; the record contains no header value, cookie or token. [D-213; wave decision: The LAN warning is unconditional; I-016; T49] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-4 SDS-AC-10]: the warning is logged after the configuration freeze and before the adapter `bind` call.

Requests with `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`, `Host: localhost:<port>` and, after `allowedHosts("myphone.local")`, `Host: myphone.local` reach the handler, and when the bind address is a host name that name is added to the allowlist; `Host: evil.example` is answered `421` with the standard error body (code `HTTP_421`) rendered by the `ErrorHandler` of FR-ENGINE-005, and neither `onError` nor the access log records it. [D-214; D-418; D-405]
`listen(0)` binds an ephemeral port: `ServerHandle.port()` returns the port TinyHttpd reports through `getPort()`, which is positive, and a client connects to it. [D-221]

A second app calling `listen(p)` on the port `p` already bound by a first app throws `AppStartException` whose cause is a `java.net.BindException`; the second app passes `FAILED` and ends `TERMINATED` as FR-APP-010 defines for a failed start, no socket and no TinyHttpd or keeper thread of the second app remains, and the first app keeps serving. [D-222; FR-APP-010] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-5 SDS-AC-7]: when TinyHttpd `start()` throws `BindException` the adapter stops the half-built server and rethrows, and the keeper thread is started only after a successful start.

records.title: TinyHttpd request limits: header size, request line, header line, slowloris guards and body framing

acceptanceCriteria.text: With default settings a request whose header section exceeds 16384 bytes is answered `431`, and a request line of 8191 bytes (method, target and version together) is answered `414` while one of 8190 bytes is served. [D-215; T48] Decision: the default request-line limit is 8190 bytes and the header-size total is 16384 bytes.

`server(o -> o.maxRequestLineLength(n))` passes `maxRequestLineBytes = n` and `inputBufferBytes = max(8192, n + 2)` to the builder, so `n` = 1, 8190, 8191 and 65534 all build and start, and `n` = 65534 gives `inputBufferBytes` 65536. [D-414; residual: Upper bounds on size settings]

A single header line of 8191 bytes is answered with TinyHttpd's transport-level `431` under default settings even when the header total stays below `maxHeaderSize`, and raising `maxHeaderSize` alone does not raise that per-line limit, while `maxRequestLineLength(10000)` raises it to 10000 bytes. [D-437; D-400]

A request with 101 header fields is answered `431`; a client that sends part of the header section and then stops is closed after the header timeout (shortened through `headerTimeout` in the test) with TinyHttpd's `408`; and with `bodyReadTimeout` set to 1 s in the test (below the 5 s grace of the body-rate guard, which otherwise ends a stalled body first) a body that stops arriving is answered `408` with `Connection: close` after the body-read timeout. [D-216; T48]

A body drip-fed at about 10 bytes per second to a route that reads it is answered `408` with `Connection: close` once TinyHttpd's 5 s body-wait grace has passed, and the connection is then closed; the adapter sets `minRequestBodyRate` from `minBodyRate` (default 240). [D-413; D-219; T48]

A request carrying both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is answered `400` by TinyHttpd's parser before dispatch, and no handler, `onError` or access-log line runs for it. [D-217; D-400; T48]

The adapter never calls `maxRequestBodyBytes` or `maxDrainBytes` on the builder, so a body larger than the JSON limit is answered `413` by the core through `onError` with the standard error body and one access-log line, and a body that no handler reads is drained by TinyHttpd up to 65536 bytes before the connection is reused or closed. [D-443; D-088; D-188]

Non-default values of `maxHeaderSize`, `maxHeaderCount`, `maxRequestLineLength`, `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout` and `minBodyRate` reach the builder unchanged (timeouts converted to milliseconds), which a test reads back through the package-private accessor of the built configuration of FR-ENGINE-004 AC-1, and a request with 20000 header bytes is served after `maxHeaderSize(32768)`. [D-225; D-215; D-216; D-413] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-5 SDS-AC-10]: the package-private accessor is `TinyHttpdAdapter.config()`.

records.title: Connection limits, derived wait queue and bounded worker pool on TinyHttpd

acceptanceCriteria.text: With default settings the adapter passes `maxWorkers` 192, `maxEventStreams` 128 (from `maxSseStreams`), `maxConnections` 512, `maxUpgradedConnections` 128 and `maxConnectionsPerAddress` 256 to the builder, which a test reads back through a package-private accessor of the built configuration, so the derived wait queue is 320 and open connections total at most 640. [D-404; D-210] Decision: TinyHttpd's own `maxEventStreams` (default 64) is set to the SSE stream limit so the effective limit is 128.

`server(o -> o.maxWorkers(4).maxSseStreams(2).maxConnections(5))` makes `listen()` throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names `maxConnections`, `maxWorkers` and `maxSseStreams` with their values from the configuration freeze of FR-APP-009 (after the `onStart` callbacks, before any `bind` call), so the app ends `FAILED` and then `TERMINATED` as FR-APP-010 defines for a failed freeze, TinyHttpd's builder is never called and no socket opens; `maxConnections(6)` with the same values starts. [D-415; FR-APP-009; FR-APP-010] Decision: the check is part of the existing freeze step and its exception reaches the caller unwrapped like the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`.

With `maxWorkers(1)`, `maxSseStreams(1)` and `maxConnections(2)` (wait queue 0), two connections held open by blocking handlers occupy both workers and a third connection is answered TinyHttpd's plain-text `503` at socket level, which reaches neither `onError` nor the access log. [D-218; D-400]
With `maxConnectionsPerAddress(2)`, a third concurrent connection from `127.0.0.1` is refused by TinyHttpd while the first two are served. [D-404]

records.requirement: The system shall map the connection settings onto TinyHttpd's builder with `maxWorkers` equal to the HTTP worker budget plus the SSE stream limit (64 + 128 = 192 by default), `maxConnections` 512, `maxUpgradedConnections` 128 and `maxConnectionsPerAddress` 256, derive the wait queue as `maxConnections - maxWorkers` (320 by default) instead of configuring it, make `listen()` fail with a configuration error before TinyHttpd's builder runs when `maxConnections` is below the worker budget plus the SSE stream limit, and use TinyHttpd's bounded worker pool, whose full wait queue answers TinyHttpd's plain socket-level `503`.
records.rationale: Covers D-404, D-415 and D-218. Measured fact: TinyHttpd has no queue setter; its `WorkerPool` holds up to `maxConnections - maxWorkers` waiting connections, `build()` requires `maxConnections >= maxWorkers`, and a connection that cannot enter the full queue gets the prebuilt `503` with `Retry-After: 1` from `HttpServer.reject`. The defaults let the T26 load from one loopback address fit (256 per address). Rejected alternative: a separate queue-length setting (TinyHttpd cannot honour it independently).

records.title: TinyHttpd error mapping, ErrorHandler, transport-level rejections and log routing

acceptanceCriteria.text: The adapter's request-body stream turns TinyHttpd's `BodyTooLargeException` into `HttpException` `413`, a `SocketTimeoutException` into `HttpException` `408` and `TruncatedBodyException` and `MalformedBodyException` into `HttpException` `400`, each keeping the original as cause; the `413` branch is tested with a constructed `BodyTooLargeException`, and a truncated body (fewer bytes than `Content-Length` before the client closes its output) read by `req.body(...)` gives `400`. TinyHttpd's `ContentLengthExceededException`, raised only by the response stream when a handler writes past its declared length, is not mapped to a client status: it reaches the error path as a server error. [D-219; wave decision: The 413 branch of D-219 is a guard]

A standard error response with status `408` carries `Connection: close` and the adapter closes the connection after it, on every adapter path that produces it (the body-read timeout of D-216 and the slow-body guard of D-413). [D-219; D-413] Decision: the core error path adds `Connection: close` to every `408` it writes, and the standard messages for `408` and `421` are `Request Timeout` and `Misdirected Request`.

The adapter installs one `ErrorHandler` through the builder; for an error TinyHttpd raises after parsing and outside a NaruServe dispatch (the `Host` rejection of D-418 is the test case) it writes the status, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and the body from `ServerSettings.errorRenderer()` (for `421`: code `HTTP_421`, message `Misdirected Request`), so two such responses carry two different request ids. [D-405; D-418]

The pre-dispatch rejections of D-400 tested here — an invalid request line (`400`), a request line over the limit (`414`), a header section over the limit (`431`), `HTTP/2.0` (`505`) and a header timeout (`408`) — are answered by TinyHttpd's fixed plain-text responses, and a recording `onError` and the access log record nothing for them. [D-400]

`CONNECT / HTTP/1.1` reaches the dispatcher and is answered with its unsupported-method `501` and one access-log line, while `CONNECT example.com:443 HTTP/1.1` is answered by TinyHttpd's transport-level `501` with no access-log line. [D-422; D-400]

The adapter passes TinyHttpd a `TinyLog` that writes through `ServerSettings.logger()`, mapping `SEVERE` to `error`, `WARNING` to `warn`, `INFO` to `info`, `CONFIG` and `FINE` to `debug` and `FINER` and `FINEST` to `trace`, with the throwable passed to `error(String, Throwable)`; a TinyHttpd warning appears in a recording app logger, and an app logger that throws does not stop the server from answering the next request. [D-220; wave decision: The adapter gets the safe logger] Decision: `isLoggable` returns `true` for every level and the app logger filters. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-6 SDS-AC-6]: below `SEVERE` (for example `WARNING`) a throwable is appended to the text as `message + ": " + throwable`, because `Logger` has no `warn(String, Throwable)`.

records.title: TinyHttpd stop, release, keep-alive shutdown behaviour and the non-daemon keeper thread

acceptanceCriteria.text: `app.shutdown(t, unit)` calls the adapter's `stop` once, which calls TinyHttpd's `stop(graceMillis)` with the milliseconds left until the deadline of D-162 (at most `t` converted, never negative), so in-flight requests may complete until the deadline and are force-closed only there; because `stop` closes the listening sockets before it waits, TinyHttpd's join tail after the deadline stays small, and a test asserts that `stop` returns within the deadline plus 1500 ms; the final `release` calls `awaitTermination` with at most 1000 ms. [D-223; D-107; D-162; FR-APP-011] Decision: the adapter passes the full time left as grace, as D-223 states, and its fixed release margin is 1 second.

After shutdown returns, no thread of that app is alive: TinyHttpd's worker threads come from a `ThreadFactory` the adapter passes to the builder, which keeps TinyHttpd's default worker properties (daemon, the configured worker stack size of 256 KiB, an uncaught-exception handler that logs through `ServerSettings.logger().error(String, Throwable)`), names each thread `naruserve-<port>-worker-<n>` and reads the bound port when it creates the thread (so `listen(0)` names the real port); the acceptor is identified by TinyHttpd's own name `tinyhttpd-acceptor-<port>`, the keeper thread by `naruserve-keeper-<port>`, and a test that starts one app at a time also finds no `tinyhttpd-watchdog` thread alive after `release`; tests use handlers that end when interrupted, and a worker that TinyHttpd reports as left after stop is logged as a warning by `release`. [D-223; I-015] Decision: worker names come from the adapter's thread factory; acceptor and watchdog names are TinyHttpd's fixed names.

A request sent on an idle keep-alive connection after `STOPPING` began receives either `503` with `Connection: close` or a connection closed without a response, and a response in flight when the stop begins is committed with `Connection: close`. [D-166; T44; wave-4 carried: TinyHttpd keep-alive socket case]

After a successful bind exactly one non-daemon thread named `naruserve-keeper-<port>` is alive and TinyHttpd's acceptor and worker threads are daemon; the keeper thread ends when the adapter stop begins and no keeper thread exists after a failed bind. [D-167; wave decision: Thread wording] Decision: the keeper thread is named `naruserve-keeper-<port>`.

A child JVM started by the test runs a `main` that calls `RestApp.create()`, registers a route that calls `app.shutdown`, calls `listen(0)`, prints the port and returns; the child process is still alive and serving 1 second after `main` returned, and exits by itself after the test requests the shutdown route. [D-167; T44]

records.title: Proxy trust through app.trustProxy applied by the core on every adapter

acceptanceCriteria.text: Without `trustProxy(true)`, a request with `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `Forwarded: for=198.51.100.1;proto=https` from `127.0.0.1` has `req.remoteAddress()` `127.0.0.1` and `req.isSecure()` `false` on both the in-memory and the TinyHttpd adapter, so FR-HTTP-011 AC-2 (the default configuration) stays true. [D-080; FR-HTTP-011]

After `app.trustProxy(true)`, `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.1` gives `req.remoteAddress()` `203.0.113.7`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` gives `req.isSecure()` `true`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` gives `false`, and a request without these headers keeps the adapter's values. [D-080; D-225] Decision: trusted mode uses the left-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry and the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value, compared case-insensitively. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-4 SDS-AC-8]: the left-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry is trimmed of surrounding whitespace.

After `app.trustProxy(true)` the `Forwarded` header alone changes neither `remoteAddress()` nor `isSecure()`, and an empty or blank `X-Forwarded-For` entry keeps the adapter's remote address. [D-080] Decision: `Forwarded` is not interpreted in v1.

The trust decision is made in `DefaultRequest` from the app setting, so the in-memory adapter and the TinyHttpd adapter give identical `remoteAddress()` and `isSecure()` results for the same headers, and no adapter class reads `X-Forwarded-*` itself. [D-080; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter]

records.title: Bootstrap AppFactory assembles TinyHttpd, Gson and the console logger, or the Logcat logger when NaruServe-logcat runs on Android, for RestApp.create()

acceptanceCriteria.text: `DefaultAppFactory` is public with a public no-argument constructor, the `NaruServe` jar holds `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory` naming it, and in the `NaruServe` module test run `ServiceLoader.load(AppFactory.class, RestApp.class.getClassLoader())` finds exactly one provider and `RestApp.create()` returns a new app in state `NEW` on every call. [D-226; D-110; wave-4 carried: D-226 lookup with the real module] Decision: the provider class is `com.snoworca.naruserve.bootstrap.DefaultAppFactory`.

An app from `RestApp.create()` started with `listen(0)` answers a JSON echo route over a real socket: a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `{"name":"a"}` is decoded into a POJO through the default codec and sent back by `res.json`, and the app's internal adapter and codec are a `TinyHttpdAdapter` and a `GsonJsonCodec` built from `GsonJsonCodec.defaultGson()`. [D-228; D-110]

In the JVM test run, where `android.util.Log` is absent, `RestApp.create().logger()` is a `ConsoleLogger`; through a dedicated class loader that sees a test-scope fake `android.util.Log` and the `NaruServe-logcat` classes, the factory's app logger is a `LogcatLogger`; through a dedicated class loader that sees the fake `android.util.Log` but not the `NaruServe-logcat` classes, it is a `ConsoleLogger`. [D-402; D-169; android-module decision 2026-10-26] Decision: once per `create()` call the factory checks `Class.forName("android.util.Log", false, <its class loader>)`, then loads `com.snoworca.naruserve.logcat.LogcatLogger` through the same loader and calls its public no-argument constructor; a missing class at either step selects the console logger.

[D-229; android-module decision 2026-10-26; central-0.9.0 pre-publication R8 check 2026-10-27] Decision: the file name is `naruserve-bootstrap.pro`.

`NaruServe-api` main classes still reference no TinyHttpd or Gson type (the build check of CON-BUILD-013), and the missing-module test of FR-APP-001 AC-3 keeps passing in the `NaruServe-api` test run. [D-226; D-227]

The class-reference build check fails when a main class of `NaruServe` references a `com/snoworca/naruserve/logcat/` type, so the bootstrap reaches the Logcat logger only by name. [android-module decision 2026-10-26]

records.title: TinyHttpd adapter implements HttpAdapter with confined engine types and per-feature classes (wave 6)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `TinyHttpdAdapter` is a public final class with a public no-argument constructor implementing `HttpAdapter`, and reflection finds no `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` type in any public or protected constructor, method or field signature of any public class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`. [D-209] Decision: the adapter class is `com.snoworca.naruserve.tinyhttpd.TinyHttpdAdapter`. re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC1

The adapter core class sets every TinyHttpd builder limit of FR-ENGINE-003 and FR-ENGINE-004, while the exchange bridge and the file-transfer, event-stream and upgrade paths of `HttpExchange` are separate classes of the module: the exchange delegates them to the module class `TinyHttpdFeatures`, and each keeps the exchange's commit lock, abort check and single-start rule. From wave 6, `sendFile(status, headers, file, offset, length)` writes the status, the given headers and exactly `length` bytes of `file` starting at `offset` through a plain buffered copy (no zero-copy transfer) and throws no `UnsupportedOperationException`; a socket test hands over a file with a non-zero offset and a length shorter than the rest of the file and reads back exactly that byte range. The event-stream and upgrade paths still throw `UnsupportedOperationException` naming wave 7, which adds them. Decision: the TinyHttpd `sendFile` hook fills D-106's extension point for apps that call it directly; the framework's own static, `res.file` and `res.download` bodies do not use it. [D-210; D-404; D-106; D-291; wave decision: File bodies come from the opened stream] Decision: a negative `offset`, a negative `length` or `offset + length` beyond the file length throws `IllegalArgumentException` before the response starts. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-9 SDS-AC-1] Decision: a file that shrinks during the copy throws `IOException` (EOF before `length` bytes) and leaves the exchange to the abort path. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-9 SDS-AC-2] Decision: `sendFile` commits through the exchange commit, so a second start throws `IllegalStateException` like `commit`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-9 SDS-AC-3] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC2 (file-transfer hook filled by wave 6)

No class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` references TinyHttpd's `TlsConfig` or calls the builder's `tls(...)` or a `listen(..., TlsConfig)` overload, which a class-reference test checks, and on the TinyHttpd adapter `req.isSecure()` returns `false` unless proxy trust of FR-ENGINE-008 reports `https`. [D-433; D-080] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC3

Over a real socket, `GET /a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and a request without `?` has a `null` raw query, because the adapter reads `getRequestURI()` and `getQueryString()` and never `getPath()`. [D-399; I-021; wave-3 carried: TinyHttpd halves] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC4

The adapter's request headers, method token, HTTP version and remote address reach the core unchanged, and the adapter's `boundPort()` throws `IllegalStateException` before bind like the SPI requires. [D-209; D-107] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC5

records.requirement: The system shall provide the TinyHttpd adapter as a public final `HttpAdapter` implementation whose public signatures expose no TinyHttpd type, whose exchange bridge and file-transfer, event-stream and upgrade paths are separate module classes receiving the exchange, whose file-transfer hook writes the requested byte range of a file through a plain buffered copy, whose event-stream path and `webSocket` path from wave 7 write a chunked event stream and run the TinyHttpd WebSocket handshake instead of throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`, holding the exchange lock only to check abort and mark the response started, and whose raw `upgrade(headers, UpgradeHandler)` path stays unsupported in v1 with a message that names no wave.
records.rationale:
Covers D-209, D-210, D-404, D-106, D-291, D-433, D-080, D-399 and D-107 as restated from FR-ENGINE-010, with AC-2 changed by wave 7 (the event-stream and `webSocket` paths are filled; raw `upgrade` stays unsupported) and new AC-3 and AC-4 from wave decisions TinyHttpd feature hooks (W2-003; D-210) and maxEventStreams (W2-009; D-336). Measured: `tinyhttpd/TinyHttpdFeatures.java:51-57` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` "arrive in wave 7" for `eventStream` and `upgrade`; `TinyHttpdExchange.java:229-240` declares `upgrade` and `eventStream` as `synchronized` methods that take the lock, abort check and single-start bookkeeping of `commit()` (wave 5 commit 387db8c, w5-P2-002), and drain writes made later from another thread must also synchronize on the exchange (FR-SSE-003). Carried note (r2 W1-002 / W1-001, D-408): TinyHttpd at 46b973e keeps only `Connection: close`/`keep-alive` on a non-`101` response (`ExchangeResponse.java:172-177`, `:466-470`), so the `426` answer's `Connection: Upgrade` cannot pass through this adapter; the D-020 TinyHttpd-gap issue is opened in the wave 7 ledger and D-408 stays below `verified` (FR-WS-004); this requirement does not patch TinyHttpd. Pitfall: holding the exchange lock for the whole WebSocket read loop or SSE drain would block every other call that synchronizes on the exchange for the life of the connection. Rejected alternative: TinyHttpd's `startEventStream()` (D-335: fixed `Cache-Control: no-cache` and a separate `retry` block). records.title: TinyHttpd conformance of res.onAbort and res.relay over real sockets

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-a, tinyhttpd, adapter-conformance, relay, abort

acceptanceCriteria.text: Over a real TinyHttpd socket, when the client closes its connection while a `res.relay(in, -1)` or `res.stream(...)` transfer from a slow source is still copying, a listener registered with `res.onAbort` runs exactly once.
Over a real TinyHttpd socket, a listener registered on a response that completes normally is never run, also after the client closes the connection once the response was read.

Over a real TinyHttpd socket, a handler that sets no `Content-Type` and calls `res.relay(in, 5)` with a 5-byte stream gives the client a response with no `Content-Type` header, `Content-Length: 5` and the 5 body bytes.
Over a real TinyHttpd socket, `res.relay(in, -1)` gives a response without `Content-Length` whose complete body the client reads under the framing TinyHttpd chooses.

Over a real TinyHttpd socket, `res.relay(in, 5)` answers a `HEAD` request with `Content-Length: 5` and no body bytes, answers a `304` response with no body bytes and no `Content-Length` (TinyHttpd 3.1.1 never writes `Content-Length` on a 304, `ExchangeResponse.commit` at commit `e73cd5d`, which RFC 9110 §8.6 allows), and a `204` response with neither, and the next request on the same keep-alive connection is served normally.

Over a real TinyHttpd socket, `res.relay(in, 5)` with a stream that ends after 3 bytes closes the connection before 5 body bytes arrive, so the client sees a truncated response rather than a complete one.

records.title: Fixed decision order for requests to auth endpoints

acceptanceCriteria.text: PROD, plain-text non-local POST /auth/refresh with two Authorization headers and a text/plain body -> 403 insecure_transport.
Secure POST /auth/login with two Authorization headers and a text/plain body -> 400 invalid_request, not 415.
Secure COOKIE-mode POST /auth/refresh with an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body containing refreshToken -> 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, not 400.
Secure COOKIE-mode POST /auth/refresh with a JSON body refreshToken, no X-CSRF-Token and a cross-origin Origin -> 400 BAD_REQUEST, not 403.
Secure BOTH-mode POST /auth/login with an Origin outside trustedOrigins and valid credentials -> 200 with body delivery and no Set-Cookie; no 403 is produced.

Secure COOKIE-mode (or BOTH-mode) with API keys enabled (.apiKeys(store)), POST /auth/refresh with a valid API-key Authorization header and a naru_rt cookie -> the key procedure decides the response before the refresh cookie is read (naru_rt is neither read nor rotated); the 403 api_key_not_allowed outcome is owned by SEC-FLOW-003 AC-5. Without .apiKeys(store) the key-scheme header is no credential (IR-TOKEN-001 AC-5) and the request is decided by naru_rt (FR-FLOW-005 statement). records.title: Token delivery rule for the five token-issuing responses

acceptanceCriteria.text: HEADER, successful POST /auth/login -> body contains accessToken and refreshToken, plus deviceToken when a device token is issued; the response has no Set-Cookie header.

COOKIE, successful POST /auth/login with a same-origin Origin -> Set-Cookie for naru_at, naru_rt and naru_csrf, plus naru_device when a device token is issued; the body contains csrfToken and none of accessToken, refreshToken and deviceToken (00 R29 (e): cookie delivery carries only csrfToken in the body).

BOTH refresh: a body refreshToken -> body delivery; only naru_rt (with matching X-CSRF-Token and a same-origin Origin) -> cookie delivery; which token is used when both are present is owned by FR-FLOW-005 AC-6, and that case answers with body delivery.

BOTH password: Authorization Bearer -> new accessToken, refreshToken and deviceToken in the body and no Set-Cookie; naru_at (with its family's X-CSRF-Token and a same-origin Origin) -> naru_at, naru_rt, naru_csrf and naru_device cookies with body csrfToken only. HEADER password: the same Bearer request -> new accessToken, refreshToken and deviceToken in the body and no Set-Cookie (00 §6.4 "R10 × Bearer 비밀번호 변경").

BOTH login: no Origin and no Referer -> 200 body delivery; same-origin Origin -> 200 cookie delivery with body csrfToken only; Origin capacitor://localhost not in trustedOrigins -> 200 body delivery without Set-Cookie and not 403. BOTH with .trustedOrigins("https://spa.example") and app.cors allowedOrigins holding https://spa.example, http://localhost and capacitor://localhost: POST /auth/login with Origin https://spa.example (trusted but not the request's own origin) -> 200 cookie delivery (Set-Cookie for naru_at, naru_rt and naru_csrf, body csrfToken only, no accessToken); the same login with Origin http://localhost or Origin capacitor://localhost (in allowedOrigins, not in trustedOrigins) -> 200 body delivery with accessToken and no Set-Cookie (00 §6.4 row "R29 × BOTH 응답 모양", R29 (e) ②, (h)).
BOTH, Origin: null, POST /auth/login -> 200 body delivery without Set-Cookie; POST /auth/register with .register(true) from the same client -> 201 body delivery without Set-Cookie.
BOTH login without Origin but with a same-origin Referer -> cookie delivery.
Every token-issuing response carries Cache-Control: no-store [INFERRED:med:advisory]

records.requirement: Hard account lockout shall be active only when a Lockout policy is configured, shall apply only to password login, shall not apply to trusted-device requests or to API-key authentication, and shall be released by DELETE /auth/admin/users/:id/lockout.
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R34 (4) and edition 23 (password login only, API keys unaffected), R45 (DELETE /auth/admin/users/:id/lockout among the 15 admin endpoints), R39 (admin writes need the :write scope); §6.4 row "R34 × 새 기기 admin" (another admin releases the lock); 07 for the builder shape.
records.research:
- Decisive facts: hard lockout is opt-in because it lets an attacker lock out a victim on purpose (OWASP lockout-DoS); the default protection is the throttle (SEC-FLOW-011). Trusted devices are exempt, so a locked admin can still log in from a known device. API keys are a separate credential and are never locked by password failures (23rd ed.). Open: the lockout response status/code, the policy parameters and the success status of the DELETE route are not given in 00; 07 proposes Lockout.after(n).forMinutes(m) (and maxPerAccount).
- [2026-11-02] Decided (Q54, Q55, Q120): a locked login runs the hash step and gets the wrong-password answer 401 invalid_credentials under the SEC-TOKEN-009 floor, so lock state never reveals that an account exists. Rejected: 423 or 403 account_locked (friendlier, but it enumerates accounts). Builder Lockout.after(5).forMinutes(15) from 07; DELETE answers 204 and clears only the lock, not the throttle keys. Supersedes the Open line above.
- [2026-11-02] Correction to the note above (feasibility review 2026-11-02): the DELETE release clears the Lockout state and the user's user-only throttle key; IP keys and (user, IP) keys stay. 00 §6.4 row 'R34 × 새 기기 admin' names another admin's lockout release as a way out of the user-only-key 429 (AC-5, SEC-FLOW-012 AC-6), while the attacker's IPs remain limited.
records.implementationNotes: - Lockout value class in utils.auth (named in the 00 §2 tree) and a builder option; lock state stored with the throttle/device-trust storage defaults (REL-FLOW-001). The DELETE route lives in auth.adminRoutes() (IAM scope owns the admin endpoint table and R31 checks).

[wave-3 carried: absolute-form target; I-021] Decision: of an absolute-form `scheme://authority/path?query` target only the path (or `/` when the path is empty) and the query are kept. records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-1]

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with `Content-Length: 0` and an empty body without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no handler sees them; a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` records that it was never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422]
In every handler call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections]
The HTTP-level assertions of T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 run as tests through the in-memory adapter and the harness in `./gradlew build`. [D-397]

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with `Content-Length: 0` and, in wave 3 (until wave 4 adds the standard error body), an empty body. [D-395; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

[D-395; T02] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-3]

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]
A request with an unsupported method token is answered `501` with `Content-Length: 0` and, in wave 3, an empty body. [D-395]

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and, in wave 3, `Content-Length: 0`, asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-4]

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered in wave 3 with the same `426`, both headers and `Content-Length: 0`, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`; this is the dispatcher mapping that FR-HTTP-008 AC-7 relies on. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and `Content-Length: 0` in wave 3. [D-395] [T02]

records.title: Interim handler failure and unfinished-response handling

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with an empty body through the harness. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` but before commit is answered `500` with an empty body. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the `500` carries only `Content-Length: 0`; the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-8]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a wave 3 handler can reach) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; wave decision: abort() after completion; wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()` yields `202` with `X-A: 1` and an empty body, and the response is `COMPLETED`. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: when the handler returns with the response `NEW` the dispatcher calls `end()`, and with it `STREAMING` it runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-10]

`app.get("/a/b", h)` followed by `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build())` makes `GET /a//b` reach `h` after the harness freeze, showing the policy applies to registrations made before it. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; FR-ROUTE-006]

The `Router` is constructed only at the freeze, and a duplicate of D-044 surfaces as the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`, not at the second registration call. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-044] Decision: the freeze propagates the `RoutingConfigException` unchanged and leaves the app unfrozen, so `dispatcher()` keeps throwing `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-12]

After the harness freeze, `app.get(...)`, `app.route(Method, path, h)`, `app.route(MethodSet, path, h)` and `app.routerPolicy(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException`, and `RouteBuilder` registration methods (`get`, `put`, ...) throw `IllegalStateException` too, including on a builder obtained from `app.route(path)` before the freeze. [wave decision: Settings after the freeze] Decision: the internal WebSocket-route hook also throws `IllegalStateException` after the freeze, and a refused call records nothing. records.title: Response body writers send, html, stream and end

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.send("hé")` writes the UTF-8 bytes `68 C3 A9` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, and after `res.header("Content-Type", "text/csv")` it keeps `text/csv`. [D-091] Decision: a body writer adds its default `Content-Type` only when no `Content-Type` header is set, compared case-insensitively. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-2]

`res.html("

é

")` writes UTF-8 bytes with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. [D-092]

`res.send(new byte[]{0, (byte) 0xFF, 10})` writes exactly those three bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` when none was set, and keeps an explicitly set `Content-Type`. [D-093; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`res.stream(in, "application/pdf")` with a 1 MiB input writes all bytes in order with `Content-Type: application/pdf`, and a counting input stream shows that every `read(byte[], int, int)` call requests fewer bytes than the 1 MiB input. [D-094] Decision: the copy reads with an 8192-byte buffer and writes each chunk to the exchange output stream in order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-3]

`res.stream(...)` closes the input stream exactly once after a successful copy, after a read failure, and after `res.abort(...)` during the transfer, including when the handler already returned; the caller does not close it. [D-094; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: the single close is guarded by a compare-and-set. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-4]

`res.end()` completes the response with the status and headers set so far and no body. [D-095] Decision: on a non-bodyless response `end()` commits with `Content-Length: 0`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-6]

`res.stream(InputStream, contentType)` does not block until the copy ends: it commits the response and returns, the copy to the end of the stream runs after the handler returns, and the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends; a test whose handler returns right after `res.stream(...)` observes the call return before the input is read to its end. [D-094; D-103; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: `stream` sets `Content-Type` to the argument, commits with unknown length, enters `STREAMING` and returns; the dispatcher runs the copy on the adapter thread after the handler returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Response commit flag, abort and header CR/LF rejection

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.isCommitted()` is `false` before any body write and `true` after `res.send("x")` handed the status and headers to the in-memory adapter. [D-096] Decision: `abort` before any commit leaves `isCommitted()` `false`, sets `ABORTED` and aborts the exchange without writing a status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-8]
`res.abort(new IOException("x"))` during a `stream(...)` transfer makes the in-memory adapter report the connection closed abnormally and leaves the response state `ABORTED`. [D-097]

`res.abort(...)` on a response that is already `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` does nothing: no exception, the state is unchanged and the adapter sees no further close. [wave decision: abort() after completion]

`res.header("X\r\nY", "1")`, `res.header("X", "a\nb")` and `res.header("X", "a\rb")` each throw an exception and add no header. [D-098] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException`, the header list stays unchanged, and the response-state check runs first. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-7] Besides CR and LF, `res.header` also throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a name that is not an RFC 9110 token (empty, or a char outside tchar) and for a value holding any control character other than HTAB (such as NUL or DEL) or any char above U+00FF. [wave 3 implementation decision]

records.rationale: Covers D-096, D-097, D-098 and the wave decision on `abort()` after completion (no-op on a complete or aborted response).

records.title: Response state machine with single commit

acceptanceCriteria.text: A response starts in `NEW`, is `COMMITTED` once status and headers are handed to the adapter, and reaches `COMPLETED` after `send`; the adapter receives the status line and headers exactly once. [D-099]

`res.status(500)` or `res.header("X", "1")` after `res.send("a")` committed the response throws an exception and the sent status and headers stay unchanged. [D-100] Decision: the exception is `IllegalStateException` naming the current state, thrown in `COMMITTED`, `STREAMING`, `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED`, and nothing changes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-10]
A second body call (`send`, `html`, `stream` or `end`) after a body was sent throws an exception and writes no further bytes. [D-101]

After `res.stream(...)` returns, the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends, then `COMPLETED`, or `ABORTED` on abort; a read failure of the input stream during the copy, including after the handler returned, ends the response `ABORTED` with the input stream closed (FR-HTTP-014 AC-5). [D-103; D-097; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: a read failure during the copy sets `ABORTED`, calls `exchange.abort()` and closes the input, without rethrowing to the adapter. records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. This order applies to requests that passed the lifecycle gate; the unrecognised-method-token `501` comes after the validator check and before a `Request` is built.

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`) without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: a pre-request `400` or `501` carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and the `Content-Length` of the standard body; for a `HEAD` method token the `Content-Length` is kept and no body bytes are written. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-14]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them; a recording global middleware, a recording `onError` and a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` record that they were never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
In every handler and middleware call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; I-014]

records.requirement: The system shall provide a dispatcher that takes each exchange from an `HttpAdapter` that passed the lifecycle gate of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013, checks the asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` first, then rejects a raw path not starting with `/` with `400`, then rejects a raw path refused by the wave 2 path validator with `400`, and only then calls the router lookup and either runs the middleware pipeline and the matched `RouteHandler` with a `Request` and a `Response` or writes the automatic response, where the pre-request rejections are answered before any `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them, and the two `400` rejections carry the standard error body.

records.title: Automatic responses for router lookup results with the standard error body (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `NOT_FOUND`). [D-395; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: the fallback answers only a response that is still `NEW`, through the request's `Response`, keeping the headers a middleware set; a response that is no longer `NEW` is left as it is. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-15]

With only `POST /p` registered, `GET /p` is answered `405` with `Allow` listing `POST, OPTIONS`, and with `GET /r` registered `DELETE /r` is answered `405` with `Allow` including the automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, both with the standard error body (`code` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`). [D-395; T02; D-134] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order.

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

`TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and `CONNECT /` with `CONNECT` disabled are each answered `501` with the standard error body (`code` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) after the global middleware ran, while a request with an unrecognised method token (FR-ROUTE-013) is answered `501` with the standard error body before any `Request` is built, as FR-HTTP-021 AC-4 states. [D-395; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; D-422] Decision: the dispatcher tells the two cases apart by whether the method token parses to a `Method` value.

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and the standard error body (`code` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`), asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd; wave decision: 426 and 501] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `.

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered with the same `426`, both headers and the standard error body, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and the standard error body. [D-395; T02]

A recording global middleware runs once before each of the `404`, `405`, `426`, automatic `OPTIONS` and disabled-`TRACE`/`CONNECT` `501` answers above and not for the unrecognised-token `501`, and a recording `onError` records no call for any of them. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; residual: onError scope; D-117]

records.title: Handler failure and unfinished-response handling through the wave 4 error path

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `INTERNAL_ERROR`) through the harness when no `onError` is registered. [D-127; D-132; wave-4 carried: interim failure handling replaced]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` and header `X-A: 1` but before commit is answered `500` with the standard error body; the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [D-127; D-132; D-134]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a handler can reach before wave 5) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; D-131; wave decision: abort() after completion]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()`, and a middleware that returns without responding or calling `next.run()`, each yield the status and headers set so far (`202` with `X-A: 1`, and `200` for the middleware case) with an empty body, the response is `COMPLETED`, and the app logger received one `warn` naming the method and path. [D-126] Decision: the finishing behaviour is a `warn` through the app logger followed by `end()`; with the response `STREAMING` the dispatcher runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread and logs no warning.

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400 through the error path (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space.

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave-4 carried: malformed query reaches middleware and onError] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse raise `HttpException` with status `400`; the dispatcher parses the query after the middleware ran and before the handler, so global and prefix middleware run, a middleware that reads `req.query(...)` receives that exception, and it reaches `onError` through the error path of FR-APP-005. The query is parsed after the route middleware ran and before the handler; a request without a matched route gets the fallback answer (`404`, `405`, ...) and its query is parsed only if a middleware reads it.

records.title: Express common HTTP methods, HEAD/OPTIONS and default outcomes

acceptanceCriteria.text: Supported common HTTP method tokens, including explicit TRACE/CONNECT and extended methods such as COPY, can be registered and observed through a documented Java API while existing Method/MethodSet usage remains available; case-sensitive token handling and actual adapter restrictions are tested.

Common HTTP defaults match case-insensitively and permit one trailing slash while preserving repeated slashes, unless the user selects explicit policy options. HTTP default changes do not silently change WS/strict-extension behavior.

HEAD falls back to GET locally within each Route according to registration order; a later explicit HEAD does not override an already selected earlier GET Route. HEAD suppresses response bytes while retaining the appropriate status/headers.

OPTIONS collects methods from matching routes only while the stack falls through, implicitly includes HEAD for GET, deduplicates and alphabetically sorts with comma-space delimiters, and returns the matching plain-text body/headers; downstream middleware can answer instead.

An ordinary unsupported path or method fallthrough uses the agreed Express404/finalhandler result rather than automatic global405; explicit options/HTTP errors retain their status. OPTIONS* and transport method parsing are separately documented/tested.
Existing Method.any() semantics and CORS preflight convenience remain identified extensions and do not suppress explicit common-method routes or silently replace ordinary OPTIONS behavior.

records.title: req.bodyStream returns the raw request body under the one-read rule

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the in-memory adapter, `bodyStream()` returns exactly the bytes sent for a JSON body mixing spaces and line breaks, a binary body holding all 256 byte values, an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body and a body sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, the gzip body still compressed.
On a request without a body, `bodyStream()` returns a non-null stream whose first `read()` returns -1.
After `bodyStream()` was read, `req.body(Map.class)` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`, and after `req.body(Map.class)` read a JSON body, `bodyStream()` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`.

Once `bodyStream()` or `bodyStream(long)` returned, even with no byte read, `req.body(...)`, `req.form(...)` and `req.parts()` throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` whatever the request `Content-Type` (JSON, urlencoded, multipart or none).
On a `Content-Type: application/json` request, `req.form("a")` returns `null` and `req.parts()` an empty list without reading the body, and a following `bodyStream()` returns the whole body.

On a request without a body, a second `bodyStream()` returns the same object as the first, and a following `bodyStream(2048)` (a limit different from the app's `rawBodyLimit`) throws `IllegalStateException`.
`bodyStream()` counts as `bodyStream(L)` where `L` is the app's `rawBodyLimit`: with `rawBodyLimit(4096)`, `bodyStream()` followed by `bodyStream(4096)` before any read returns the same object.
On a request with a body, after one byte was read from `bodyStream()`, a further `bodyStream()` and a further `bodyStream(2048)` each throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`, whatever the limit.

A `read` that returns at least one byte, a `skip` that advances and a `close` of the returned stream each count as consumption, so a later `bodyStream` call throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`, while `available()` does not count and a later call with the same limit still returns the same object.

When a handler neither reads `bodyStream()` to its end nor closes it, the framework closes the returned stream and the adapter's request input exactly once in the request cleanup after the response ends, which a recording adapter input asserts.

`BodyStateTest#sdsAc11_FR_HTTP_019_AC5_requestHasNoPublicBodyReadingMethod`, re-pointed to this requirement, accepts `body(Class)`, `body(TypeRef)`, `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts` as before and exactly `bodyStream()` and `bodyStream(long)` as the `InputStream`-returning readers, which take the body through the `RAW` kind of `BodyState`, and still finds no `byte[]`, text or other raw reader on `Request`.
