The raw bytes serve webhook signature checks and file relays as well as the proxy; the repeat rule stops later code from silently continuing a body that earlier code read in part.
records.implementationNotes: - Take the body through `BodyState.begin(Kind.RAW)` (the kind already exists) and wrap the adapter input with `body.stream(...)` so the access log counts it. The same-object rule for an unconsumed repeat call sits in `DefaultRequest` above `BodyState`, so FR-HTTP-019 AC-3 (a second raw `begin` through `BodyState` throws) stays true and is not expired; FR-HTTP-019 AC-5 is a statement about the wave 3 merge. The cleanup of AC-10 is the existing `DefaultRequest.closeBody()` path (FR-APP-023 AC-3). Pitfall (design D-057, code map risk R-2): on TinyHttpd the adapter body stream throws unchecked `HttpException` (`413`, `408`, `400`) from `read()`, so a `bodyStream` reader can see an unchecked exception besides `IOException`. records.title: Size limits of req.bodyStream: app default, per-call limit, 413 before reading and BodyTooLargeException while reading

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `app.rawBodyLimit(1024)`, `bodyStream()` on a 1025-byte body without `Content-Length` returns the first 1024 bytes and throws `BodyTooLargeException` with `limit()` 1024 on the read that would return byte 1025, never returning a byte beyond the limit.

In an app whose `rawBodyLimit` is 1 MiB, `bodyStream(2097152)` reads a 1572864-byte (1.5 MiB) body to its end, and `bodyStream(1024)` throws `BodyTooLargeException` on the read that would return byte 1025, each limit applying to that call only.
`bodyStream(0)`, `bodyStream(-1)` and `bodyStream(1073741825)` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, while `bodyStream(1)` and `bodyStream(1073741824)` are accepted.

When the declared `Content-Length` is larger than the limit in force (the app's `rawBodyLimit` for `bodyStream()`, the argument for `bodyStream(long)`), the `bodyStream` call itself throws `HttpException` with status `413` before any byte is read from the adapter's request input, which a recording input asserts.

A chunked request body (no `Content-Length`) larger than `rawBodyLimit`, read through `bodyStream()`, throws `BodyTooLargeException` on the read that crosses the limit, and when the handler lets that exception leave unwrapped the client receives `413` with the standard error body (FR-APP-006 code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`).

records.title: req.headerNames() and req.rawHeaders() enumerate request headers as the adapter reported them

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the in-memory adapter, a request carrying `X-A: 1`, `x-a: 2` and `X-B: 3` gives `headerNames()` iterating exactly `[x-a, x-b]`.
For the same request `rawHeaders()` holds exactly the entries (`X-A`, `1`), (`x-a`, `2`), (`X-B`, `3`) in that order, with name case and duplicate names kept.

`add`, `remove` and `clear` on the `headerNames()` set, `add`, `set` and `remove` on the `rawHeaders()` list and `setValue` on any of its entries each throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, and the results stay unchanged.

Under the default locale `tr-TR`, a request header `TITLE: x` appears in `headerNames()` as `title`, because names are lowercased character by character without a locale (`Character.toLowerCase`), never with the default locale.
Two calls of `headerNames()`, and two calls of `rawHeaders()`, in one request return the same instance.

For every name of `headerNames()`, `req.headers(name)` equals, in order, the values of the `rawHeaders()` entries whose name matches it case-insensitively, so the enumeration keeps every value of a repeated header.

Names that match case-insensitively by `String.equalsIgnoreCase` are one name and nothing else is: through the in-memory adapter, `X-İd: 1` with `x-id: 2` gives one listed name `x-id` whose `headers` are `[1, 2]`; `X-Σ: 1` with `x-σ: 2` gives one name `x-σ` with `[1, 2]`; `x-ıd: 1`, `X-İd: 2` and `x-i̇d: 3` give names whose `headers` together hold each value exactly once; and every listed name has the length of its first raw name.

records.title: res.append adds a response header line under the res.header check

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that calls `res.append("Set-Cookie", "a=1")` and then `res.append("Set-Cookie", "b=2")` makes the client receive two `Set-Cookie` header lines, `a=1` then `b=2`.

`res.header` keeps its replace semantics: `res.header("X", "1")` followed by `res.header("X", "2")` sends the single line `X: 2`, while `res.header("X", "1")` followed by `res.append("X", "2")` sends both lines in that order.
`res.append` returns the same `Response` object, so `res.append("A", "1").append("A", "2").status(201)` chains.
`res.append("X", value)` with a value holding CR, LF, NUL, DEL or U+0100 throws `IllegalArgumentException` and adds no header line, exactly as `res.header("X", value)` does for the same value.
`res.append` with an empty name or a name that is not an HTTP token (for example `X Y` or `X:Y`) throws `IllegalArgumentException` and adds nothing, while a value holding HTAB or U+00FF is accepted.
On a committed response `res.append` throws `IllegalStateException` and adds nothing, as `res.header` and `res.addCookie` do.

records.title: req.isFromTrustedProxy() reports whether the app's proxy trust setting trusts the direct peer

acceptanceCriteria.text: `isFromTrustedProxy()` returns `false` on an app with no proxy trust setting, on an app with `trustProxyHops(0)` and on an app with an empty `trustProxyCidrs()`.
`isFromTrustedProxy()` returns `true` on an app with `trustProxyHops(1)`, on an app with `trustProxyHops(3)` and on an app with the legacy `trustProxy(true)`.
On an app with `trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`, `isFromTrustedProxy()` returns `true` for a request whose socket address is `10.1.2.3` and `false` for one whose socket address is `192.168.0.1`.
Under `trustProxyCidrs(...)`, a request whose socket address does not parse as an IPv4 or IPv6 address (for example an empty or `unknown` peer of the in-memory adapter) gets `false`.

`isFromTrustedProxy()` and the forwarding decision of `remoteAddress()` and `isSecure()` call one package-private helper of `ProxyTrustSetting`, and a unit test of that helper over the settings of AC-1 to AC-4 gives the same answers as `isFromTrustedProxy()`.

records.title: res.onAbort notifies listeners once when a response ends abnormally

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that registers a listener with `res.onAbort` and then calls `res.abort(new IOException("x"))` sees the listener run exactly once, and a second `res.abort` call runs it no further time.
A listener registered on a response that then completes normally through `send`, through `stream` copied to its end or through `relay` copied to its end is never run, also not after completion.
A listener registered after the response was aborted runs immediately, once, on the thread that calls `res.onAbort`.

With two listeners registered where the first throws `RuntimeException`, an abort still runs the second listener, the first listener's exception is logged through the app logger, the response ends `ABORTED` and a stream input it owned is closed.
`res.onAbort(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, and reflection finds the return type of `onAbort` to be `void`.
When a thread other than the request thread calls `res.abort` during a streaming transfer, the listener runs on that aborting thread; the core never hands it to the request thread.

An abort that an exchange reports through `HttpExchange.onAbort` (IR-HTTP-009) runs each `res.onAbort` listener once, and the core adds no detection of its own: with a test exchange whose SPI `onAbort` is not overridden, closing the client side runs no listener while `res.abort` still does.

The javadoc of `Response.onAbort` states that the listener may run on a thread other than the request thread and that an adapter may not report a disconnect during an idle period until the next I/O, which a source test reads.

records.title: res.relay leaves Content-Type to the app, frames from its length argument and adds no defaultCache

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that sets no `Content-Type` and calls `res.relay(in, 5)` with a 5-byte stream makes the client receive no `Content-Type` header, `Content-Length: 5` and the 5 body bytes.
A `Content-Type` the app set before the call (for example `res.header("Content-Type", "application/x-custom")`) is sent exactly as set, with no charset or other change.

A `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding` header the app set before the call (`res.header("Content-Length", "99")`, `res.header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")`) is dropped, and the framing comes only from the `contentLength` argument.

Headers set before the call through `res.header`, `res.append` and `res.addCookie` are sent as set, and the header list the in-memory adapter receives at commit equals those headers plus `Content-Length` when the length is sent, with no other header added by the core.

In an app with `app.defaultCache(CachePolicy.noCache())`, a response sent with `res.relay` carries no `Cache-Control`, while a `Cache-Control` the app set with `res.header` or `res.cache` before `relay` is sent as set.

Restating FR-STATIC-008 AC-5 with the change: with the default `defaultCache(null)` a JSON route and a static file without a matching pattern send no `Cache-Control`; with `defaultCache(CachePolicy.noCache())` every response that holds no `Cache-Control` at commit, error and `304` responses included, sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`, while `res.cache(noStore())`, `res.header("Cache-Control", "max-age=5")`, a matching `options.cache` pattern and a global middleware's `res.header("Cache-Control", "private")` keep their own value; a response written by `res.relay` is the one exception and never receives the `defaultCache` value.

records.title: res.relay sends exactly contentLength bytes, keeps the length on HEAD and 304, and owns its stream like res.stream

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.relay(in, 5)` with a stream that ends after 3 bytes aborts the response after the commit: the adapter sees the connection closed abnormally and the response state is `ABORTED`.
`res.relay(in, 5)` with a stream holding 8 bytes sends exactly 5 body bytes, closes the stream and completes the response normally (state `COMPLETED`, no abort).
`res.relay(in, -1)` commits with unknown length and no `Content-Length` header, leaves the framing to the adapter and copies the stream to its end.
`res.relay(in, -2)` and `res.relay(in, Long.MIN_VALUE)` throw `IllegalArgumentException` and close the stream they were given.

For a `HEAD` request and for a response whose status is `304`, `res.relay(in, 5)` commits `Content-Length: 5` with no body bytes to the adapter (the in-memory test adapter delivers that header to the client), closes the stream without reading it and completes normally; `res.relay(in, -1)` there commits no `Content-Length` and no body; whether a client receives the `Content-Length` of a `304` is the adapter's choice (RFC 9110 §8.6 makes it optional; FR-SVL-010 and FR-ENGINE-014 state the built-in adapters).
For a response whose status is `204`, `res.relay(in, 5)` sends neither a body nor a `Content-Length` header, closes the stream without reading it and completes normally.

`res.relay` commits and returns without reading the stream to its end, the copy runs after the handler returns, and a handler that returns right after `relay` observes the call return before the input is read to its end.

The response closes the relayed stream exactly once after a successful copy, after a read failure and after `res.abort(...)` during the transfer, the caller not closing it, and a `relay` call on an already committed response throws `IllegalStateException` and closes the stream it was given, as `res.stream` does.

Restating FR-HTTP-017 AC-1 with the change: `res.status(204).send("x")` yields `204` with zero body bytes, and for every body writer other than `relay` a `204` or `304` response commits with length 0, adds no `Content-Length` header and drops the body bytes; `relay` alone keeps a non-negative length as `Content-Length` on `304` in the headers it commits to the adapter.

records.title: Scope grammar, covering semantics and reserved auth-* resources

acceptanceCriteria.text: Valid grants: posts:read, posts:*, *, auth-users:read, auth-groups:*. Invalid (IllegalArgumentException at registration): Posts:Read, posts, posts:read:own, po*, *:read, posts::read, a resource of 33 characters, posts read.

Covering table: posts:* covers posts:write and posts:*; posts:read does not cover posts:write; * covers anything:here and posts:*; posts:read does not cover posts:*; admin:* does not cover posts:write.
A required scope (auth.require) containing * is rejected at registration with IllegalArgumentException; only grants may contain wildcards.
RolePolicy.builder().role("x", "auth-reports:read").build() throws (reserved auth-* resource); auth-users, auth-groups and auth-apikeys with read, write or * are accepted.

Scope matching uses no regular expression at request time and performs at most 3 hash lookups per required scope (exact, resource:*, *). [INFERRED:med:advisory] (03 §2: at most segments + 1 hash lookups, no regex; 00 R46 does not state it)
Scopes exposes a public covers(grant, required) check (name not final) usable by app code without an Auth instance.

records.title: User delete ordering: memberships, then API keys, then the user row

acceptanceCriteria.text: Deleting user u7 with memberships in eng and ops and 2 API keys calls GroupAdminStore.removeUser(u7) (or removeMember per group), then ApiKeyStore.deleteAllByOwner(u7), then UserStore.delete(u7), in that order.
If removeUser throws, the response is 503, deleteAllByOwner and UserStore.delete are not called, and the user row still exists.
If deleteAllByOwner throws, the response is 503 and the user row still exists; a second delete call completes and leaves no membership, key or row for u7.
Each step is idempotent: running the full delete twice on an already-deleted user returns the A5 unknown-user 404 NOT_FOUND of IR-IAM-005 AC-6 on the second call and raises no store error.
After a successful delete, a refresh with the user's refresh token answers 401 because findById returns null.

records.title: JdbcLoginThrottle and JdbcDeviceTrust shared counters

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two JdbcLoginThrottle instances over one SQLite database each record 3 failures for the same (user, IP) key within one window: the shared count is 6, and with max 5 the key is blocked after the 5th combined failure. [INFERRED:low:test-parameter]
recordFailure issues an UPDATE ... SET <count> = <count> + 1 (with an insert path for a missing row) rather than SELECT-then-UPDATE (SQL-text test).

JdbcLoginThrottle.usesLimitArguments() returns true and retryAfter(key, max, windowMillis) / recordFailure(key, max, windowMillis) apply the passed max and window (a call with max 100 does not block at 5).
JdbcDeviceTrust: a device token invalidated on node A (failure limit 5 per 15 minutes reached) is rejected on node B on the next login attempt.
Both classes reference only java.sql and javax.sql types.

The counting window is fixed, not sliding (00 gives no rule; decided 2026-11-02): each key row holds its count and its window start, taken from auth's TimeSource and passed as a statement parameter (never the database clock); a failure within windowMillis of the window start adds one, and the first failure after the window has passed resets the row to count 1 with a new window start in the same atomic statement. With max 5 and windowMillis 900000 over SQLite: 4 failures, then the TimeSource advanced by 900001 ms, then 2 failures leave the key with count 2 and not blocked; 5 failures within one window block the key until the window start plus 900000 ms.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A4 with a username another user already holds plus a new password answers 409 with code duplicate_user and applied: [] in the response JSON (the A4 handler writes this answer itself, not the auth router ErrorMiddleware; statement); the target's username and password hash are unchanged.
A4 with a password and roles where changePassword loses a race to another write answers 409 with code write_conflict and applied: []; the roles are not applied and the admin reset is not retried.

A4 with a free new username plus a password that loses a race answers 409 with code write_conflict and applied: ["username"]; the new username is stored and the password hash is unchanged; exactly one onUserUpdated with origin ADMIN carrying only USERNAME is emitted, and no onPasswordChanged (00 R37 14th ed.: one onUserUpdated with what was applied; 00 user-change event table, A4 row: applied changes only).
A4 with username "Bob" on a target named "alice" stores "bob" (rename-path normalization); A4 with the target's own current username is not a 409, writes no rename and applies the other fields.
A4 by a delegated admin (auth-users:write, posts:read) carrying attributes plus roles ["editor"] (posts:write) answers 403 insufficient_scope and nothing is applied, including the attributes.

A4 where the password was applied and the following security write (setEnabled or setRoles) still fails after its 3 retries (the SINGLE_INSTANCE default throws an AuthUnavailableException with code security_write_conflict, IR-AUTH-003 AC-6, REL-IAM-001 AC-2) answers 503 with body code security_write_conflict and an applied list naming the password change, and one audit event security_write_conflict is emitted. The A4 handler catches that exception and writes this answer itself through AuthResponses (the auth error body plus the applied list; the exception does not reach the FR-AUTH-006 AC-3 ErrorMiddleware), and the A4 handler emits the audit event through the builder's AuditSink (FR-AUTH-009 AC-2). Exactly one onUserUpdated with origin ADMIN carrying only PASSWORD and one onPasswordChanged are emitted (00 R37 14th ed.; 00 event-table note: rows that change the password, A4 included, also emit onPasswordChanged).

A successful A4 changing username, enabled and attributes answers the A4 success status of IR-IAM-005 AC-5 with a hash-free user body and fires exactly one onUserUpdated event carrying all three applied changes, with origin ADMIN.

A4 with roles only leaves the target's ver unchanged; A4 with a password increments ver by exactly one; A4 with enabled false increments ver by exactly one (setEnabled(false) then bumpTokenVersion, SEC-IAM-003 AC-1); A4 with enabled true alone leaves ver unchanged.

Password-step and plain store failures are answered by the A4 handler too (statement): (a) A4 {username: a free name, password} over a test store implementing only the five required methods whose update() applies the rename but silently does not apply the hash change (the SINGLE_INSTANCE default changePassword throws an AuthUnavailableException with code security_write_conflict, REL-IAM-002 AC-7) answers 503 with body code security_write_conflict and an applied list naming only the username change; the new username is stored, the password hash and ver are unchanged, one audit event security_write_conflict is emitted, and exactly one onUserUpdated with origin ADMIN carrying only USERNAME and no onPasswordChanged are emitted. (b) A4 {password, roles} over a test store whose setRoles throws a store exception that is not an AuthUnavailableException (for example java.sql.SQLException) after changePassword succeeded answers 503 with body code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and an applied list naming the password change, one audit event of type user_update_failed is emitted, and exactly one onUserUpdated with origin ADMIN carrying only PASSWORD and one onPasswordChanged are emitted. In both cases the A4 handler writes the answer itself through AuthResponses and the exception does not reach the FR-AUTH-006 AC-3 ErrorMiddleware.

applied member format (open question Q74, decided 2026-11-02): in every A4 409 and 503 answer of this requirement the error body has a top-level member applied beside the error object (which holds code, message and requestId), whose value is a JSON array of the A4 request field names of the changes applied before the failing step, in application order; A4 {username: a free name, password, roles} whose setRoles fails as in AC-9 (b) answers with applied equal to ["username", "password"].

records.requirement: PATCH /auth/admin/users/:id (A4) shall run the R31 check once over all changed fields before applying any of them, then apply the username change (through the rename path), the password (changePassword with the re-read ver, no retry), the remaining security fields and the profile attributes in that order, answering 409 with an applied list holding only the changes already applied when the rename or the password step conflicts, 503 with the applied list when the rename, the password or a later step fails with a store error, with an audit event for every 503 after the password and for every security_write_conflict answer, and emitting one onUserUpdated event for what was applied. The A4 handler shall catch every such failure of these steps and write the 409 or 503 answer itself through AuthResponses: the rename DuplicateUserException and a false changePassword (409), an AuthUnavailableException thrown by the rename, by the password step (the SINGLE_INSTANCE default changePassword throws one with code security_write_conflict for an unconfirmed write, REL-IAM-002 AC-7) or by a later step, and any other store exception thrown by one of these steps (any exception from a store call other than DuplicateUserException, AuthRejection and IllegalArgumentException); the answer is the auth error body with the status and code the FR-AUTH-006 AC-3 mapping gives that failure (DuplicateUserException 409 duplicate_user; a lost password race 409 write_conflict, IR-AUTH-003 AC-3; an AuthUnavailableException 503 with its own code, security_write_conflict for an unconfirmed security write, IR-AUTH-003 AC-6; any other store exception 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE) plus the applied list of the changes applied before the failing step (empty, the username change, or the changes up to that step), carried as the top-level member applied of the error body: an array of the A4 request field names of the applied changes in application order (open question Q74, decided 2026-11-02), so none of these failures reach the auth router ErrorMiddleware. An AuthRejection or IllegalArgumentException thrown by a step after the password was applied is a failure after the password too and is answered by the A4 handler as 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with the applied list and an audit event (00 R37 14th edition: any field after the password that fails midway answers 503 with applied and leaves an audit event; open question Q76). The A4 handler also emits the audit event through the builder's AuditSink (FR-AUTH-009): security_write_conflict for an unconfirmed write at the password or a later step, and one event of type user_update_failed for any other failure after the password (00 R37 names no type; open question Q75, decided 2026-11-02).
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R37 "관리자 PATCH" (7th ed. Q-9: R31 once over all changed fields; 13th ed.: order username → password → other security fields → profile, 409 with applied: [] on a duplicate name; 14th ed.: same-name no-op, password race 409 carrying only an earlier rename, later failure 503 with applied and audit, one onUserUpdated), R37 12th ed. (admin username via the rename path), R37 T-1 (admin reset never retries), R37 6th ed. (role/group changes do not bump ver), §6.4 rows "R37 × PATCH 비밀번호 경쟁", "R37 × 관리자 이름 변경", "R37 × PATCH 이름과 비밀번호", "R37 × 동시 비활성화".
records.research:
- Decisive facts: the 13th-edition order exists so that a duplicate-name 409 happens before anything is written (the 10th-edition "password first" order changed the hash and then failed). R31 is checked once up front, so a partially authorized PATCH never applies the authorized half.
- Ground truth: admin password reset passes the re-read ver to changePassword and does not retry on false (only the user's own /auth/password retries once after re-verifying); security writes (setEnabled, setRoles, bumpTokenVersion) retry up to 3 times, then 503 + security_write_conflict; only rehash is ever skipped silently.
- Pitfall: 05 A4 bumps ver on role changes and calls R.revokeUser; 00 R37 6th ed. replaces that — roles and groups propagate through the principal cache TTL (R36), and only password, disable, logout-all and recovery bump ver. Two admins patching the same user concurrently: last write wins, documented.
- Open: the element format of applied (field names) and the 409 error code string are not given by 00; ACs assert only the list contents.
- Rejected: per-field transactions with rollback; stores are not transactional across field methods. Reopen if UserStore gains a multi-field atomic write.
- [2026-11-02] Decided (Q74, Q14, Q75, Q76): applied is a top-level array of A4 request field names in application order (AC-10); a lost password race is 409 write_conflict and a duplicate name 409 duplicate_user (IR-AUTH-003 AC-3); a store failure after the password audits user_update_failed; an AuthRejection or IllegalArgumentException after the password keeps its own status and adds applied (AC-11), so a client always learns that the password changed. Supersedes the Open line above.
- [2026-11-02] Correction to the note above (feasibility review 2026-11-02): an AuthRejection or IllegalArgumentException after the password is answered 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with applied plus a user_update_failed audit event, not with its own status. 00 R37 14th edition says any field after the password that fails midway gets 503, applied and an audit event (statement, AC-11).
records.implementationNotes:
- A4 handler in the adminRoutes() router (IR-IAM-005), registered with methodAsync because it may hash (REL-TOKEN-001).
- Uses the rename core shared with AuthUsers.rename (NFKC + Locale.ROOT normalization, same-name no-op, DuplicateUserException; FR-IAM-003), UserStore.changePassword with SINGLE_INSTANCE default algorithm (REL-IAM-001, REL-IAM-002), setEnabled/setRoles, then the mutator core of AuthUsers.update for attributes (SEC-IAM-001 field rules); all inside the per-user lock. It does not call the AuthUsers.rename or AuthUsers.update facade methods, because each raises its own beforeUserUpdate and onUserUpdated with origin APP (FR-IAM-003 AC-4, FR-AUTH-008 AC-1); the A4 handler raises one beforeUserUpdate over all changed fields and one onUserUpdated with origin ADMIN for the applied changes itself (FR-AUTH-008 AC-2/AC-3, AC-3 and AC-7 here; 00 user-change event table, A4 row).
- Service-account password and key-actor password writes are rejected earlier (FR-APIKEY-006, SEC-APIKEY-008).
- Bound by CON-AUTH-001..004.

records.title: Auth file key wiring, PROD and DEV policy, plain-value migration and doctor count

acceptanceCriteria.text: Additive API: NaruServe-api offers new FileUserStore(File, @Nullable AuthFileKey), new FileUserStore(File, long, Logger, @Nullable AuthFileKey) and KeySources.fromFile(File, @Nullable AuthFileKey); new FileUserStore(File), new FileUserStore(File, long, Logger) and KeySources.fromFile(File) still compile unchanged and behave exactly as the overload with a null key (API surface test).

File defaults inherit the key: with .users(new FileUserStore(file, key)) and no refresh, throttle or device-trust store configured, the effective default FileRefreshTokenStore, FileLoginThrottle and FileDeviceTrust carry the same AuthFileKey instance as that FileUserStore (internal accessor test); their files keep their current fields and format versions because none of their values is a secret (SEC-IAM-008 inventory).

PROD without a key: Auth.builder(KeySources.fromFile(keyFile)).mode(AuthMode.PROD).users(new FileUserStore(usersFile)) ... build() throws AuthConfigException whose message names FileUserStore(file, AuthFileKey), KeySources.fromFile(file, AuthFileKey) and NARU_AUTH_FILE_KEY (names not final); when only one of the two lacks a key the message names only that one; with a key for both, build() succeeds; a PROD Auth that uses neither FileUserStore nor KeySources.fromFile (for example InMemoryUserStore with KeySources.fromEnv) is not affected.

DEV without a key: the same configuration in AuthMode.DEV builds, logs exactly one WARN per build() naming each unencrypted file and NARU_AUTH_FILE_KEY, and the stores write what they write today: the users file keeps format version 1 and stores each passwordHash as the plain password-hash string, and the key file holds the raw 32 key bytes. (AuthMode has only DEV and PROD; tests that need no key run in DEV.)

Migration on first load with a key: given a version-1 users file with three users holding plain hashes (and one null-hash service account) and a raw 32-byte key file, constructing the stores with a key rewrites each file once atomically (AtomicFiles for the users file, the existing staging-and-rename path for the key file; no .bak, temp or staging file left): the users file then has format version 2 and every non-null passwordHash is enc(...), the null hash stays null, the key file holds enc(...), the three users log in with their old passwords, and a token signed before the migration still verifies after it.

After migration without the key: opening the migrated users file or key file with no key (DEV or PROD) fails closed with an IOException stating that the file holds encrypted values and that an AuthFileKey is needed, and the file is byte-for-byte unchanged; an older reader that knows only users-file version 1 rejects the version-2 file through REL-IAM-004 AC-7 instead of treating enc(...) as a hash.

Doctor count: the doctor report holds an item 'plain secret values in auth files' with the count of non-null plain passwordHash values plus plain key files; DEV without a key and the AC-5 fixture -> count 4 at WARN level; with a key after migration -> count 0 and no WARN; an Auth with no file store reports no such item (OPS-AUTH-001 runner).

Rotation is out of scope: no public method re-encrypts files under a new key; opening files with a different key fails closed (SEC-IAM-008 AC-4 and AC-5); docs/api states that key rotation is not supported in 0.11.0 and that the payload version byte reserves room for it.

Kotlin (CLAUDE.md T11): a Kotlin test compiles and runs val key: AuthFileKey? = AuthFileKey.fromEnv() with no platform type, then FileUserStore(file, AuthFileKey.of(ByteArray(32) { it.toByte() })) and KeySources.fromFile(keyFile, key) passed to Auth.builder(...).users(...).build(), and a password login through the in-memory harness succeeds.

docs/api/auth.md and docs/api/en/auth.md describe the enc(...) form, which values are encrypted and which stay plain with the reason (SEC-IAM-008 inventory), how to make a key (32 random bytes, base64, for example openssl rand -base64 32), AuthFileKey.of/fromEnv and NARU_AUTH_FILE_KEY, the PROD failure and the DEV WARN with what DEV stores, the migration on first load, the doctor item and the rotation limit, with Express-user framing and Java and Kotlin examples; a docs test asserts these items in both languages.

records.research:
- Decided (open items settled while authoring, per the project rule): migration runs on first load rather than on the next write of each record, because it is deterministic, testable in one step, and leaves no plain secret behind after start; the doctor count is then 0 in PROD and non-zero only in DEV without a key. records.title: req.body media-type, syntax, size, depth, UTF-8 and polymorphism checks

acceptanceCriteria.text: Bodies with `Content-Type` `application/json`, `application/json; charset=utf-8`, `application/problem+json` and `APPLICATION/JSON` are decoded, while `text/plain`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `application/jsonx`, `application/json; charset=iso-8859-1` and a missing `Content-Type` make `req.body(...)` throw `UnsupportedMediaTypeException`, answered `415` with the standard error body (code `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`) without calling the codec. [D-186; T09] Decision: an allowed type is `application/json` or `application/<subtype>+json`, compared case-insensitively, with no `charset` parameter or `charset=utf-8`. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-7]: the media type is checked before the codec is called or the body stream is read. Content-Type uses valid media-type token and quoted-parameter syntax; quoted delimiters in unrelated parameters are not charset declarations. Invalid syntax is rejected with415 before invoking the codec.
With the default codec, `{"a":1} x` and `{} {}` are answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`. [residual: Trailing JSON data; D-187; T09]

A body of 1048577 bytes with `Content-Length` is answered `413` with code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before the codec reads it, and a chunked body without `Content-Length` larger than the limit, decoded through the default `GsonJsonCodec`, is answered `413` (not `400`) after at most limit + 1 bytes were taken from the exchange stream; with `app.jsonLimit(10)` an 11-byte body gives `413` and a 10-byte body is decoded. [D-188; D-088; T09]
With the default codec, an array nested 65 levels deep is answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST` and one nested 64 levels deep is decoded. [D-189; T09]

A body holding the bytes `{"a":"` `0xC3 0x28` `"}` or a truncated UTF-8 sequence is answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`, because the core decodes the body with a UTF-8 decoder whose malformed and unmappable actions are `REPORT`. [D-190]

Decoding `{"@class":"<canary class>","class":"<canary class>","@type":"<canary class>"}` into `Object.class` with the default codec returns a `Map` and never initialises the canary class, whose static initializer records any loading. [D-191]
The bodies `null` and ` null ` decoded with `req.body(User.class)` and with `req.body(new TypeRef<List<User>>() {})` return `null`. [D-431; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`]

expiredAcceptanceCriteria.text: The bodies `{"a":`, `[1,]`, an empty body and a body of only spaces and newlines are each answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`; the empty and whitespace-only bodies never reach the codec, and an `IOException` thrown by `JsonCodec.decode` is turned into `HttpException` `400` with that exception as cause unless AC-9 applies. [D-187; T09; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`] Decision: the core maps a codec `IOException` to `400` and lets an unchecked codec exception reach the error path as `500`.

When decoding fails and the core's size-limited stream recorded an overrun (its internal `BodyTooLargeException`, an `IOException` that a codec such as Gson may wrap), the core answers `HttpException` `413`; when the failure's cause chain holds an `HttpException` (for example the adapter `408` of FR-ENGINE-005), that exception is rethrown with its own status; each failure of this requirement reaches `onError` and the access log like any handler exception of FR-APP-005. [D-186; D-187; D-188; D-219] Decision: the overrun is detected from the limited stream's state, not only from the exception the codec rethrows. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-11]: an `HttpException` found in the cause chain is rethrown unchanged (the same instance).

records.title: res.json encodes through the app codec and round-trips JSON values

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.json(value)` calls the app codec's `encode` once and sends status 200 (or the status set before) with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a `Content-Length` equal to the encoded byte count. [D-193]

A T08 echo route `res.json(req.body(type))` returns values equal to the sent ones for a POJO `User`, a `List<User>` read through `TypeRef`, the string `"x"`, the numbers `42` and `1.5`, `true` and `null`, while `{"n":42}` read with `req.body(Map.class)` comes back as JSON equal to `{"n":42.0}`, which the test compares as JSON values. [D-194; T08]
`res.json("hello")` sends exactly the 7 bytes `"hello"` and `res.json(null)` sends exactly `null`. [D-195]

A codec whose `encode` writes part of the output and then throws leaves the response uncommitted, and the request is answered `500` with exactly the standard error body of FR-APP-006 and no byte of the partial output. [D-136; D-112; wave-4 carried: res.json serialisation failure] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-12]: `res.json` encodes into a buffer that is discarded when `encode` throws, so the response stays `NEW` and the error path answers `500`.

`res.json(value)` on a response that is already committed or completed throws `IllegalStateException` before calling the codec; on a committed but not completed response (committed in the test through the internal response, as the wave 4 error-path tests do) the error path of FR-APP-005 aborts it, so the client sees an abnormally closed response and no standard error body, and on a completed response the client response stays as completed and nothing more is written. [D-136; FR-APP-005; FR-HTTP-016; wave-4 carried: a committed response is aborted]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `res.json(mapOf("success" to true))` inside a route lambda. [D-193; C-03; I-010]

records.title: GsonJsonCodec with STRICT, Unsafe-free defaults, a nesting limit and end-of-document check

acceptanceCriteria.text: `GsonJsonCodec` is public, final and implements `JsonCodec` with the public constructors `GsonJsonCodec()`, `GsonJsonCodec(Gson)` and `GsonJsonCodec(Gson, int maxDepth)` and the public static method `Gson defaultGson()`; a `null` `Gson` throws `NullPointerException` and a `maxDepth` below 1 or above 255 throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-196; wave decision: The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec] Decision: the depth setting is the constructor argument `maxDepth`, and `GsonJsonCodec()` uses `defaultGson()`. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-1]: the `IllegalArgumentException` message names `maxDepth`, and both exceptions are thrown before the instance keeps any state.

`defaultGson()` returns a `Gson` built with `Strictness.STRICT` and `disableJdkUnsafe()`: decoding `{a:1}`, `{'a':1}` and `{"a":1 /* c */}` with `new GsonJsonCodec()` throws `IOException`, and through `req.body` each is answered `400`. [D-197; D-198]

Decoding `{}` with `new GsonJsonCodec()` into a class whose only constructor takes arguments throws an unchecked exception and creates no instance, and through `req.body` the request is answered `500`. [D-199] Decision: a codec failure that is not malformed input stays unchecked and gives `500`, because it is a server-side type error. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-3]: the unchecked exception is Gson's `JsonIOException`, propagated without wrapping.

`new GsonJsonCodec()` and `new GsonJsonCodec(customGson)` both reject an array nested 65 levels deep with `IOException` and decode one nested 64 levels; `new GsonJsonCodec(gson, 10)` rejects 11 levels and decodes 10. [D-189; wave decision: The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-4]: the nesting limit is set on the `JsonReader` on every `decode`, so it also holds for an instance built from a caller-supplied `Gson`.
`decode` of `{"a":1} x` and of `{} {}` throws `IOException`, while `decode` of `null` and of ` null ` returns `null`. [residual: Trailing JSON data; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`]

Every malformed-input failure of `decode` (syntax, lenient construct, nesting, trailing data, wrong JSON type for the target) is thrown as `java.io.IOException` with the Gson exception as cause, and no `com.google.gson` type appears in a `GsonJsonCodec` method signature other than the constructor and `defaultGson()`. [D-187; D-196] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-6]: Gson's `JsonSyntaxException` and `MalformedJsonException` are rethrown as `java.io.IOException` with that cause, while `JsonIOException` stays unchecked (AC-3).
`encode(null, w)` writes `null`, `encode("hello", w)` writes `"hello"` and `encode` of a `List<User>` writes a JSON array through the configured `Gson`. [D-193; D-195]

`NaruServe-gson` main classes pass the animal-sniffer API 21 check and reference no TinyHttpd type, and a Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.jsonCodec(GsonJsonCodec(GsonJsonCodec.defaultGson(), 32))`. [C-02; I-001; C-03]

records.title: Nullability check over the public API packages of NaruServe-api

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test in `NaruServe-api` fails, naming the package, when `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` or `com.snoworca.naruserve.routing` lacks `@NullMarked` on its package, and it also asserts that `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` keeps `@NullMarked` although the method-level checks skip that package. [D-348]

The same test parses the nullable-accessor table of `docs/api/kotlin.md` and, for every row whose Kotlin type column ends in `?`, finds every public overload of that name that returns a value (for example `Request.query`, `header`, `form`, `cookie`, `file`, `lastEventId`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `body(Class)` and `body(TypeRef)`; the void overload `attribute(String, Object)` is skipped) and fails when `getAnnotatedReturnType()` lacks `@Nullable`; for every row without `?` it fails when such an overload's return type is `@Nullable`. [D-348; D-351]

Reflection over every public class and interface of the three public API packages in the main jar named by `naruserve.apiJar` (not the test class path) finds no `org.jspecify.annotations.NonNull` on a type, member, parameter or type use, because under `@NullMarked` an unannotated reference type is non-null. [D-348]

records.rationale: Covers D-348, wave decisions Nullability check (r1 W2-005) and its second reading (r2 W2-004), and the Kotlin-visible part of I-007 and I-010; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `package-info.java` of `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `.spi`, `.routing` and `.internal` each carries `@org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked`; `grep -rn NonNull NaruServe-*/src/main` finds no `@NonNull` (only `Objects.requireNonNull`); the nullable `Request` accessors are `query`, `header`, `lastEventId`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `body(Class)`, `body(TypeRef)`, `cookie`, `form` and `file` (`Request.java:29-127`). Decision: "has a nullability annotation" is satisfied by the package default plus `@Nullable`, because under `@NullMarked` an unannotated reference type is non-null by contract and Kotlin reads it as `T`; no `@NonNull` exists. The round-1 test "a null-capable type without `@Nullable`" is dropped because it cannot be derived from signatures. Pitfall: the test class path of `NaruServe-api` also holds classes of package `com.snoworca.naruserve` (for example `NullabilityFixture`, which carries `@NonNull` on purpose, CON-BUILD-011 AC-2); every enumeration of this requirement and of FR-KT-002 and FR-KT-003 therefore reads the classes of the main jar given by the existing system property `naruserve.apiJar` (`build.gradle:179-183`), never the test class path. Pitfall: JSpecify `@Nullable` is a type-use annotation, so on `<T> @Nullable T attribute(...)` it sits on the return type, not the method; reflection must read `getAnnotatedReturnType()`. Rejected alternative: adding `@NonNull` to every signature; it is redundant under `@NullMarked` and the wave 1 convention (CON-BUILD-011) already drops it; reopen only if Kotlin stops reading the package default.

Decision: the check list is the ten words that are Kotlin hard keywords and legal Java identifiers; the other Kotlin hard keywords (`break`, `class`, `do`, `else`, `for`, `if`, `interface`, `package`, `return`, `super`, `this`, `throw`, `try`, `while`, `continue`, `null`, `true`, `false`) are Java keywords or literals and cannot be method names. Pitfall: Kotlin soft and modifier keywords (`get`, `set`, `by`, `value`, `where`, `open`, `field`) are legal names and `app.get(...)` depends on it; adding them to the list would forbid the Express-style `get`. Rejected alternative: also scanning every other published module; their public classes (`TinyHttpdAdapter`, `GsonJsonCodec`, loggers, servlet classes) are implementation classes that app code rarely calls; reopen if one of them gains a keyword-named public method.

records.title: Engine-free multipart parser shared by every adapter: boundary 400, nested parts, part-header limits 413

acceptanceCriteria.text: The multipart parser is a class of `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` that references no adapter, TinyHttpd, Servlet or `java.nio.file` type, no class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` references TinyHttpd's `MultipartReader` (class-reference test), and the T13 to T16 tests and the T17 cases other than the mid-upload disconnect run both over a TinyHttpd socket and over the in-memory test adapter with the same results; the T17 mid-upload disconnect case of FR-MULTIPART-006 AC-1 runs over a TinyHttpd socket only. [D-247]

A `multipart/form-data` request without a `boundary` parameter, or whose boundary is empty, longer than 70 characters or contains a character outside the RFC 2046 `bchars` set, or whose body lacks the first delimiter or the close delimiter, is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 through `onError` when an accessor reads it, and the handler's accessor call throws `HttpException(400)`. Decision: a body truncated before the close delimiter is malformed and gets `400`. [D-236] Decision: the `boundary` parameter name is matched case-insensitively, a quoted-string value is unquoted, and the value must consist of RFC 2046 `bchars` with no trailing space. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-1] Decision: a part without a `Content-Disposition: form-data` carrying a `name` parameter is also malformed and answered `400`, and every temporary file of that parse is deleted before the `HttpException(400)` is thrown. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-2] Decision: bytes before the first delimiter and after the close delimiter are ignored as preamble and epilogue. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-3]

A part whose `Content-Type` is `multipart/mixed` inside a `multipart/form-data` body appears in `parts()` as one entry whose `contentType()` is `multipart/mixed` and whose content is the raw nested body bytes, and the parser does not split it into further parts. [D-237]

A part header line of 8192 bytes is accepted, a part header line of 8193 bytes is answered `413`, and a part whose header lines total more than 16384 bytes is answered `413`, both with the standard error body, like the other multipart limits. [D-235; D-233; wave decision: Oversized part headers] Decision: a header line is counted in bytes without its CRLF for the 8192 line limit, and the 16384 total is the sum of those line lengths. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-4]

Over TinyHttpd with default settings, a multipart body of 67108864 bytes in total holding a file part of 33554432 bytes is parsed and both reach the handler, while a body one byte above 67108864 is answered `413` by the core, because TinyHttpd's default body limit stays `-1` (no cap) and the adapter never sets `maxRequestBodyBytes` (FR-ENGINE-003 AC-7). [D-232; D-247; wave-5: FR-ENGINE-003]

records.title: Multipart and urlencoded size limits on accumulated received bytes answered 413

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `maxFileSize(1024)`, a file part of 1024 bytes is accepted and one of 1025 bytes is answered `413`; with `maxRequestSize(4096)`, a body of more than 4096 bytes is answered `413`; and with the default `maxParts` 20, a body of 20 parts is accepted and one of 21 parts is answered `413`; each `413` carries the standard error body of FR-APP-006 and passes through `onError`. [D-233; T15] Decision: under `maxParts` 20 the `413` is thrown when the 21st part delimiter is reached, before that part's headers are read. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-5] Decision: a file part fails with `413` on the first byte above `maxFileSize`, and text parts never count against `maxFileSize`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-6]

A chunked multipart body and a multipart body without `Content-Length` that exceed `maxRequestSize` are answered `413` once the accumulated received bytes pass the limit, the parser reads no more than the limit plus one internal read buffer of 8192 bytes of the body, and a body whose `Content-Length` already exceeds `maxRequestSize` is answered `413` before any part reaches the handler. Decision: the parser's internal read buffer is 8192 bytes. [D-234; T15] Decision: the body stream is wrapped in a limit counter bound to both `maxRequestSize` and `Content-Length`, so a `Content-Length` above the limit fails on the first read and a chunked body fails after the limit plus one read buffer. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-7] With unknown Content-Length, bytes in the epilogue after the closing delimiter count toward maxRequestSize as well; consume the remaining request body through the bounded counter before accepting the parse and clean temporary parts on overflow.
With the default `formLimit`, an urlencoded body of 1048576 bytes is parsed and one of 1048577 bytes is answered `413`, also when it is sent chunked without `Content-Length`. [D-238; D-234]

records.title: form, file, files and parts behaviour over urlencoded and multipart bodies with one shared parse

acceptanceCriteria.text: For the urlencoded body `name=Kim+Lee&name=x&city=%EC%84%9C%EC%9A%B8`, `req.form("name")` returns `Kim Lee`, `req.form("city")` returns `서울` and `req.form("zip")` returns `null`, decoded by the form rules of FR-HTTP-025 (`+` as space, percent-decoded UTF-8); an urlencoded body with malformed percent-encoding (`a=%G1`, `a=%4`) or invalid UTF-8 (`a=%FF`) makes the accessor throw `HttpException(400)`, answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006, like the malformed query of FR-HTTP-025; for a multipart body, `form(name)` returns the first part of that name that has no `filename` parameter, and never a file part. [D-240] Decision: an urlencoded pair without `=` (such as `a`) yields the value `""` and an empty pair (as in `a&&b=1`) is skipped; a multipart text part is decoded as strict UTF-8 and malformed bytes make the accessor throw `HttpException(400)`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-2] Decision: for an urlencoded body `parts()` is empty and `file(name)` returns `null`, while `form(name)` returns the first decoded value. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-3]

Decision: on a request whose `Content-Type` is neither `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` nor `multipart/form-data` and whose body is still unread, `req.form(name)` returns `null`, `file(name)` returns `null`, `files(name)` and `parts()` return empty lists, none of them reads the body, and a later `req.body(...)` on a JSON body still reads it; once `req.body(...)` has read the body, a call of `form`, `file`, `files` or `parts` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` (FR-HTTP-019 AC-3), as `docs/api/request.md` states. [D-240; D-241] Decision: the media type is the `Content-Type` text before `;`, trimmed and compared case-insensitively; for any other media type the accessors leave the body state untouched while it is unread and throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` once it is not. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-1]

Decision: a file part is a part whose `Content-Disposition` carries a `filename` parameter. `req.file("doc")` returns the first file part named `doc` or `null`, and `req.files("doc")` returns every file part named `doc` in body order, or an empty list when there is none. [D-241; T13]

A multipart request holding the text fields `title` and `tag`, two files named `photos` and one file named `doc` exposes `form("title")`, `form("tag")`, `file("doc")`, `files("photos")` with both files in body order, and `parts()` with all five parts in body order, all inside one handler. [D-242; T13]

Repeated calls of `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts` in one request parse the body once and return the same `UploadFile` instances, and after any of them a call of `req.body(...)` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` because the body was read as the `FORM` kind (exclusive kinds of FR-HTTP-019 AC-3); the body-state check of `req.body` runs before the JSON media-type check of FR-JSON-001, so this case never yields `UnsupportedMediaTypeException`. Decision: the four accessors share one cached parse result. [D-242; D-240; D-241] Decision: when the shared parse failed with `400` or `413`, a later accessor call throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Memory and disk spooling with bounded heap, server-generated temp names and unchanged client filenames

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `memoryThreshold(1024)`, a file part of 1024 bytes creates no file in the temp directory (the test lists the directory before and after), and a file part of 1025 bytes creates exactly one temporary file in the configured `tempDirectory` while its request runs. [D-243; T14] Decision: when byte `memoryThreshold`+1 of a file part arrives the temp file is created, the buffered bytes are flushed to it and the memory buffer is dropped. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-1]

Uploading a 32 MiB file with the default 64 KiB `memoryThreshold` keeps the used heap, measured after `System.gc()` before the upload and while the handler holds the `UploadFile`, from growing by 8 MiB or more. Decision: the asserted heap bound is 8 MiB for a 32 MiB upload. [D-244; T14]

Every temporary file is created through `File.createTempFile` in `tempDirectory` with the prefix `naru-upload-` and the suffix `.tmp`; for a part whose filename is `../../evil.sh`, `a/b\c.txt` (one backslash) or a 300-character name, the temporary file name contains no part of the filename or the field name, and no file appears outside `tempDirectory`. Decision: the temp-name prefix is `naru-upload-` and the suffix `.tmp`. [D-245; T16]

`UploadFile.filename()` returns the client's `filename` parameter unchanged, including `../../evil.sh` and a non-ASCII name, and `save(File)` writes only to the destination the app passes, so no framework code builds a path from the filename (a test checks that no file named after the client value appears anywhere under the temp directory or the working directory). [D-246; T16]

Decision: a multipart text part (one without a `filename` parameter) is never spooled and is held in memory, and the total of the content bytes of all text parts of one multipart request is capped by the `formLimit` of IR-MULTIPART-001 (default 1 MiB, like multer's `fieldSize` but per request), so the heap held by text parts never exceeds the same bound as an urlencoded body; with the default `formLimit`, one text part of 1048576 bytes reaches `form(name)` and `parts()`, one text part of 1048577 bytes is answered `413`, and two text parts of 600000 bytes each are answered `413`, each `413` with the standard error body; text parts also count against `maxRequestSize` and `maxParts` but not against `maxFileSize`. [D-243; D-244; D-238]

records.title: UploadFile content methods: save, transferTo, bytes limit and use after the request ended

acceptanceCriteria.text: `save(dest)` writes content byte-equal to the uploaded part for an in-memory part and for a spooled part, replacing an existing `dest`, and after it returns the spooled part's temporary file no longer exists. Decision: `save` replaces an existing destination file. [D-249; T18] Decision: `save` copies through a truncating `FileOutputStream` and then deletes the temp file, never `File.renameTo`, so the result is the same across file systems. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-3]
`transferTo(out)` writes the full content of an in-memory part and of a spooled part into `out`, and a test stream that records `close()` shows that `transferTo` never closed it. [D-250; T18]

`bytes()` returns the full content for a part of 8388608 bytes and throws `IllegalStateException` naming the part size and the 8388608-byte limit for a part of 8388609 bytes; `inputStream()` reads the full content and `size()` equals the number of content bytes. [D-251; D-248; D-239]

After the request of an upload has ended, `inputStream()`, `save(File)`, `transferTo(OutputStream)` and `bytes()` throw `IllegalStateException`, while `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()` and `size()` keep returning their values. Decision: only the content methods throw after the request ended. [D-252] Decision: when the request ends every `InputStream` handed out by `inputStream()` is closed, so a later read on it throws `IOException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-4]

Decision: after a successful `save(dest)`, a later `inputStream()`, `bytes()`, `transferTo(OutputStream)` or second `save(File)` on the same part throws `IllegalStateException` for in-memory and spooled parts alike, because the content now lives only at `dest`, while `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()` and `size()` keep returning their values; a test calls `bytes()` after `save` on a spooled part and on an in-memory part. [D-249; D-252] Decision: `close()` called before the request ended releases the content like `save`, after which the content methods throw `IllegalStateException` and the metadata methods keep their values. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Temporary upload file cleanup at request end, after save, after 413, on disconnect and through an after-onStop shutdown participant

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test that lists `tempDirectory` finds it empty after each of: a request whose handler ignores its spooled upload and returns; a request whose handler calls `save`; a request answered `413` because a spooled part passed `maxFileSize`; and a request whose client closes the socket after sending half of a spooled part over TinyHttpd. [wave decision: Spool cleanup closes the spool registry; D-255; D-254]

Each upload deletes its own temporary file when its request ends while other requests still hold open uploads, whose files stay until their own requests end. [D-254; wave decision: Spool cleanup closes the spool registry]

records.title: Proxy.to(url) accepts an http or https origin with an optional base path, strips trailing slashes and rejects every other URL at the call

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Proxy.to` throws `IllegalArgumentException` at the call for a URL with a query (`http://h:8081/?a=1`), a fragment (`http://h:8081/#f`), user information (`http://user@h:8081`), the scheme `ftp` (`ftp://h/x`) and no host (`http:///x`, `http://:8081`).

`Proxy.to` accepts `http://h`, `HTTPS://h:8443`, `http://127.0.0.1:8081` and `http://[::1]:8081`, accepts a host name only as dot-separated labels of 1 to 63 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`, each holding a letter or digit and neither starting nor ending with `-`, at most 253 characters in all with one optional trailing root dot, and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a host name such as `.`, `-`, `_` or `a..b`, an IPv6 literal with a zone id (`http://[fe80::1%25eth0]:8081`), a malformed IPv4 or IPv6 literal, a non-ASCII host, a port of `0`, `65536` or `abc`, and a string that is not a URL.

On a mount at `/api/orders`, `Proxy.to("http://h:8081/")` forwards `/api/orders/x` as `/api/orders/x`, and `Proxy.to("http://h:8081/base/")` and `Proxy.to("http://h:8081/base//")` forward it as `/base/api/orders/x`, so the proxy never builds a path holding `//` from the base path.
On a mount at `/api/orders`, `Proxy.to("http://h:8081/api/orders")` forwards `/api/orders/x` as `/api/orders/api/orders/x`.

`Proxy.to` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a base path that fails the request-target character or path segment checks of SEC-PROXY-001, for example `http://h/a/../b`, `http://h/a;x`, `http://h/a//b`, `http://h/%2e` and `http://h/a%zz`.
`Proxy.to(null)` throws `NullPointerException`.

records.title: Proxy option values are checked at the option call: range errors and managed header names throw IllegalArgumentException, null throws NullPointerException

acceptanceCriteria.text: `connectTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `readTimeout` and `totalTimeout` each throw `IllegalArgumentException` at the call for `0` and for `-1` in any unit (for example `readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`), and accept `1` nanosecond.
`retries(-1)` and `retryDelay(-1, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, while `retries(0)` and `retryDelay(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)` are accepted.

`bodyLimit(0)` and `bodyLimit(1073741825)` throw `IllegalArgumentException` while `bodyLimit(1)` and `bodyLimit(1073741824)` are accepted, and `maxConcurrent(0)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` while `maxConcurrent(1)` is accepted.

`requestHeader(name, value)` and `removeRequestHeader(name)` throw `IllegalArgumentException` for every name the proxy manages, in any letter case: `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Trailer`, `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Expect`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Host` (for example `requestHeader("Host", "h")`, `requestHeader("connection", "x")`, `requestHeader("X-Forwarded-For", "1.2.3.4")`, `requestHeader("Forwarded", "for=x")` and `removeRequestHeader("Host")`).

`requestHeader` and `removeRequestHeader` throw `IllegalArgumentException` for a name that is not an RFC 9110 token, and `requestHeader` for a value that `HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue` rejects, for example `requestHeader("X-A", "a\r\nb")` and `requestHeader("X-A", "a\u0000b")`.

`responseHeader(name, value)` and `removeResponseHeader(name)` throw `IllegalArgumentException` for the hop-by-hop names listed in AC-4 and for `Content-Length`, in any letter case, for a name that is not a token and, for `responseHeader`, for a value `isFieldValue` rejects, for example `responseHeader("Content-Length", "1")`, `removeResponseHeader("Transfer-Encoding")` and `responseHeader("X-A", "a\nb")`.

A `null` argument throws `NullPointerException` at the call, for example `requestHeader(null, "x")`, `requestHeader("X-A", null)`, `removeRequestHeader(null)`, `responseHeader(null, "x")`, `removeResponseHeader(null)`, `sslSocketFactory(null)` and `readTimeout(1, null)`.

Time options convert to the socket timeout in milliseconds by rounding up to at least 1 ms and clamping to `Integer.MAX_VALUE`: the package-private accessors report 1 ms for `readTimeout(1, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS)`, 2 ms for `readTimeout(1500, TimeUnit.MICROSECONDS)` and `Integer.MAX_VALUE` ms for `readTimeout(Long.MAX_VALUE, TimeUnit.DAYS)`, whose watchdog value saturates at `Long.MAX_VALUE` nanoseconds.
`Proxy.to("http://h").sslSocketFactory(factory)` with a non-null factory returns a new `Proxy` without an exception, and that proxy forwards plain HTTP without calling the factory.

records.title: Proxy request header forwarding: received order and duplicates kept, hop-by-hop and Expect removed, Cookie lines merged, no Via, headers checked and written in ISO-8859-1

acceptanceCriteria.text: Client headers `X-A: 1`, `X-B: 2` and `X-A: 3` arrive at the backend as three lines in that order with their values unchanged, and a header the proxy does not manage arrives with the name letters the adapter reported.

None of the client's `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization` and `Trailer` lines arrives at the backend, nor a header named in the client's `Connection` (for `Connection: close, X-Hop` the client's `X-Hop` does not arrive); the only `Connection` and framing lines the backend receives are the ones the proxy writes itself.

A client `Expect: 100-continue` header does not arrive at the backend, and a client that sends `Expect: 100-continue` with a body gets the body delivered to the backend and receives the backend's final response.
Client lines `Cookie: a=1` and `Cookie: b=2` arrive as the single line `Cookie: a=1; b=2` at the position of the first `Cookie` line.
The proxy adds no `Via` header, and an `OPTIONS` request carrying `Max-Forwards: 0` arrives at the backend with `Max-Forwards: 0` and the backend's response reaches the client.
A request whose header name is not an RFC 9110 token, or whose header value `HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue` rejects (for example a value holding NUL), gets 400 and no backend connection is opened.
A client header value holding the character U+00E9 as the adapter reports it arrives at the backend as the single byte 0xE9, because the proxy writes the request line and headers in ISO-8859-1.

The backend header block is, in order: `Host`; the client headers in received order without the removed and replaced ones, with the merged `Cookie` at the first `Cookie` position; `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Host`; the `.requestHeader` values in option-call order; then the framing header and `Connection: close`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On an app with no proxy trust setting, `Proxy.to("http://127.0.0.1:8081")` sends `Host: 127.0.0.1:8081` for a request whose `Host` is `gw.example`, and the backend receives `X-Forwarded-Host: gw.example`.

`Proxy.to("http://h")`, `Proxy.to("http://h:80")` and `Proxy.to("https://h:443")` send `Host: h`, `Proxy.to("https://h:8443")` sends `Host: h:8443`, and `Proxy.to("http://[::1]:8081")` sends `Host: [::1]:8081`.
With `.preserveHost(true)` the backend receives the client's `Host: gw.example` unchanged and also `X-Forwarded-Host: gw.example`; without the option `Host` is replaced as in AC-1.

For a request whose adapter reports no `Host` header, or a `Host` line whose value is empty after removing optional whitespace, the backend receives the target host as `Host` and no `X-Forwarded-Host`, with and without `.preserveHost(true)`.
A request carrying two `Host` lines gets 400 and no backend connection is opened.

records.title: Proxy fixed request headers: requestHeader replaces the client's same-name header, removeRequestHeader drops it, both apply last and the later call for a name wins

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `.requestHeader("X-Gateway-Source", "gateway")` every forwarded request carries exactly one `X-Gateway-Source: gateway`, also when the client sent `x-gateway-source: spoofed`.
With `.requestHeader("X-Forwarded-Prefix", "/api/orders")` the backend receives exactly one `X-Forwarded-Prefix: /api/orders`, also when the client sent its own `X-Forwarded-Prefix`.

With `.removeRequestHeader("X-User-Id")` a client `X-User-Id: admin` does not arrive at the backend, and with `.removeRequestHeader("X-User-Id").requestHeader("X-User-Id", "u")` exactly one `X-User-Id: u` arrives.

With `.requestHeader("X-A", "1").removeRequestHeader("X-A")` no `X-A` line arrives, neither the configured value nor the client's, and with `.requestHeader("X-A", "1").requestHeader("X-A", "2")` exactly one `X-A: 2` arrives.
With `.requestHeader("Via", "1.1 gw")` the backend receives `Via: 1.1 gw`, because fixed headers apply after the proxy's own header processing, which adds no `Via`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On `app.use("/api/orders", Proxy.to(url))`, `POST /api/orders/query?x=1&y=%ED%95%9C` with a JSON body arrives at the backend with the method `POST`, the request target `/api/orders/query?x=1&y=%ED%95%9C` and the JSON body bytes identical to those the client sent.

records.title: Proxy request body framing to the backend: the length header is rewritten for the body actually sent, streamed without buffering, with a one-byte pre-read for requests without length headers

acceptanceCriteria.text: A bodyless `GET` arrives at the backend with neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`.

`POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` requests sent without length headers and without a body arrive with `Content-Length: 0`, while `DELETE`, `OPTIONS` and an extension method sent the same way arrive with no length header.
A `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` request arrives chunked with no `Content-Length`, and the backend decodes exactly the body bytes the client sent.
A `Content-Length: n` request arrives with the single line `Content-Length: n` and exactly those n body bytes.
A request that carries a body but neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`, such as a POST the servlet adapter received over HTTP/2, arrives chunked with the whole body.

When a client sends `Content-Length: 10`, then 5 body bytes and then disconnects, the backend's connection is closed before it receives 10 body bytes, so the incomplete request is never complete at the backend.

urlencoded, binary, chunked and large bodies arrive byte for byte, and a proxy JVM started with `-Xmx64m` forwards a 1 GiB body through a mount with `.bodyLimit(1073741824)` without an `OutOfMemoryError`.

The one-byte pre-read runs after `req.bodyStream(...)` returns and before the concurrency slot is taken and the total-timeout watchdog starts, as a unit test that records the order of these steps shows.

records.title: Proxy body limit and client body failures: bodyLimit or rawBodyLimit gives 413, read failures close the backend connection, a consumed body gives 500 without connecting

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request whose `Content-Length` exceeds `n` on a mount with `.bodyLimit(n)`, and one whose `Content-Length` exceeds the app's `rawBodyLimit` on a mount without the option, each get 413 and no backend connection is opened.

On an app whose `rawBodyLimit` is 1 MiB, a mount with `.bodyLimit(2097152)` forwards a 1.5 MiB body completely, and a mount with `.bodyLimit(1024)` answers 413 to a 2048-byte `Content-Length` body although the app limit is larger.

A chunked body that passes `n` while being forwarded through a mount with `.bodyLimit(n)` makes the proxy close the backend connection, the client receives 413, and the exception that reaches `onError` is an `HttpException` with status 413 whose `getCause()` is a `com.snoworca.naruserve.BodyTooLargeException`.

Any other exception thrown while reading the client body, including an unchecked `HttpException` with status 400, 408 or 413 thrown by the TinyHttpd body stream and an `IOException` from a client disconnect, closes the backend connection and reaches the error flow unwrapped.

A request whose body an earlier middleware read with `req.body(...)`, or partly read through `req.bodyStream()`, gets 500 with no backend connection, and the exception that reaches `onError` is the `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` or `IllegalStateException` from `req.bodyStream`, unwrapped.

records.title: Proxy method handling: tokens forwarded as received, CONNECT and TRACE answered 405, WebSocket upgrades passed to next(), other upgrades forwarded without Upgrade, no next() after forwarding

acceptanceCriteria.text: Requests with the methods `PATCH`, `PROPFIND` and `PURGE` arrive at the backend with the same method token in a request line ending in `HTTP/1.1`.
A request whose method, as the adapter reports it, is not an RFC 9110 token (for example `GE(T` through the in-memory adapter) gets 400 and no backend connection is opened.
Origin-form `CONNECT /api/orders/x`, `TRACE /api/orders/x` and `trace /api/orders/x` each get 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS`, and no backend connection is opened.

A WebSocket upgrade request (`GET` with `Connection: upgrade` and `Upgrade: websocket`, judged by `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade` with each header's lines joined by `, `) makes the proxy call `next()` and open no backend connection.

With `app.use("/api/orders", Proxy.to(url))` and `app.ws("/api/orders/live", ...)` registered in either order, a WebSocket upgrade to `/api/orders/live` reaches the `app.ws` handler and never the backend.

A `GET` carrying `Upgrade: h2c` and `Connection: Upgrade, HTTP2-Settings`, and a `POST` carrying `Upgrade: websocket`, arrive at the backend without `Upgrade` and without `HTTP2-Settings`, and the proxy never attempts an h2c upgrade or sends an HTTP/2 preface to the backend.

With two proxies mounted on `/api/orders` towards different backends, a request reaches only the backend of the first-registered mount, also when that backend answers 404 or cannot be reached, because the proxy does not call `next()` for a request it forwarded.

records.title: Proxy check order and its own answers: one fixed order of checks before forwarding, with 400, 405 and 501 thrown as plain HttpException with a null message

acceptanceCriteria.text: A WebSocket upgrade request to `/api/orders//live` makes the proxy call `next()` rather than answer 400, because the upgrade check runs first.
`TRACE /api/orders/../x` gets 405, not 400, because the method checks run before the path check.
`POST /api/orders/%2e%2e/x` with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked` gets 400, not 501, because the path check runs before the framing check.
A request carrying a header value with NUL and `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked` gets 400, not 501, because the header check runs before the framing check.

On a mount with `.bodyLimit(1)`, a request with the two lines `Content-Length: 5` and `Content-Length: 6` gets 400, not 413, and a `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked` request whose body an earlier middleware already read gets 501, not 500, because the framing check runs before `req.bodyStream(limit)`.

On a mount with `.maxConcurrent(1)` whose only slot is held by a pending request, a request whose `Content-Length` exceeds the body limit gets 413 and a request whose body an earlier middleware read gets 500, neither 503, because `req.bodyStream(limit)` runs before the slot is taken.

The 400, 405 and 501 answers of AC-2 to AC-5 reach `onError` as an exception whose class is exactly `com.snoworca.naruserve.HttpException`, whose `getMessage()` is `null` and which is not a `ProxyException`, and without `onError` the default error response carries the standard reason phrase of the status.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Backend statuses 200, 302, 400, 404 and 500 each reach the client unchanged, and for a backend `302` with `Location: /next` the client receives that 302 while the backend receives exactly one request, because the proxy never follows a redirect.

A backend response with two `Set-Cookie` lines, a `Content-Type`, a `Content-Length` and a body reaches the client with both `Set-Cookie` lines in received order, the same `Content-Type` value, the same `Content-Length` value and identical body bytes.

The proxy calls neither `res.header` nor `res.append` for the backend's `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization` and `Trailer` lines or for a header named in its `Connection` (for `Connection: close, X-Hop` the backend's `X-Hop`), as a unit test with a recording `Response` shows; over a socket the client receives none of the backend's `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization` and `X-Hop` lines, and receives the body of a chunked backend response that carries a `Trailer` header and trailer fields without that `Trailer` header and without the trailer fields.
When the backend response has no `Content-Type`, the client receives no `Content-Type` either.

The proxy never passes `Content-Length` to `res.header` or `res.append`; the backend's `Content-Length` value reaches `res.relay` as its length argument only, as a unit test with a recording `Response` shows.

When an app sets `res.header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")` and `res.header("X-App", "1")` before the proxy and the backend sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://a.example`, the client receives exactly one `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://a.example` and also `X-App: 1`.
When an app adds one cookie with `addCookie` before the proxy and the backend sends two `Set-Cookie` lines, the client receives three `Set-Cookie` lines.
When an app sets `res.header("Vary", "Origin")` before the proxy and the backend sends `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, the `Vary` the client receives holds both tokens `Origin` and `Accept-Encoding`.
A backend status line `HTTP/1.1 404 Nope` reaches the client as status 404 with the reason phrase the adapter writes for 404 by itself, not `Nope`.

Header names compare case-insensitively: a backend line `access-control-allow-origin: https://a.example` replaces an app-set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, and backend lines `set-cookie: a=1` and `Set-Cookie: b=2` are both appended next to an app cookie.

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-b, proxy, response, headers, options

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `.removeResponseHeader("Server")` the backend's `Server` line does not reach the client, and when the app sets `res.header("Server", "gw")` before the proxy the client receives exactly one `Server: gw`.

With `.responseHeader("Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=31536000")` the client receives exactly one `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` when the backend sends `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=0` and the app set another value before the proxy.
With `.responseHeader("X-A", "1").removeResponseHeader("X-A")` neither the backend's `X-A` nor the value `1` reaches the client.

With `.removeResponseHeader("X-A").responseHeader("X-A", "2")`, and with `.responseHeader("X-A", "1").responseHeader("X-A", "2")`, the client receives exactly one `X-A: 2` when the backend sends `X-A: 9`.

`.responseHeader` applies after the header copy and the `Location` rewrite: with `.responseHeader("Location", "/fixed")` a backend `Location: http://<target host:port>/x` reaches the client as exactly one `Location: /fixed`, and with `.responseHeader("X-A", "1")` two backend `X-A` lines reach the client as exactly one `X-A: 1`.
`.removeResponseHeader("server")` hides a backend `Server` line, and `.responseHeader("x-a", "1")` replaces a backend `X-A` line, because option names compare case-insensitively.
