records.requirement: The system shall enforce RFC 6455 on accepted WebSocket connections through TinyHttpd's websocket module, closing with `1002` for an unmasked client frame or an oversized or fragmented control frame, `1007` for invalid UTF-8 text and `1009` for a message above the configured limit whether sent as one frame or fragmented, delivering fragmented messages reassembled, answering Ping with Pong, sending Ping on `ws.ping()`, and completing the close handshake on `ws.close(code, reason)` after which `isOpen()` returns `false`.
records.rationale: Covers D-302, D-304, D-305, D-306, D-307, D-308, D-309, D-310, D-419 (limit mapping part), wave decision Ping (r2 W2-001) and carried loop-D fixes V1-004 and V2-003 (both: the configured message limit goes to both `maxFramePayloadBytes` and `maxMessageBytes`, tested at a non-default limit as one frame and fragmented); tests T20 and T21. Measured: TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` offers `sendText`, `sendBinary`, `ping(byte[] <= 125)`, `close(code, reason)` and `isOpen`; NaruServe adds no frame codec (D-302), so these ACs are end-to-end tests over the TinyHttpd adapter with a raw-socket client that writes frames by hand. Pitfall: passing the limit only to `maxMessageBytes` lets one unfragmented frame above the limit through until reassembly, and only to `maxFramePayloadBytes` lets a fragmented message grow without bound (V1-004). Decision: `ws.ping()` sends an empty-payload Ping through the session's sender slot (FR-WS-007), calling `WebSocketChannel.ping(new byte[0])`, so it never interleaves with a data frame being written. Rejected alternative: a NaruServe-side UTF-8 or size check before TinyHttpd; duplicate logic, reopen only if TinyHttpd lacks a check.

records.title: WebSocketSession semantics: unique ids, per-connection attributes, onClose once, JSON through JsonCodec, onJson failure and listener exceptions

acceptanceCriteria.text: Three sessions opened on one app get ids `0000000000000001`, `0000000000000002` and `0000000000000003`, each matching `[0-9a-f]{16}`, and 1000 sessions opened concurrently from 8 threads get 1000 distinct ids. Decision: the id is 16 lowercase hex digits of an app-wide counter starting at 1. [D-312]

`ws.attribute("user", "kim")` set in the handler is read back as `"kim"` by `ws.attribute("user", String.class)` in a later `onText` listener, `req.attribute("user", String.class)` stays `null`, attributes written under distinct keys from 8 threads concurrently are all readable afterwards without an exception, and after the session closed the session's attribute map is empty, which a test asserts through the internal session (T21). [D-313] Decision: setting an attribute to a null value removes the key, the typed read boxes a primitive class as `Request.attribute` does, and the map is cleared after the `onClose` listeners ran. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-2] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-3]

`onClose` listeners run exactly once per connection with the close code and reason of AC-9: a client close `(1000, "done")` delivers `(1000, "done")` once, and a session closed by the server and then by an abort of the socket still runs each listener once, which a counter asserts. [D-314] Decision: the listeners run only on the first `onClose` call, guarded by one `AtomicBoolean`, on the calling thread in registration order; a `CloseListener` exception is logged at ERROR and the next listener still runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-4]

`ws.sendJson(Collections.singletonMap("a", 1))` sends a text message equal to the app `JsonCodec` encoding of the value, and `ws.onJson(Msg.class, l)` passes `l` the value the app `JsonCodec` decodes from a text message, which a test with a recording stub codec asserts by observing both codec calls. [D-315] Decision: `sendJson` encodes on the calling thread with `codec.encode` into a `StringWriter` and queues the result as a text message; an `IOException` from the codec is rethrown as `HttpException(500, "JSON encoding failed")` with nothing queued, because `UncheckedIOException` needs API 24. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-5] Decision: `onText` and `onJson` entries share one registration-ordered list, and each `onJson` entry decodes with `codec.decode(new StringReader(text), type)` on its own. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-6]

A text message `{bad` delivered to an `onJson(Msg.class, l)` listener does not call `l`, passes the codec's decode exception to every `onError` listener, and leaves `ws.isOpen()` `true`; with no `onError` listener the failure is logged at WARN with the request id. Decision: an `onJson` parse failure is reported through `onError`, not by closing the connection. [D-317] Decision: a listener whose decode throws `IOException` or `RuntimeException` is skipped, the later entries still run, and with no `onError` listener the core logs WARN `websocket <rid> json decode failed`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-7]

An exception thrown by an `onText` listener is passed to the `onError` listeners, logged at ERROR with the request id, and the client receives close `1011`; `onClose` receives `1011` as AC-9 states; no exception propagates to the adapter's endpoint callback, which the in-memory adapter asserts by observing its `onText` call return normally. Decision: user listener exceptions after `101` close the session with `1011`. [wave decision: User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005)] Decision: a throwing text, binary or JSON listener calls `fail(e, "listener")`, skips the remaining listeners of that message and returns normally to the adapter, with the ERROR line `websocket <rid> listener failed`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-8] Decision: an `onError` listener that itself throws is logged at ERROR and ignored, and the next `onError` listener and the `1011` close still run, with no recursion into `fail`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-9]

`sendText`, `sendBinary`, `sendJson` and `ping` called on a closed session return without an exception and send nothing, and `isOpen()` returns `false`. Decision: sends on a closed session are dropped silently. [D-311; D-310] Decision: the call returns before encoding or counting bytes when `isOpen()` is false. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-10]

`close(1005, "")`, `close(1016, "")`, `close(2000, "")`, `close(999, "")` and `close(5000, "")` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, `close(1000, r)` with a reason of 124 UTF-8 bytes throws `IllegalArgumentException`, and `close(1012, "")`, `close(3000, "")` and `close(4999, "x")` are accepted. Decision: the close code must be 1000-1003, 1007-1014 or 3000-4999 (RFC 6455 section 7.4 and the sendable set that TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` also checks on receive), and the reason must fit 123 UTF-8 bytes. [D-310] Decision: `checkClose` runs first, also on a closed session, with the messages `close code must be 1000-1003, 1007-1014 or 3000-4999: <code>` and `close reason over 123 UTF-8 bytes: <n>`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-11]

When the core starts the close with code c and reason r (`ws.close(c, r)`, queue overflow `1008`, idle timeout `1001`, shutdown `1001`, listener exception `1011`), the `onClose` listeners and the FR-APP-019 close line report (c, r) whatever the peer answers, also when the peer never answers and the socket is aborted; a close TinyHttpd starts itself (ping timeout `1001`, protocol failures such as `1002`, `1007`, `1009`) reports the code TinyHttpd delivers; a close started by the client reports the client's code and reason; an end without any close frame from either side reports `1006` with an empty reason. A test asserts each case over the in-memory adapter, the overflow case over TinyHttpd with a client that does not answer the server's close frame, and the client-close case over TinyHttpd. Decision: the server's own close code wins over the `1006` TinyHttpd delivers to `WebSocketListener.onClose` when the peer does not answer. [D-314; D-310; D-321; D-325] Decision: when several closes are started by the core, the first recorded pair is reported to `onClose`, and with no recorded pair the code the adapter delivers. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-12]

An exception, checked or unchecked, thrown by the `ws` handler itself, which runs from the endpoint's `onOpen` after `101` (FR-WS-001 AC-3), is caught by the core endpoint, passed to every `onError` listener the handler registered before the throw, logged at ERROR with the request id, and closes the session with `1011`; `onClose` receives `1011` as AC-9 states; no HTTP error answer is written because the connection is already upgraded, and no exception reaches TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener.onOpen`; an in-memory test and a TinyHttpd test assert that the client receives close `1011` after the `101` and no other HTTP status line, and that an `onError` listener registered before the throw received the exception. Decision: an exception from the `ws` handler is handled like a listener exception after `101`. [wave decision: User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005)] [D-295] Decision: the core calls `fail(e, "handler")` with only the `onError` listeners registered before the throw, logs `websocket <rid> handler failed` and writes no HTTP answer. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-13]

records.requirement: The system shall give each WebSocket session an id unique within its app, a per-connection concurrent attribute map separate from request attributes and released at close, `onClose` listeners run exactly once with the close code and reason, `sendJson` and `onJson` through the app's `JsonCodec`, `onJson` decode failures reported to `onError` with the session left open, and user listener exceptions caught, logged and answered by close `1011`.
records.rationale:
Covers D-312, D-313, D-314, D-315, D-317 (decision part), wave decision User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005, core endpoint part) and the C-07 send/close choices; test T21. Decisions (C-07): session id = 16 lowercase hex digits of an app-wide counter starting at 1; sends on a closed session are dropped without exception, like the `ws` library's send on a closed socket, with `isOpen()` reporting the state; `close(code, reason)` accepts only the codes an endpoint may send per RFC 6455 section 7.4 (1000-1003, 1007-1014 and 3000-4999; 1004-1006, 1015 and the unassigned 1016-2999 are rejected, matching TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` receive check so a NaruServe close is never failed as a protocol error by a strict peer) and rejects a reason over 123 UTF-8 bytes instead of truncating. Decision (close codes on TinyHttpd, AC-9): measured `WebSocket.java:261-405` at 46b973e reports to `WebSocketListener.onClose` the code of the peer's close frame, its own code for a close it starts itself (ping timeout `1001`, protocol failure), and `1006` when the socket ends without a close frame, so a close the core started and the peer never answered would surface as `1006`; the core therefore records the code and reason of every close it starts and reports those to `onClose` and to the FR-APP-019 close line. This decision applies to FR-WS-005 AC-8, FR-WS-007 AC-6, FR-WS-008 AC-4, FR-WS-010 AC-2/AC-7 and FR-APP-019 AC-9. Decision for D-317: an `onJson` parse failure goes to the `onError` listeners and the session stays open; with no `onError` listener it is logged at WARN with the request id. Rejected alternative: closing 1007 on a JSON parse failure; a malformed application message is not a protocol error, reopen if users ask for strict mode. Decision for r2 W2-005: an exception from any user listener is caught, passed to the `onError` listeners, logged at ERROR with the request id, and the session is closed with `1011`; nothing reaches TinyHttpd's callbacks. Pitfall: an `onError` listener that itself throws must not recurse; it is logged and ignored. Rejected alternative: random UUID ids; the counter is cheaper on API 21 and unique per app as D-312 requires.
- [2026-10-20] Handler exceptions (AC-10, r2 W2-005): the `ws` handler runs from the core endpoint's `onOpen` after `101`, and TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener.onOpen` declares no checked exception and answers a RuntimeException with close 1011 plus a rethrow out of `handle`, so the core catches every handler exception itself, reports it to the onError listeners registered so far, logs it at ERROR and closes 1011; no HTTP answer is possible after the upgrade.

records.title: Bounded per-session send queue drained by one app-wide sender executor, whole ordered messages and the 1008 overflow policy

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `sendQueueSize(1000)`, a session whose client does not read accepts queued sends up to 1000 bytes of payload without closing, and the in-memory test observes the queued byte count never exceed 1000; a test with non-ASCII text (`"é"` counts 2 bytes) asserts the count. Decision: queued bytes count the UTF-8 encoded length of a text message's payload and the array length of a binary message's payload; ping and close frames are not counted. [D-318] Decision: `sendJson` counts its encoded text, and the bytes are released when that write returns, so the in-flight message stays counted. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-1] Independently of the payload-byte budget, each session permits at most1024 pending sender tasks including a task in flight and empty text/binary/Ping writes; task-count overflow follows the existing1008 overflow policy. The final close task may replace queued writes so termination is never prevented by the cap.

All sessions of an app share one sender executor whose maximum thread count equals `maxUpgradedConnections` (default 128), which a test reads from the internal executor; its threads are named `naruserve-<port>-ws-sender-<n>`, with `<port>` the app's bound port read when the thread is created, so two apps in one JVM own distinct thread names, which a test with two bound apps asserts; an idle thread ends after the executor's keep-alive time, which a test that sets the internal keep-alive to 200 ms asserts by observing the thread count fall to 0 within 1 s after the last send. Decision: the keep-alive time is 60 s, overridable only through an internal test hook. Decision: sender threads are named `naruserve-<port>-ws-sender-<n>` like the adapter's `naruserve-<port>-worker-<n>`, so thread-count tests attribute them per app. [D-417] Decision: the sender is a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max, max, keep-alive, LinkedBlockingQueue)` with `allowCoreThreadTimeOut(true)` and daemon threads with a 256 KiB requested stack, with `port.getAsInt()` read in `newThread`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-3]

At most one write task of a session runs at a time: a test whose in-memory channel blocks the first `sendText` observes that a second `sendText` on the same session is not started until the first returns, while a `sendText` on another session completes meanwhile. [D-417; D-319]

Eight threads that each send 500 text messages tagged with their thread number and sequence to one session make the client receive all 4000 messages whole, with each thread's messages in its send order and no frame of one message interleaved with another's (T23). [D-319]

Over TinyHttpd, with 20 sessions whose clients stopped reading while the server sent to them until their writes blocked and one healthy session, a `sendText` to the healthy session reaches its client within 1 s (T23); with `writeTimeout(1, SECONDS)`, each stalled session's sender thread is released within 2 s after its write blocked, because TinyHttpd's write timeout aborts the socket. [D-320; D-417]

When a send would make a session's queued bytes exceed `sendQueueSize`, that message is dropped, the queue is emptied, the client receives close `1008` with reason `send queue overflow`, `onClose` receives `(1008, "send queue overflow")` even when the client never answers the close frame (FR-WS-006 AC-9), and the send call returns normally without an exception (T23); a single message larger than `sendQueueSize` overflows on an empty queue and closes the session the same way, which `docs/api/websocket.md` states. Decision: the overflow policy closes the session with `1008` instead of throwing. [D-321]

After a session closed, by client close, overflow or abort, its queue is released, no sender task for it remains, and its attribute map is empty, which a test asserts through the internal session registry after 200 sessions opened and closed (T23). [D-322]

After `HttpExchange.webSocket` returns, the core waits for that session's in-flight sender task to end before the exchange finishes, which a test asserts by blocking a sender task and observing that the exchange's finish is reached only after the task ended; the wait does not run in the TinyHttpd class or in `onClose`. [wave decision: Sender slot release (W2-007)] [wave decision: Sender-slot wait (r2 W2-004)] Decision: the wait is `awaitIdle(session)` without a time bound, run in `WebSocketUpgrade.run` when `ex.webSocket` returns or throws after open, and before `res.upgraded()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-7]

records.requirement: The system shall queue every WebSocket send in a per-session outbound queue bounded by `sendQueueSize` and drain the queues with one app-wide sender executor whose thread limit equals `maxUpgradedConnections`, running at most one write task per session at a time so that messages go out whole in queue-entry order and a stalled session never delays another session, closing a session whose queue would overflow with `1008`, and leaving no queue, thread or attribute of a closed session behind.
records.rationale: Covers D-318, D-417, D-319, D-320, D-321 (decision), D-322, wave decisions Sender slot release (W2-007) and Sender-slot wait (r2 W2-004, which moves the W2-007 wait into the core after `HttpExchange.webSocket` returns and before the exchange finishes, behaviour unchanged); test T23. Reason: TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` send is synchronous, so a direct send from a broadcaster would block on a slow peer. Measured: `ServerOptions.java:41-54` already defines `maxUpgradedConnections` (default 128, FR-ENGINE-004); TinyHttpd's write timeout defaults to 30 s. Decision for D-321 (C-07): when queuing a message would make the session's queued bytes exceed `sendQueueSize`, the message is dropped, the queue is discarded, close `1008` with reason `send queue overflow` is handed to the sender slot as the last task, `onClose` receives `1008`, and the overflowing send returns normally. Rejected alternative: throwing from `send` on overflow; it forces every broadcaster to catch per peer, reopen if users need synchronous backpressure. Pitfall: a fixed pool of 16 threads would let 16 stalled peers block every other session (D-320 asks for at least 20 stalled sessions in the test). Pitfall: reusing a sender thread for another session's task while one write is in flight would interleave frames (D-319). Thread total and stack figures belong to PERF-APP-001 in the APP scope.

records.title: Ping interval, pong timeout, idle timeout scheduler and the handshake bound on TinyHttpd

acceptanceCriteria.text: The TinyHttpd `WebSocketHandler` receives `pingInterval` equal to the configured ping interval in milliseconds (default 30000), which a test with `pingInterval(2, SECONDS)` asserts as 2000, and NaruServe starts no thread or timer for pings. [D-423; D-323]

Over TinyHttpd with `pingInterval(1, SECONDS)`, a client that completes the handshake and then sends nothing and answers no Ping receives at least one Ping and then a close `1001` within 3 s (two ping intervals plus 1 s) of its last frame, and `onClose` receives `1001`, the code TinyHttpd delivers for its own ping-timeout close (FR-WS-006 AC-9) (T21). [D-424; D-423]

Reflection finds no pong-timeout setting, and `docs/api/websocket.md` and `docs/api/defaults.md` state that the pong timeout equals the ping interval; `docs/api/websocket.md` also states that a separate pong timeout is not available because TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener` has no Pong callback and that this is a deferred TinyHttpd limitation, which a docs test finds by a fixed phrase. Decision: the pong timeout is fixed to the ping interval in v1. [D-424] Decision: reflection finds no method of `WebSocketOptions` or `ServerOptions` whose name contains `pong` or `handshake`, ignoring case. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-9]

With `idleTimeout(1, SECONDS)` and `pingInterval(30, SECONDS)`, a session whose client sends a Ping frame every 300 ms but no text or binary message is handed close `1001` by the scheduler within 2 s of its last text or binary message, the client receives a Pong for each Ping until then, then stops pinging and answers the server's close frame, and `onClose` receives `1001` as FR-WS-006 AC-9 states (T21). [D-425; D-323] Decision: the idle check compares `nanoTime - lastActivityNanos >= idleTimeout`, then calls `closeBy(1001, "idle timeout")` and schedules one abort check 1000 ms later. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-11]

All idle checks of one app run on one thread named `naruserve-<port>-ws-idle`, with `<port>` the app's bound port read when the thread is created, which never calls a `WebSocketChannel` write method itself: a test with a session whose in-memory channel blocks `close` observes the scheduler run the idle check of another idle session within 500 ms and call `abort()` on the blocked session 1 s (plus 700 ms of scheduling slack) after it handed over the close task. Decision: the idle scheduler thread is named `naruserve-<port>-ws-idle`, so thread-count tests attribute it per app. Decision (timing bounds): the 500 ms and 700 ms slack replace 100 ms and 200 ms because macOS timer coalescing was measured to delay every timed wait by about 150 ms (up to 200 ms), while a scheduler thread held by the blocked close would still delay the other check by about 1 s, so the bound still tells the two apart. [D-425]

A text message received or sent resets the session's idle clock: with `idleTimeout(1, SECONDS)`, a session that receives one text message every 500 ms for 3 s stays open. [D-425] Decision: `touch()` runs when `onText` or `onBinary` runs and when a text or binary write returns; pings, pongs and close frames do not touch. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-10]

On TinyHttpd, a client that sends `GET /ws HTTP/1.1` and then stalls before the end of the request headers is disconnected within `headerTimeout` plus 1 s, which a test with `headerTimeout(1, SECONDS)` asserts, and reflection finds no handshake-timeout setter on `WebSocketOptions` or `ServerOptions`; `docs/api/websocket.md` and `docs/api/defaults.md` state that the handshake is bounded only by `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout` and that a dedicated upgrade deadline is a deferred TinyHttpd limitation, which a docs test finds by a fixed phrase. Deviation (recorded): D-323's handshake timeout is met on TinyHttpd only by `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout`. [D-323; residual: WebSocket handshake timeout (r5 W2-002)]

records.requirement: The system shall pass the WebSocket ping interval to TinyHttpd's `WebSocketHandler.pingInterval` so that a silent peer is closed with `1001` after two intervals, fix the pong timeout to the ping interval, enforce the idle timeout with one NaruServe scheduler thread that hands close `1001` to an idle session's sender slot and aborts the session's socket 1 s later when that close task has not returned, and bound the handshake on TinyHttpd by the server-wide `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout`.
records.rationale:
Covers D-323, D-423, D-424, D-425 and residual WebSocket handshake timeout (r5 W2-002); test T21. Measured: TinyHttpd's read loop sends a Ping after one interval without an inbound frame and closes with 1001 after a second such interval, treats any inbound frame as the answer, and its `WebSocketListener` has no Pong callback, so NaruServe runs no ping scheduler (D-423) and cannot measure a separate pong timeout (D-424). TinyHttpd counts Ping and Pong as activity, so a peer that answers pings never idles out there; the idle timeout counts only text and binary messages received or sent (D-425). TinyHttpd at 46b973e has no upgrade-specific deadline; `ServerOptions.headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout` (`ServerOptions.java:29,32`, mapped in the adapter core under D-210) bound the handshake. Deviation (recorded): D-323 asks for a configurable handshake timeout; on TinyHttpd it is satisfied only through these existing server-wide timeouts, and no separate setting is added because it would have no effect. Deferred D-020 TinyHttpd-gap issues (opened by the orchestrator in the run's issue ledger at triage, not patched in TinyHttpd by wave 7): (1) the missing Pong callback of `WebSocketListener`, which blocks a separate pong timeout (D-424); (2) a dedicated upgrade (handshake) deadline (r5 W2-002). AC-3 and AC-7 check the user-facing statement of both gaps in `docs/api/`. Pitfall: a scheduler thread that writes the close frame itself would block on a stalled peer and delay every other session's idle check; it only enqueues and aborts. Rejected alternative: one timer per session; it multiplies threads on API 21. Defaults (30 s ping, 5 min idle) are settled in IR-WS-001.
- [2026-10-20] AC-4 has the client answer the server's close frame. A peer that never answers the close and keeps sending frames keeps the session open: TinyHttpd's closing read timeout restarts on every inbound frame, so such a peer is ended only by its own close, the shutdown abort or `writeTimeout`. This is a TinyHttpd gap under D-020, deferred and not patched by wave 7.

records.title: WebSocket connection limit and session registration: 503 beyond maxUpgradedConnections, reservation before the upgrade, refusal after the closed flag and after STOPPING

acceptanceCriteria.text: Over TinyHttpd with `maxUpgradedConnections(2)`, two open WebSocket sessions are accepted and a third upgrade receives `503` with a `Retry-After` header and the standard error body, without `101` and without running the `ws` handler. [D-324; D-444]

The core reserves a session in the WebSocket session registry, under the registry lock, before it calls `HttpExchange.webSocket`, which an in-memory adapter test asserts by reading the registry size inside its `webSocket` call before `onOpen`. [wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)]

When the registry's closed flag is already set, an upgrade request that reaches the upgrade extension point receives `503` with `Connection: close` before any `101`, `HttpExchange.webSocket` is not called and no session is registered. [D-445; wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)]

A handshake refused before `101` (for example `426` from the adapter) removes its reservation, and an upgrade refused with `403` by the Origin check of FR-WS-003 or by any other core check before `HttpExchange.webSocket` leaves no reservation, so the registry size returns to its previous value, which a test asserts after 10 refused handshakes of each kind. [wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)]

A reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the closed flag was set gets its channel, hands close `1001` to its sender slot as its only task and does not run the `ws` handler, which an in-memory test asserts by setting the flag between the reservation and `onOpen`. [wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)] [D-445] Decision: the close task is `closeBy(1001, "server shutdown")`, and the idle watch is skipped as well as the handler. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-5]

An upgrade request that reaches the dispatcher after `STOPPING` began receives `503` with `Connection: close` from the stopping gate of FR-APP-013 and is not upgraded: `HttpExchange.webSocket` is never called. [D-301]

records.requirement: The system shall count WebSocket upgrades against `maxUpgradedConnections` and answer an upgrade beyond it with `503`, reserve each session in the WebSocket session registry under its lock before calling `HttpExchange.webSocket`, refuse the reservation with `503` and `Connection: close` once the registry's closed flag is set, remove the reservation when the handshake is refused, send close `1001` without running the handler for a reserved session whose `onOpen` comes after the flag, and reject upgrade requests arriving after `STOPPING` began without upgrading.
records.rationale: Covers D-301, D-324, D-445 (WebSocket part: closed flag before snapshot, upgrade answered `503` + `Connection: close` before any `101`) and wave decision Session registration (r2 W2-003). Measured: `ServerOptions.java:41-54` defines `maxUpgradedConnections` (default 128, range up to 65536) and `TinyHttpdAdapter.java:105-116` maps it onto TinyHttpd's `maxUpgradedConnections` (wave 5, FR-ENGINE-004), so TinyHttpd answers `503` + `Retry-After` beyond the limit and FR-WS-002 maps that rejection. D-301 is satisfied by FR-APP-013's stopping gate (requests reaching the dispatcher during `STOPPING` get `503` + `Connection: close`). The closing participant that sets the flag and takes the snapshot is FR-WS-010; the shared coordination across WebSocket and SSE belongs to FR-APP-020 in the APP scope. Pitfall: registering only in `onOpen` would let a session open between the closing participant's snapshot and the flag and escape the 1001 close; the reservation before `webSocket` closes that window. Rejected alternative: a NaruServe-side counter in addition to TinyHttpd's; two counters drift, reopen if a non-TinyHttpd adapter lacks a limit.

records.title: Shutdown of WebSocket sessions: before-wait participant closes with 1001, bounded close wait and abort through UpgradedConnection

acceptanceCriteria.text: The WebSocket closing participant is registered in the before-wait phase of the shutdown participants of FR-APP-011 and, when run, first sets the registry's closed flag under the registry lock and then takes its snapshot, so a session reserved before the flag is in the snapshot and an upgrade after it is refused as FR-WS-009 states. [D-435; D-445] Decision: the closing participant is registered in `BEFORE_WAIT` and the terminate step in `FORCE_CLOSE`, once per app. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-13]

During shutdown, an open healthy session's client receives close `1001` and its `onClose` listeners run once with `1001`, the server's own code as FR-WS-006 AC-9 states, also when the client does not answer the close frame (T21, T44). [D-340; D-435]

When the participant runs, no message queued before it is sent: a session with 50 queued messages behind a blocked write receives none of them after the participant started, and a `sendText` called after the participant started sends nothing and returns normally. [D-435] Decision: the close is `closeBy(1001, "server shutdown")` on every opened session, whose `last()` discards the queue and refuses later sends. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-7]

With two sessions whose clients stopped reading while the server sent to them until their writes blocked, the participant returns within 1 s plus 200 ms of scheduling slack, and both sessions' client sockets reach end of stream or reset by then, because the participant aborted them through `UpgradedConnection.close()` (T44). [D-435; D-343] Decision: when the close wait ends, the registry state is set to ENDED under the lock first, then `abort()` is called on each snapshot session with a channel whose slot is not idle. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-9]

When the participant receives a deadline that leaves 300 ms, its close wait ends after at most 300 ms plus 200 ms of scheduling slack before it aborts the unreturned sessions, which a test with a shutdown timeout of 300 ms and one stalled session asserts. [residual: Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003)] [D-435] Decision: the close wait ends at `min(now + 1000 ms, deadlineNanos)`, and earlier only when every snapshot session is removed or opened with `awaitIdleUntil` true. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-8]

A reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the closed flag but before the close wait ended hands close `1001` to its sender slot as its only task, and the participant waits for that task within the same close wait and aborts the connection only if it has not returned by then. [wave decision: Reserved session at shutdown (r3 W2-003)]

A reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the close wait ended is aborted within 100 ms of its `onOpen` through its `UpgradedConnection` with no close frame sent, its `ws` handler never runs, and its FR-APP-019 close line reports `1006` (no close frame from either side, FR-WS-006 AC-9). Deviation (recorded): D-340 requires close `1001` for every open session at shutdown; this late-opening session is aborted without a close frame so TinyHttpd's stop callback never waits on a blocked close write. [D-340; wave decision: Session opening after the close wait (r4 W2-002)]

After `shutdown` returns, the sender executor and the idle scheduler thread of that app have terminated and the session registry is empty, which a test asserts by listing live threads whose names start with `naruserve-<port>-ws-` for that app's bound port (the names of FR-WS-007 AC-2 and FR-WS-008 AC-5), so another app's threads in the same JVM are not counted (T44). [D-343; D-435] Decision: terminate calls `shutdownNow(500)` on the sender and the idle scheduler and then clears the registry. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-12]

records.requirement: The system shall register a before-wait shutdown participant that sets the WebSocket registry's closed flag, snapshots every reserved and open session, stops the sender executor from taking new messages, discards every session's queued messages, hands close `1001` to each session's sender slot as its last task, waits until every close task returned or until the earlier of 1 s and the time left to the shutdown deadline, and then aborts through `UpgradedConnection.close()` the socket of every session whose close task has not returned.
records.rationale:
Covers D-340, D-343 (WebSocket part), D-435, wave decisions Reserved session at shutdown (r3 W2-003, which replaces the round-2 "abort as soon as its channel is set"), Session opening after the close wait (r4 W2-002) and residual Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003, WebSocket use of the deadline; the add-only `ShutdownParticipants` overload itself is FR-APP-020 in the APP scope); tests T21 and T44. Measured: `internal/ShutdownParticipants.java:10-50` has a `Phase` enum and `add(Phase, Runnable)` without a deadline; `internal/DefaultRestApp.java:114-127,539-636` holds the shutdown deadline and `runShutdownSequence` (FR-APP-011). The bound rests on the abort alone with no write tracking: closing the socket makes a blocked write throw, including TinyHttpd's read-loop Ping/Pong writes and a close frame blocked on a full receive window, which share one write lock, so TinyHttpd's later stop callback `close(1001)` finds `closeSent` set or the socket closed and returns at once. Deviation (recorded): D-340 says shutdown closes every open session with 1001; a reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the close wait ended is aborted at once with no close frame (r4 W2-002), which `docs/api/websocket.md` records, so TinyHttpd's stop callback never waits on a blocked close write and D-344's bound holds. Pitfall: waiting the full TinyHttpd write timeout (30 s) on a stalled peer would break the D-344 bound. Rejected alternative: tracking per-write ages to decide what to abort; the abort-all-unreturned rule is simpler and bounded. records.title: AuthApiKeys app facade issue, list and revoke

acceptanceCriteria.text: `issue(botId, "ci-bot", null, "posts:read")` returns an `IssuedApiKey` whose `getPlainKey()` is the plaintext key and whose stored key has `issuedByUserId` null and `expiresAt` null.
`issue` with an unknown owner, a disabled owner, scopes violating R46, or `expiresAt` equal to or less than `TimeSource.nowMillis()` throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
`issue` when the owner already has 20 live keys throws `AuthRejection` with status 409 and code `api_key_limit`.
`list("u-404")` for an unknown owner throws `IllegalArgumentException`; `list(owner)` returns `ApiKey` values with a status and no secret hash.
`revoke("k-404")` returns false without an exception; `revoke` of an existing key returns true and deletes it.
Any facade call without `.apiKeys(store)` throws `AuthStateException`.
`auth.errors()` renders `AuthRejection(409, "api_key_limit")` thrown from an app route as a 409 JSON body with `code` `api_key_limit`.

With `.allowAdminScopesOnApiKeys(true)`, `issue(adminId, "n", null, "auth-users:write")` called from an app route whose request principal holds only `posts:read` succeeds (the facade runs no R31 or key-actor check), and the `AuthApiKeys` Javadoc states that the facade performs no actor checks and that apps building delegated-admin screens must check the actor themselves (docs test).

`issue(Request req, String ownerUserId, String name, @Nullable Long expiresAt, String... scopes)` and `revoke(Request req, String keyId)` behave like the forms without a request and also run no actor check; their audit event names the request's user as actor, carries `req.requestId()`, the client address and, for a request authenticated by an API key, that key's `apiKeyId`; `issue(req, ...)` records the request's user as the stored key's `issuedByUserId` and as the event's `issuedByUserId`; an anonymous request gives no actor and no issuer. Both forms compile and run from a Kotlin trailing-lambda route. Decision (2026-11-09): overloads that take the request, because the facade cannot see the request otherwise and a thread-local would break async handlers.

records.title: ApiKeyStore SPI method contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: A reflection test lists the `ApiKeyStore` methods and finds exactly the 13 table entries; the defaults are `deleteFutureByOwner`, the lastUsedAt update, `supportsAtomicLimitInsert` and `countKeysWithAdminScopes`.

`insertIfUnderLimit` counts as live only keys that are unexpired at `nowMillis` and whose ownerVer is greater than or equal to the inserted key's ownerVer; with 19 such keys and limit 20 it inserts and returns true, with 20 it returns false.
The default `deleteFutureByOwner(u, 5)` on a store holding u's keys with ownerVer 4, 5 and 6 deletes only the ownerVer 6 key via `listByOwner` and `deleteById` and returns 1.
A minimal store implementing only the abstract methods reports `supportsAtomicLimitInsert()` false and `countKeysWithAdminScopes()` -1, and its lastUsedAt update does nothing.
`countKeysWithAdminScopes()` on a store that implements it counts keys naming an `auth-` resource scope (dead keys included) and does not count keys whose only scope is `*`.

On a protected request, a store exception from a call the response depends on (`findByPrefix`, `findById`, `listByOwner`, `insertIfUnderLimit`, `deleteByIdAndOwner`, `deleteById` on the admin DELETE endpoint, `deleteAllByOwner` during user deletion, and `deleteFutureByOwner` before an issuance, pending-marker re-delete included) is wrapped by auth into 503 JSON `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; an exception from the lastUsedAt update or from a deletion run off the request path (scheduled `deleteStaleByOwner`, invariant-violation `deleteById`, scheduled re-delete, `deleteExpired`) leaves the response unchanged (PERF-APIKEY-001 AC-3); a `deleteFutureByOwner` exception before an auth-triggered `ver++` does not answer 503 and follows REL-APIKEY-003 AC-3 (ERROR log, `ver++` proceeds, pending marker).
Kotlin sees `findByPrefix`/`findById` as nullable and all other returns as non-null (Kotlin nullability test).

records.title: Explicit entry point RestApp.builder() and the JsonCodec SPI

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(a).jsonCodec(c).build()` returns a `RestApp` whose `state()` is `NEW` and whose class is the internal `DefaultRestApp`; two `build()` calls on one builder return two distinct apps. [D-111; wave-4 carried: public entry point constructs DefaultRestApp] Decision: the entry point is `RestApp.builder()` returning `RestApp.Builder`, a public final nested class whose setters return the builder. Decision: two `build()` calls on one builder share the configured adapter, codec and logger. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-1]

`build()` without `httpAdapter(...)` and `build()` without `jsonCodec(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the missing setter, and `httpAdapter(null)`, `jsonCodec(null)` and `logger(null)` each throw `NullPointerException`. [D-111; D-137] Decision: the adapter is checked first, so a builder missing both names `httpAdapter(...)`, and a `null` setter argument throws at the setter, not at `build()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-2]

An app built without `logger(...)` has `app.logger()` returning an instance of the public console logger `com.snoworca.naruserve.ConsoleLogger` of IR-APP-006, and an app built with `logger(l)` has `app.logger()` returning `l`. [D-169; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: each `build()` without `logger(...)` creates its own new `ConsoleLogger`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-3]

Reflection on `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.JsonCodec` finds exactly the two abstract methods `<T> T decode(java.io.Reader, java.lang.reflect.Type) throws java.io.IOException` and `void encode(java.lang.Object, java.io.Writer) throws java.io.IOException`, and no parameter, return or exception type of the interface lies in a `com.google.gson` package. [D-182; D-112]

`JsonCodec` and `RestApp.Builder` carry nullability annotations on every public parameter and return value, and a Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(adapter).jsonCodec(codec).build()` with a Kotlin object implementing `JsonCodec`. [D-111; D-182; C-03] Decision: package `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` is `@NullMarked` and the `value` parameter of `JsonCodec#encode` is `@Nullable`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Middleware and Next interfaces and the middleware registration methods

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `Middleware` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Request, Response, Next) throws Exception`, and `Next` with exactly the abstract methods `void run()` and `void error(Throwable)`; a Java lambda `(req, res, next) -> next.run()` compiles as a `Middleware`. [D-115; D-116]

`RestApp` declares `use(Middleware)`, `use(String, Middleware)`, the seven overloads `get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options(String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(Method, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(MethodSet, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)`, each returning `RestApp`, and every wave 3 `RestApp` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-005 AC-5 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed to the wave 4 method set: the wave 3 methods plus those of IR-APP-002, IR-APP-003, IR-APP-005, IR-APP-006 and IR-APP-007, with `create()` and `builder()` as the only static methods. [D-119; I-014; D-137] Decision: the route-middleware overloads return `RestApp` like the plain registration methods. Amended by FR-DX-012 (target start-api): the static methods of `RestApp` are `builder()`, `create()` and `start(int, Configurer)`.

`RouteBuilder` declares `use(Middleware)` returning `RouteBuilder`; middleware added through it applies as route middleware to every method the same builder registers after the `use` call, in `use` call order, so `app.route("/a").use(m1).use(m2).get(h)` runs `m1`, `m2`, then `h` for `GET /a`. [D-137; D-120] Decision: `RouteBuilder.use(middleware)` is adopted and is the way to attach several route middleware; no varargs or multi-middleware overload is added to `RestApp`.

`use(null)`, `use("/api", null)`, `use(null, mw)` and every route-middleware overload with a `null` middleware or handler throw `NullPointerException`, and `use(prefix, mw)` with a prefix that does not start with `/` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-118; D-119] Decision: each refused call throws before anything is recorded. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-7] User-approved revision: FR-DX-008 overrides scope regrouping: global and matching prefix middleware execute in their combined registration order, then route middleware.

No public type of `NaruServe-api` declares a method that resumes a middleware chain from another thread or returns a future, and `Next` has no method other than `run()` and `error(Throwable)`. [D-128]

A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `app.use { req, res, next -> next.run() }`, `app.use("/api") { req, res, next -> next.run() }` and `app.get("/x", mw) { req, res -> res.send("x") }` without a DSL. [D-115; C-03]

records.title: onError, ErrorHandler and the framework HTTP error types

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `ErrorHandler` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Throwable, Request, Response) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onError(ErrorHandler)` returning `RestApp`; `app.onError((error, req, res) -> res.status(500).send("x"))` compiles in Java and `app.onError { error, req, res -> }` in a Kotlin test. [D-129; D-137] Decision: the callback interface is `ErrorHandler` and it may throw `Exception`.

`HttpException` extends `RuntimeException`, has public constructors `(int status)`, `(int status, String message)` and `(int status, String message, Throwable cause)`, and `status()` returns the given status; a status outside `400..599` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-130; D-134] Decision: framework errors expose their status through `HttpException#status()`. Decision: the `IllegalArgumentException` message names the refused status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-9]
`HttpException#code()` returns the `code` value of FR-APP-006 for its status (for example `BAD_REQUEST` for `400`, `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` for `422`). [D-130; D-137]
`new UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` and `new UnsupportedMediaTypeException("m")` are `HttpException`s with `status()` `415` and `code()` `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`. [D-134; wave decision: 415]
`onError(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, and `onError` is a registration method under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002. [D-114; D-129]

records.title: ServiceRegistry, ApplicationContext and the request service accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `ServiceRegistry` exactly `register(Class, Object)`, `registerExternal(Class, Object)`, `get(Class)`, `getOrNull(Class)` and `contains(Class)` with the generic signatures of the requirement, and on `ApplicationContext` (a subinterface of `ServiceRegistry`) `attribute(String, Object)`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `own(AutoCloseable)` and `logger()`. [D-138; D-151] Decision: an externally owned object is registered with `registerExternal(Class<T>, T)`, which the framework never closes.

`get(type)` for a type that is not registered throws `ServiceNotFoundException` (a `RuntimeException`) whose message names the type, and `getOrNull(type)` returns `null` and `contains(type)` returns `false` for it. [D-138] Decision: the `ServiceNotFoundException` message contains the binary name of the type. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-1]

`Request` declares `ApplicationContext application()` and `<T> T service(Class<T> type)`, and every wave 3 `Request` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-001 AC-3 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed so that `service` and `application` are expected on `Request` from wave 4. [D-142; I-014]

`register`, `registerExternal` and `own` with a `null` argument, `get`, `getOrNull` and `contains` with a `null` type, and `attribute` with a `null` key throw `NullPointerException`; the value parameter of `attribute(String, Object)` is `@Nullable` and storing a typed `null` variable (`Object v = null; ctx.attribute(key, v)`) removes the key, because a literal `null` resolves to the read overload; `attributeAs(key, type)` throws `ClassCastException` when the stored value is not an instance of `type`, as the request attribute store of FR-HTTP-012 does. [D-138; D-144]

The new types carry nullability annotations on public signatures (`getOrNull` and `attribute(String, Class)` `@Nullable`, `get` and `service` `@NonNull`), and a Kotlin test compiles `ctx.register(UserService::class.java, s)` and `req.service(UserService::class.java)` with a non-null result type. [D-138; C-03] Decision: of these signatures only the returns of `getOrNull` and `attribute(String, Class)` are `@Nullable`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Lifecycle API: AppState, onStart/onStop, listen, ServerHandle and shutdown

acceptanceCriteria.text: `AppState.values()` is exactly `NEW, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, FAILED, TERMINATED` in that order, and `app.state()` of a newly built app is `NEW`. [D-152]

Reflection finds `LifecycleCallback` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(ApplicationContext) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onStart(LifecycleCallback)` and `RestApp.onStop(LifecycleCallback)` returning `RestApp`; `onStart(null)` and `onStop(null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-137] Decision: `onStart` and `onStop` share the callback interface `LifecycleCallback`, which may throw `Exception`.

`ServerHandle` declares exactly `int port()`, `String address()`, `AppState state()`, `String url()` and `void shutdown(long, TimeUnit)`; after `listen(0)` succeeded `port()` returns the adapter's `boundPort()`, `address()` returns `127.0.0.1` and `state()` returns the app's current state, so it reads `TERMINATED` after shutdown. [D-155] Decision: the accessors are `port()`, `address()` and `state()`, and `listen` binds to `127.0.0.1`. Amended by FR-DX-013 (target start-api): the original set was exactly `port()`, `address()` and `state()`; `url()` and `shutdown(long, TimeUnit)` are added and specified there.

`listen(port)` with a port outside `0..65535` throws `IllegalArgumentException` and leaves the state `NEW`; `shutdown(timeout, unit)` with a negative timeout throws `IllegalArgumentException` and with a `null` unit `NullPointerException`. [D-153; D-161] Decision: the argument checks of `listen` and `shutdown` run before any state change. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-6]

`AppStartException` extends `RuntimeException`; it is the type `listen()` throws for a checked start-failure cause (as its cause) and for a start ended by a pending stop. [D-159; D-426] Decision: the unchecked wrapper type is `AppStartException`. Decision: `AppStartException` has a public `(String message, Throwable cause)` constructor. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-7]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.onStart { ctx -> ctx.attribute("k", 1) }`, `val h = app.listen(0)`, `h.port()`, `app.state()` and `app.shutdown(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`. [D-152; D-155; C-03]

records.title: Logger SPI, LogLevel, the console logger and app.logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `Logger` exactly the six abstract methods `trace(String)`, `debug(String)`, `info(String)`, `warn(String)`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)`, and `LogLevel.values()` is `TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR`. [D-168; wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`new ConsoleLogger()` writes `info`, `warn` and `error` records and drops `trace` and `debug`; `new ConsoleLogger(LogLevel.TRACE)` writes all five levels. Each record is one line `<timestamp> <LEVEL> <message>` where the timestamp is formatted with `SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ")` (offset like `+0900`; no `java.time`, no `X` pattern, both absent from Android API 21), checked by a test under two time zones, `TRACE`/`DEBUG`/`INFO` go to `System.out` and `WARN`/`ERROR` to `System.err`, and `error(m, t)` writes the stack trace of `t` after the line. [D-169; D-181] Decision: the console logger defaults to threshold `INFO` and uses this line format. Decision: the console logger reads `System.out` and `System.err` at write time, so a stream replaced through `System.setOut` or `System.setErr` receives later records. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-9]
`ConsoleLogger#close()` and `flush()` flush both streams and leave `System.out` and `System.err` open, so a later `System.out.println` still prints. [wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`app.logger(l)` makes `app.logger()` return `l`, `app.logger()` before any call returns the builder's logger (the console logger by default), and `app.logger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; `logger(l)` is under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 while `logger()` is readable in every state. [D-170; D-114]
`ConsoleLogger` is in `NaruServe-api` and references no SLF4J or `android.*` type. [D-169; D-178]

records.title: Public surface of the registration list app.registrations() and the watcher app.onRegistration(RegistrationListener)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `registrations()` (name not final) returning a `java.util.List` of registration records in registration order; calling `add` on the returned list throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, and `registrations()` throws no `IllegalStateException` in `NEW` or after `listen` (it is a read accessor, not a configuration method). Iterating a list returned by `registrations()` never throws `ConcurrentModificationException` while another thread registers after `listen` (decide during implementation whether the result is a call-time snapshot or a concurrency-safe view, and document it in `docs/api/app.md`); a test iterates the list on one thread while another thread adds 1,000 routes.

`RestApp` declares `RestApp onRegistration(RegistrationListener listener)` (names not final); `onRegistration(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, a call outside `NEW` throws `IllegalStateException` through `AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable`, and the reflection test of CON-APP-002 AC-1 lists `onRegistration` and finds it rejected in `RUNNING` with nothing recorded.

`RegistrationListener` (name not final) is a public interface in `com.snoworca.naruserve` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with exactly one abstract method that receives one registration record, and it is not a `java.util.function` type (CON-HTTP-002).

The registration record type (name not final) exposes `getKind()`, `getMethod()`, `getPath()` and `getTarget()`, and the accessors FR-APP-026 AC-4 and AC-5 require (names not final): the enclosing `ROUTER_MOUNT` record (`@Nullable`, null for app-level records) and the original path object or a non-string-path flag; `getKind()` is non-null through the `com.snoworca.naruserve` package's `@NullMarked` default (unannotated: no `@Nullable` and no `@NonNull`, FR-KT-001 AC-3) and returns an enum (name not final) whose constants are exactly `ROUTE`, `WEBSOCKET`, `STATIC`, `ROUTER_MOUNT`, `GROUP`, `CORS`, `MIDDLEWARE`, `PATH_MIDDLEWARE`, `ERROR_MIDDLEWARE` and `PARAM`; every return position that can be null is annotated `@Nullable`, no `@NonNull` appears on the new types and accessors, and the nullability reflection test of FR-KT-001 passes over them.

A Kotlin source test compiles and runs `app.onRegistration { r -> kinds.add(r.kind) }` without a DSL, registers `app.get("/x") { _, res -> res.send("ok") }`, and reads `app.registrations()` with property syntax (`r.kind`, `r.path`, `r.target`), seeing a `ROUTE` record for `/x` both in the watcher and in the list; no platform type is needed to compile the assignments (CLAUDE.md T11).

`docs/api/app.md` and `docs/api/en/app.md` each document `registrations()` and `onRegistration` with an Express comparison, the kind table, the record accessors including the enclosing `ROUTER_MOUNT` record and the non-string-path accessor of AC-4, the order validate → watcher → apply → record, and one Java and one Kotlin example that compile under CON-HTTP-009; a name settled during implementation loses its (미확정) marker in the same change (CON-APP-009).

`CallbackMatrix.CALLBACK_TYPES` and the Kotlin callback matrix include `RegistrationListener` (name not final), so the exact-equality inventory test `CallbackInventoryTest` of FR-KT-003 AC-4 stays green with the new public `@FunctionalInterface`.

records.rationale: 00 §8 C4 (required Core change, §9 roadmap row "선행 (Core)"), editions 10–13. utils.auth uses Core public API only (00 §2, §8), and R28 (install order, post-start registration check), R30 (doctor check of the auth error-layer object after the last ROUTE, request-time re-check) and R40 consume this list and watcher. Today DefaultRestApp keeps only partial private lists (route+ws `registrations`, `middlewareRegistrations`, `errorHandlers`), so no public reader can see the shared registration order of FR-APP-021.
records.research:
- Decisive facts: the record shape `{kind, method, path, target}` and the ten kinds come from 00 §8 (C4 kind table). `target` is the registered object reference (12th edition) so doctor can tell `auth.errors()`/`auth.errorMiddleware()` from an app handler (R30 12th edition; the 11th edition looked only at the kind and could not).
- Decision: `onRegistration` is a configuration method under the NEW guard, because `auth.install(app)` runs in NEW before route-family registrations (R28) and CON-APP-002 requires every `RestApp`-returning method to be guarded. `registrations()` is a read accessor like `logger()`/`state()` and stays unguarded so request-time checks (R30 14th edition) can read it while running.
- Rejected alternative: an unguarded `onRegistration` callable after start. A late watcher misses earlier post-start registrations and breaks the CON-APP-002 reflection rule. Reopen if a module must attach a watcher after start.
- Decision: record accessors use `getX` naming (IR-KT-001) because the record is a value object; the `req`/`res`/`app` short-name rule does not apply to it.
- Pitfall: the watcher type must be a NaruServe `@FunctionalInterface`, not `java.util.function.Consumer` (CON-HTTP-002), or Kotlin `app.onRegistration { r -> }` still compiles but the public API rule fails.
- Names `registrations`, `onRegistration`, `RegistrationListener`, the record type and the kind enum type are proposals (00 §8 "이름은 제안", §7 table row). Settle during implementation per CLAUDE.md and remove the (미확정) marker.
- 0.11.0 auth always installs the watcher, independent of `protectOnly` (R28 13th edition, R30 14th edition), so the watcher must be cheap when it does nothing.

records.title: App option app.rawBodyLimit(bytes) for the raw request body

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `RestApp rawBodyLimit(long bytes)`, which returns the receiver.

On an app that never calls `rawBodyLimit`, `req.bodyStream()` reads a 1048576-byte body without `Content-Length` to its end and throws `BodyTooLargeException` with `limit()` 1048576 on the read that would return byte 1048577.
`rawBodyLimit(0)`, `rawBodyLimit(-1)` and `rawBodyLimit(1073741825)` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, while `rawBodyLimit(1)` and `rawBodyLimit(1073741824)` are accepted.

`rawBodyLimit` calls `AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable` before it records anything: a call outside `NEW` throws `IllegalStateException` and changes nothing, and the reflection test of FR-APP-002 AC-4 and CON-APP-002 AC-1 (`AppLifecycleGuardTest`) lists `rawBodyLimit` and finds it rejected in `RUNNING`.

records.title: AuthRejection value type and the auth status and error code catalog

acceptanceCriteria.text: new AuthRejection(500, "x", null) and new AuthRejection(422, "Bad-Code", null) both throw IllegalArgumentException; new AuthRejection(422, "domain_not_allowed") is valid and has message null and getRetryAfterSeconds() null.
A rejection with null message is rendered with a non-empty default message; one with retryAfterSeconds 30 renders header Retry-After: 30.

The auth-owned codes that 00 names are exactly: unauthenticated 401, invalid_token 401, invalid_api_key 401, invalid_request 400, insufficient_scope 403, api_key_not_allowed 403, insecure_transport 403, csrf_failed 403, api_key_limit 409, too_many_attempts 429, service_account_no_password 400, username_mismatch 400, security_write_conflict 503, plus the flow-owned codes invalid_credentials 401 (FR-FLOW-004 AC-2) [INFERRED:med:advisory] and invalid_refresh_token 401 (FR-FLOW-005 AC-4) [INFERRED:med:advisory], and the wrong-current-password 401 code shared by SEC-FLOW-014 AC-2 and FR-APIKEY-003/004 (name not final; 00 R47 (10) leaves it open). The answers whose code 00 leaves open were decided on 2026-11-02 (open questions Q14, Q15, Q23, Q54, Q55, Q120) and use these auth-owned lower-case AuthErrorCode constants: duplicate_user 409 for a duplicate username or rename (DuplicateUserException; FR-IAM-001, FR-IAM-003, FR-AUTH-006 AC-3, IR-AUTH-002 AC-1, FR-FLOW-007 AC-3, FR-IAM-014 AC-1); write_conflict 409 for a lost password race (SEC-FLOW-014 AC-4, REL-IAM-002 AC-4, FR-IAM-014 AC-2/AC-3); group_cycle 409 for a group cycle or depth conflict (IR-IAM-004 AC-4/AC-5); group_too_large 409 for the group-delete limit of 1,000 affected users (SEC-IAM-005 AC-2); invalid_setup_token 401 for a POST /auth/setup whose string token does not match the logged setup token (SEC-AUTH-003 AC-2); setup_not_local 403 for a POST /auth/setup that passes the R33 transport check but is not local (SEC-AUTH-003 AC-1, AC-8). A setup body without a token field or whose token is not a JSON string is instead the input-validation 400 BAD_REQUEST of AC-4, and a PROD plaintext non-local request is 403 insecure_transport (SEC-FLOW-001 AC-6). The Lockout login refusal has no code of its own: it is the wrong-password answer invalid_credentials 401 (FR-FLOW-009 AC-2; 00 R34 (4)). Still open (name not final): the 403 of auth.requireRole (IR-AUTH-004 AC-4), the 403 of a false auth.check rule (IR-AUTH-004 AC-8), any other auth answer for which a 0.11.0 block names a status but no code because 00 gives none, and the R31 (3) self-rule refusal (SEC-IAM-004 AC-3, AC-6), for which 00 gives neither status nor code. Each of these uses a code named in this AC that fits the failure, a Core code (StandardErrors.code(status), for example HTTP_403), or a new lower-case AuthErrorCode constant with that status (name not final); the choice is made at implementation and recorded in docs/api, and the producing blocks assert only the status (for the self-rule refusal, neither status nor code). A catalog test asserts each named pair, the six decided pairs included, through the error-code constants (AuthErrorCode), asserts that the wrong-current-password constant exists with status 401, and asserts that AuthErrorCode defines no other auth-owned lower-case code beyond the named pairs and the constants chosen for the open answers above, each of which docs/api lists with its status and producing answer (the Core codes of AC-4 are not auth-owned).

Input-validation 400 uses Core code BAD_REQUEST and is thrown as a Core HttpException, not an AuthRejection; a non-JSON body on an auth endpoint POST is answered 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE in the standard JSON error body by the auth middleware before the body is read (on an admin path behind an API-key guard, by Core's JSON body reader), never as an AuthRejection. Auth 404 answers use code NOT_FOUND and store/throttle 503 answers use code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (the 503 is answered directly by the middleware or guard, FR-AUTH-006 AC-2, or comes from an AuthUnavailableException with the default code through the auth router ErrorMiddleware, FR-AUTH-006 AC-3, or auth.errors()/auth.errorMiddleware(), IR-AUTH-002 AC-1, or is written by the admin PATCH A4 handler with its applied list for a store failure of its steps, FR-IAM-014 AC-9); the only auth 503 with another code is the unconfirmed security write of AC-6 (security_write_conflict).
invalid_request is produced only for multiple credentials on protected paths and credential endpoints, never on a public path.

An AuthUnavailableException created without a code reports code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, and one created with code security_write_conflict reports that code (constructor and accessor names not final). The SINGLE_INSTANCE default security field methods throw it with code security_write_conflict when the re-read does not confirm the write: setEnabled, bumpTokenVersion and setRoles after their 3 retries (REL-IAM-001 AC-2) and changePassword (REL-IAM-002 AC-7). The default updatePasswordHash (rehash) never throws it: over a store whose update() silently does not apply, a call of the default updatePasswordHash raises no exception and the rehash is skipped silently (00 R37: only the rehash is skipped silently; REL-IAM-001). It stays an AuthUnavailableException, so the four AuthUsers exception types (IR-IAM-003) are unchanged. It is answered 503 with body code security_write_conflict by the auth router ErrorMiddleware (FR-AUTH-006 AC-3) and by auth.errors() and auth.errorMiddleware() (IR-AUTH-002 AC-1), except in admin PATCH A4, whose handler catches it when the rename, the password step or a later step throws it and writes the 503 answer with the applied list itself (FR-IAM-014 statement, AC-6 and AC-9).

records.title: Principal access API and route guards

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a protected route auth.user(req) returns the principal; on a public route without a principal auth.user(req) throws AuthStateException (a subclass of IllegalStateException), which auth.errors() turns into 500 JSON without the exception message; auth.userOrNull(req) returns null there.

auth.loadUser(req) never throws and returns null when there is no principal. When the attached principal is a minimal one (.statelessAccess(true), route without a guard), loadUser promotes it: it returns null if the user is missing or disabled, ver differs, or the store throws (store errors are logged), and otherwise a principal with isLoaded() true and the user's roles and scopes (hasScope("posts:write") true for a user holding the 00 §3 role editor with posts:read and posts:write). When the attached principal is already loaded (without statelessAccess, or after a guard promoted it), loadUser returns that same principal and makes no further UserStore call; the ver and enabled check of SEC-AUTH-007 AC-2 and AC-3 has already been applied to it.

app.post("/posts", auth.require("posts:write"), handler) compiles in Java and as a Kotlin trailing lambda; a principal lacking posts:write gets 403 insufficient_scope JSON and the handler is not called; a principal with posts:* or * passes.

auth.requireRole("editor") passes only principals holding role editor and otherwise answers 403 JSON (body code not fixed by 00; chosen per the open-answer rule of IR-AUTH-003 AC-3, and this AC asserts only the status); without a principal every guard answers 401 JSON.
auth.authenticated() promotes a minimal principal (statelessAccess) and answers 401 JSON if the user is disabled or ver differs and 503 JSON if the store throws.
On a RouteGroup, which lacks the (String, Middleware, RouteHandler) overload, route(path).use(auth.require("posts:read")) guards the routes registered through it.
AuthPrincipal getters (getId, getUsername, getRoles, getScopes, getAttributes, isLoaded, hasScope, getApiKeyId) declare no checked exception and getApiKeyId() is @Nullable (null for JWT login).

AccessRule (public in utils.auth, 00 §2) is an @FunctionalInterface with exactly one abstract method allows(AuthPrincipal, Request), and the guard auth.check(AccessRule) (name not final) returns a Middleware: a rule returning true calls the handler, false answers 403 JSON without calling the handler (body code not fixed by 00; chosen per the open-answer rule of IR-AUTH-003 AC-3, and this AC asserts only the status), and without a principal it answers 401 JSON like every guard; auth.check { p, req -> p.hasScope("x") } compiles as a Kotlin SAM lambda. records.title: Cookie value class and SameSite enum

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie` public and final with exactly one public constructor `(String, String)`, a `getName()` method and no `setName` method; `new Cookie("sid", "abc").getName()` returns `sid` and `getValue()` returns `abc`; `new Cookie(null, "v")` and `new Cookie("n", null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-200]

`Cookie` declares `String getValue()`/`void setValue(String)`, `@Nullable String getPath()`/`void setPath(@Nullable String)`, `@Nullable String getDomain()`/`void setDomain(@Nullable String)`, `int getMaxAge()`/`void setMaxAge(int)`, `boolean getSecure()`/`void setSecure(boolean)`, `boolean isHttpOnly()`/`void setHttpOnly(boolean)` and `@Nullable SameSite getSameSite()`/`void setSameSite(@Nullable SameSite)`; a new cookie has path, domain and SameSite `null`, `getSecure()` and `isHttpOnly()` `false` and `getMaxAge()` `-1`. [D-201; D-208] Decision: setters return `void` like the Servlet `Cookie`, and an unset path, domain or SameSite is `null`.
`SameSite.values()` is exactly `STRICT, LAX, NONE` in that order. [D-202]

`setMaxAge(int)` accepts every `int`: a negative value (the default `-1`) means the attribute is not set, so the cookie is a session cookie, `0` means delete and a positive value is a lifetime in seconds. [D-208] Decision: the default `maxAge` is `-1`, and every negative value means "no `Max-Age`" as in the Servlet `Cookie`.

The constructor rejects with `IllegalArgumentException` a name that is empty or not an RFC 7230 token (for example containing a space, `=`, `;`, `,`, CR or LF), and the constructor and `setValue` reject a value with any character outside RFC 6265 `cookie-octet` (CR, LF, `;`, `,`, space, `\\`, a control character or non-ASCII), except that one pair of surrounding double quotes is accepted; `setPath` and `setDomain` reject CR, LF, `;` and every control character; the exception message names the rejected attribute. [D-205; I-017] Decision: an empty value is allowed, so `new Cookie("sid", "")` is valid.

`Cookie` has a package-private static factory method that builds a cookie from a name and a value without validation; the request-cookie parser in `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` reaches it through the internal class `CookieFactoryHook`, whose `private static final java.lang.reflect.Method` field is resolved once with `Class.forName("com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie")` (which also initialises `Cookie`) and `setAccessible(true)`, so no mutable static field exists and the no-mutable-static check of FR-APP-002 AC-2 still passes; the `NaruServe-api` consumer rules of IR-JSON-001 AC-3 also keep that factory method by name; reflection finds no public or protected member of `Cookie` other than those of AC-1 and AC-2 and the `Object` methods. [residual: Building request cookies; wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; FR-APP-002] Decision: the bridge is a reflective, immutable `Method` handle in `internal.CookieFactoryHook`, with no `java.util.function` type (absent from API 21).

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `val c = Cookie("sid", "v"); c.maxAge = 60; c.secure = true; c.isHttpOnly = true; c.sameSite = SameSite.LAX; c.path = "/"; val p: String? = c.path; val n: String = c.name`. [D-201; C-03; I-010]

records.title: Server settings API: app.server(Configurer<ServerOptions>) and app.trustProxy

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `RestApp server(Configurer<ServerOptions>)` and `RestApp trustProxy(boolean)`; `server(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, both methods throw `IllegalStateException` outside `NEW` through the guard of FR-APP-002, and several `server(...)` calls apply in call order to one options object. [D-225; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter] Decision: the settings entry point is `app.server(options -> ...)` and proxy trust is `app.trustProxy(boolean)` (Express `app.set('trust proxy', true)`).

`ServerOptions` declares exactly these setters, each returning `ServerOptions`, with these defaults and inclusive ranges: `bindAddress(String)` `127.0.0.1`; `allowedHosts(String...)` none; `maxHeaderSize(int bytes)` 16384, 1..1048576; `maxHeaderCount(int)` 100, 1..10000; `maxRequestLineLength(int bytes)` 8190, 1..65534; `headerTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 10 s, `bodyReadTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 30 s and `writeTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 30 s, each 1 ms..1 h; `minBodyRate(int bytesPerSecond)` 240, 1..104857600; `maxWorkers(int)` 64, 1..1024; `maxSseStreams(int)` 128, 1..1024; `maxConnections(int)` 512, 1..65536; `maxUpgradedConnections(int)` 128, 1..65536; `maxConnectionsPerAddress(int)` 256, 1..65536. [D-225; D-215; D-216; D-404; D-413; D-414; residual: Upper bounds on size settings] Decision: these names and maxima; `maxWorkers` is the HTTP worker budget of D-404, and `writeTimeout` maps TinyHttpd's socket write timeout (default 30000 ms) so the socket write timeout that `docs/api/defaults.md` names is configurable.

A value below the minimum or above the maximum of AC-2 makes its setter throw `IllegalArgumentException` naming the setting and the allowed range, and `bindAddress(null)`, `bindAddress("")`, `allowedHosts((String[]) null)`, a `null` or empty host name and a `null` `TimeUnit` throw `NullPointerException` or `IllegalArgumentException`; no setter accepts `0`, a negative value or another value meaning unlimited. [residual: Upper bounds on size settings; I-012]

`maxHeaderSize` changes only the total header size of D-215 and leaves the per-line header limit of D-437 unchanged, and `maxRequestLineLength(n)` is the request-line limit that D-414 turns into TinyHttpd's `inputBufferBytes = max(8192, n + 2)`. [D-437; D-414]
`listen(port)` keeps the loopback default: an app that never calls `server(...)` binds `127.0.0.1`. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; D-211]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.server { o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0").allowedHosts("myphone.local").maxHeaderSize(32768) }` and `app.trustProxy(true)`. [D-225; C-03; I-010]

The `RestApp` surface test of IR-APP-002 AC-2 (`HttpApiSurfaceTest`, the wave 4 method set) is re-pointed to the wave 5 set: the wave 4 methods plus `server`, `trustProxy`, `jsonCodec` and `jsonLimit`, every wave 4 signature unchanged, `create()` and `builder()` still the only static methods and no `@Nullable` position on `RestApp`. [I-014; D-225; D-185] Amended by FR-DX-012 (target start-api): the static methods of `RestApp` are `builder()`, `create()` and `start(int, Configurer)`, and `HttpApiSurfaceTest` asserts exactly that set.

records.title: HttpAdapter settings bind: ServerSettings value, ErrorRenderer and safe logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: `HttpAdapter` keeps `void bind(String, int, ExchangeHandler) throws IOException` unchanged and gains the `default` method `void bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler) throws IOException` whose body calls `bind(settings.bindAddress(), settings.port(), handler)`; the test-fixtures `InMemoryHttpAdapter` and a minimal adapter that implements only the four wave 3 methods compile and bind unchanged. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; I-014; D-107]

`DefaultRestApp.listen(port)` calls `bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` exactly once with a settings value whose `port()` is the `listen` argument and whose other values equal the frozen `ServerOptions` (defaults when `server(...)` was never called), so a recording adapter sees `127.0.0.1` by default and `0.0.0.0` after `server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0"))`. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; D-225]

`ServerSettings` is a public final class with a getter for every setting of IR-ENGINE-001 AC-2, the port, `Logger logger()` and `ErrorRenderer errorRenderer()`; it has no setter, `allowedHosts()` returns an unmodifiable list, and no parameter, return or field type of `ServerSettings` or `ErrorRenderer` lies outside `java.*` and `com.snoworca.naruserve` packages. [D-104; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter]

The `logger()` of the settings value is the core's exception-safe wrapper of the app logger, so a test app logger that throws on every call, used by an adapter through `settings.logger().warn(...)`, never lets an exception reach the adapter. [wave decision: The adapter gets the safe logger; D-220]

`ErrorRenderer` is a `@FunctionalInterface` with `String render(int status)`; the renderer in the settings returns the standard error body of FR-APP-006 for that status with the `code` of its status and a fresh 16-hex-digit request id on every call, identical in format to the body the dispatcher writes. [D-405; D-132; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter] Decision: the renderer returns the JSON text, which the adapter sends as `application/json; charset=UTF-8`.

records.title: Proxy trust configuration API: app.trustProxyHops(int), app.trustProxyCidrs(String...) and read accessors for the current proxy trust setting

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `RestApp trustProxyHops(int hops)` and `RestApp trustProxyCidrs(String... cidrs)`; each throws `IllegalStateException` outside `NEW` through `AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable`, and the reflection test of CON-APP-002 AC-1 lists both and finds them rejected in `RUNNING`.

`trustProxyHops(-1)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Decision: `trustProxyHops(0)` is accepted and leaves the direct peer untrusted, so `remoteAddress()` and `isSecure()` keep the adapter values (R32: the peer is trusted when n ≥ 1).

`trustProxyCidrs((String[]) null)` and `trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8", null)` throw `NullPointerException`; `"10.0.0.0/33"`, `"fd00::/129"` and `"abc/8"` each throw `IllegalArgumentException` whose message contains the rejected value; `"10.0.0.0/8"`, `"192.168.1.0/24"` and `"fd00::/8"` are accepted.

Public read accessors (names not final) report the proxy trust setting without reflection and are all non-null: the legacy flag is a `boolean`, the hop count an `int` and the CIDR list a non-null `List<String>`. Decision: an unset hop count reads `0` (the same meaning as `trustProxyHops(0)` in AC-2: the peer is not trusted) and an unset CIDR list reads as an empty list, so "no proxy trust configured" is legacy flag `false`, hop count `0` and an empty CIDR list.
