records.title: WWW-Authenticate challenge shapes for 401 and 403 auth responses

acceptanceCriteria.text: API keys disabled, protected path, no credential -> 401 code unauthenticated with header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer (no error attribute).
API keys disabled, expired Bearer token on a protected path -> 401 code invalid_token with header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token".
API keys enabled with the default scheme, no credential -> one header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, ApiKey; a malformed or wrong key -> the same header value with body code invalid_api_key.
API keys enabled, expired JWT -> WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", ApiKey; with .apiKeyScheme("ak") the same response carries Bearer error="invalid_token", ak.
No response puts error= or error_description= on the key-scheme challenge, and the key-scheme challenge appears only on 401 responses.
A key-authenticated request rejected with 403 insufficient_scope or 403 api_key_not_allowed -> the response has no WWW-Authenticate header.
A JWT-authenticated request rejected by a scope guard with 403 insufficient_scope -> the response carries a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge with error="insufficient_scope".

traceLinks.notes: 401/403 bodies use the standard error JSON shape; this adds the WWW-Authenticate header.
second challenge uses the configured scheme

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI exchange data contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: The SPI exposes, per request, the request line as the method token, the raw request-target path, the raw query string (or its absence) and the HTTP version, plus the header names and values in received order, a body `InputStream`, the remote address and the secure flag. [D-105] Decision: the headers are exposed as a `List<Map.Entry<String, String>>` in received order with duplicates kept, not as a `Map`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-1]

The SPI accepts from the core a status code, response headers and a body `OutputStream`, and the core writes status and headers before the first body byte. [D-105] Decision: status, headers and the content length (`-1` when unknown) pass in one `commit` call that returns the body `OutputStream`, and a second start of the response throws `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-2] The exchange outlives `ExchangeHandler#handle` until the core calls `finish` or `abort`, and the adapter may force-close it only at its stop deadline; `abort()` is idempotent and thread-safe (it may run on any thread, also while another thread is in `commit`, a body write or `finish`, which then fail with an `IOException`). The headers passed to `commit` are sent as given: they already carry `Content-Length` when the core knows it (a `HEAD` response carries the length the `GET` body would have had) and the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`; `contentLength` is the number of body bytes the core will write, `0` for a bodyless response (`204`, `304`, `HEAD`) or `-1` when unknown, which the adapter frames itself (chunked, or close on HTTP/1.0) and is the only case where it may add a framing header. Header names and values are ISO-8859-1: the core guarantees every char is at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, so the adapter writes each char as one byte. [wave 3 implementation decision]

The raw request-target path and the raw query string travel through the SPI as separate undecoded fields: an exchange with target `/a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and the core alone yields `req.path()` = `/a b` and `req.query("x")` = `A`. [D-399; wave decision: Adapter halves] Decision: the raw query is `null` when the target has no `?`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-3]

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI extension points and bind/stop lifecycle

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the file-transfer extension point the core hands the adapter a `java.io.File` with an offset and a length, and the adapter writes exactly those bytes of the file as the response body; an in-memory test hands over a file with a non-zero offset and a length shorter than the rest of the file and reads back exactly that byte range from the client body. [D-106]

Through the protocol-upgrade extension point the core hands the adapter an upgrade callback with a `101` response, and the adapter invokes that callback with the exchange's raw input and output streams after writing the `101` response; an in-memory test observes that the callback ran with the exchange's streams (or that the in-memory adapter recorded the hand-over). [D-106]

The event-stream point hands the adapter a core-owned drain loop that keeps writing after the handler returned until the core reports the stream ended, and the adapter chooses the thread that runs it; in wave 3 (before `res.sse` exists) an in-memory test supplies a drain loop through the SPI type, runs it on an adapter-chosen thread after the handler returned and sees it end only when the end is reported. [D-106] Decision: `eventStream` returns to the caller at once, and the in-memory adapter runs the drain on its own worker thread, completing the client response when the drain returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-4]

The three extension points are SPI types in `NaruServe-api`, usable by an adapter without any NaruServe class outside `NaruServe-api`, so waves 6, 7 and 8 add adapter classes against them without changing the SPI. [D-106]

The SPI declares a bind to an address and port that returns only after binding completed, and a separate call through which the core reads the actual bound port; with the in-memory adapter, a bind with port `0` reports a positive bound port that the core reads back through the SPI and that stays the same on every read until stop, and a bind with a positive port reports that port. [D-107] Decision: for a bind with port `0` the in-memory adapter assigns a positive port from a counter starting at `49152`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-5]

The SPI declares a blocking stop that stops accepting, waits for in-flight exchanges until a deadline passed by the core and then force-closes the remaining connections, and a separate final release that waits at most a fixed margin for the adapter's threads to end; the in-memory adapter implements both and a test shows an in-flight exchange still running at the deadline is force-closed. [D-107] Decision: an exchange in flight at the deadline is aborted so its client response reports `abnormallyClosed`, and the in-memory adapter's release shuts its worker pool waiting at most 1 second. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: HttpException response headers: withHeader, headers() and the error path that applies them

acceptanceCriteria.text: `HttpException` declares `public HttpException withHeader(String name, String value)` returning the same instance and `public List<Map.Entry<String, String>> headers()`, which returns an empty list for a new exception; the existing constructors, `status()` and `code()` keep their signatures, which a reflection test asserts. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)]

`new HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1").withHeader("Connection", "close")` returns entries in that order from `headers()`, adding the same name twice keeps both entries in order, and calling `add` or `remove` on the returned list throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] Decision: entries are kept in an `ArrayList` of `SimpleImmutableEntry` so the exception stays `Serializable`, and `headers()` returns `Collections.unmodifiableList` of it. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-8]

`withHeader` with a name or value containing CR or LF throws `IllegalArgumentException`, with a `null` name or value throws `NullPointerException`, and in both cases `headers()` is unchanged afterwards. Decision: the check is the `res.header` check of FR-HTTP-015. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] Decision: a name that is not a token, a control character in the value and a character above U+00FF in the value are refused with `IllegalArgumentException` as well as CR and LF. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-7]

A handler that sets `X-App: 1` and then throws `new HttpException(426).withHeader("Sec-WebSocket-Version", "13")` gives the client `426`, the header `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`, the standard error body with the request id, and no `X-App` header, because the error path drops app-set headers as FR-APP-005 states and then applies the exception's headers. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] [D-444] Decision: the exception's headers are appended after the app-set headers were cleared and `Content-Type` was set; when an `onError` handler itself throws, that exception is the error, so the original exception's headers are not added. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-9]

When an `onError` handler leaves the response `NEW`, the standard error response still carries the exception's headers; when an `onError` handler answers with `res.status(418).send("x")`, the client receives only the headers that handler set and none of the exception's. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)]

Over TinyHttpd, a handler throwing `new HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1").withHeader("Connection", "close")` gives the client `503` with `Retry-After: 1` and `Connection: close`, and the server closes the connection after the response. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] [D-445]

A `withHeader("Content-Length", "5")` entry is not written to the error response, whose `Content-Length` matches the standard error body, which a test asserts byte for byte. Decision: the body writer owns `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)]
A Kotlin test compiles `throw HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1")` inside a SAM handler, and `withHeader` and `headers()` return non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [C-03; T11]

records.requirement: The system shall let an `HttpException` carry response headers through `withHeader(String name, String value)`, which validates the header like `res.header` and returns the same exception, and `headers()`, an unmodifiable list in insertion order, and shall set those headers on the standard error response that the dispatcher's error path renders for that exception.
records.rationale: Covers wave decision Rejection headers (W2-002; D-444, D-445): it carries `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` (FR-WS-002), `Retry-After` (FR-WS-009) and `Connection: close` (FR-WS-009, FR-APP-020) from a pre-`101` rejection to the error response, the way Express `finalhandler` applies `err.headers`. Measured: `HttpException.java:8-37` has the constructors `(int)`, `(int, String)`, `(int, String, Throwable)` and `status()`/`code()` and no header field; `internal/ErrorPath.java` and `internal/StandardErrors.java:60-92` render the standard error body after dropping app-set headers (FR-APP-005 AC-4, which still holds: the exception's own headers are new, not app-set ones). IR-APP-003 lists no method set, so the add-only methods need no supersede. Decision: `withHeader` returns `this` so `throw new HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1")` compiles; duplicates are kept in order; validation reuses the `res.header` CR/LF check (FR-HTTP-015). Decision: an `onError` handler that leaves the response `NEW` still gets the exception's headers on the standard error response; an `onError` handler that answers itself decides its own headers. Pitfall: a `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding` set through `withHeader` would corrupt the error body framing; the error path lets the body writer own those two names and skips them. Rejected alternative: a separate `HeaderedHttpException` subclass; every catch site would need two types, reopen never in v1.

records.title: Source-compatible detected transport-abort notification for deferred requests

acceptanceCriteria.text: The default method validates a nonnull Runnable and remains a no-op for legacy/custom exchanges that do not support detection, so existing implementations compile and remain usable. Built-in Tiny/Servlet exchanges implement actual listener registration; normal successful finish does not report an abort.

Detected abort, write/read failure, async timeout, disconnect or forced stop notifies each registered listener once, including listeners registered after the abort. State/listener snapshots are guarded briefly and user callbacks execute outside locks; repeated aborts and concurrent registrations do not duplicate callbacks.

Callback failures do not prevent remaining listeners, terminal state, stream closure, adapter in-flight removal or bounded-pool release. A focused utility in the API common package is reused by adapters rather than duplicating listener-state algorithms.

The core registers before invoking user callbacks and translates the detected abort into its existing response/request termination path exactly once, respecting active callback/upload/stream ownership and avoiding recursion when Response.abort itself invokes HttpExchange.abort.

Normal response finish retains the existing Response.onDone lifecycle path, so an early transport finish callback cannot incorrectly convert a successful response into ABORTED. Existing WS/SSE protocols and binary/source compatibility are tested.

Tests cover synchronous abort during registration, delayed/late/concurrent abort, throwing listeners and built-in adapter timeout/disconnect integration. Notification is for transport events the adapter actually detects; instant detection of an idle peer closure without I/O is not promised.

Existing recoverable request-body protocol, size-limit and read-timeout errors remain eligible for their declared HTTP 400/408/413 response while the output is writable; mapping such an error does not itself eagerly notify terminal abort. A detected terminal I/O/reset, asynchronous lifetime timeout or failure while writing that error response does notify abort. Adapter tests distinguish recoverable HTTP rejection from transport termination.

When an adapter emits an error response independently of the core (including unsupported Servlet asynchronous configuration), terminal access logging preserves its actual status and successfully written body-byte count. Source-compatible optional HttpExchange default methods responseStatus() and responseBytesWritten() report unknown as 0 and -1; the Servlet adapter reports its synthetic response and the core otherwise retains its own metrics. Invalid or failing optional observations fall back without blocking cleanup or emitting a second response; no new abstract SPI method or dependency is introduced.

records.title: Public BodyTooLargeException in com.snoworca.naruserve

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `com.snoworca.naruserve.BodyTooLargeException` public, final and a direct subclass of `java.io.IOException`, declaring a public constructor `(long limit)` and a public `long limit()` that returns the constructor argument.

`Class.forName("com.snoworca.naruserve.internal.BodyTooLargeException")` throws `ClassNotFoundException`, and the `NaruServe-api` JAR holds no class of that name and no other alias of the moved class.

The internal limit-enforcing stream throws the public class with `limit()` equal to its limit for both overruns of FR-HTTP-020 (limit 10 with an 11-byte source of unknown length, and limit 10 with a declared `Content-Length` of 11), the urlencoded form reader still answers such an overrun `413`, and the multipart parser still recognises the overrun through the public class.

A JSON body over `jsonLimit` without `Content-Length`, decoded through the default codec, is still answered `413` with code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (FR-JSON-001 AC-4 and AC-8 of this requirement), the overrun being detected through the public class.

A Kotlin source test compiles and runs `try { ... } catch (e: BodyTooLargeException) { val limit: Long = e.limit() }` against the public class without a platform type, and the nullability reflection test of FR-KT-001 passes over the class with no `@NonNull` on it.

With limit `10`, reading an 11-byte source without a declared `Content-Length` (a chunked-style source of unknown length) through the internal limit-enforcing stream throws the public `com.snoworca.naruserve.BodyTooLargeException` on the read that would return byte 11, no byte beyond the limit is returned, and the stream reads at most limit+1 bytes from the source.

With limit `10` and a declared `Content-Length` of `11`, the first read of the internal limit-enforcing stream throws the public `com.snoworca.naruserve.BodyTooLargeException` without reading any byte from the source, so the body readers can tell it from a transport `IOException` and answer `413`.

When `req.body(...)` decoding fails and the core's size-limited stream recorded an overrun (the public `com.snoworca.naruserve.BodyTooLargeException`, an `IOException` that a codec such as Gson may wrap), the core answers `HttpException` `413`, detecting the overrun from the limited stream's state and not only from the exception the codec rethrows; when the failure's cause chain holds an `HttpException` (for example the adapter `408` of FR-ENGINE-005), that same instance is rethrown with its own status; and each such failure reaches `onError` and the access log like any handler exception of FR-APP-005.

The bodies `{"a":`, `[1,]`, an empty body and a body of only spaces and newlines are each answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`; the empty and whitespace-only bodies never reach the codec, and an `IOException` thrown by `JsonCodec.decode` is turned into `HttpException` `400` with that exception as cause unless AC-8 of this requirement applies; an unchecked codec exception reaches the error path as `500` (restates FR-JSON-001 AC-2 with its exception now pointing at AC-8).

records.title: Public header value predicate HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `public static boolean isFieldValue(String)` on `com.snoworca.naruserve.common.HttpHeaderValues`, beside the existing public `isToken`, with no `@NonNull` on it.
`HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue` returns `true` for the empty string and for a value holding HTAB, and `false` for values holding CR, LF, NUL, DEL or U+0100.
`isFieldValue` returns `true` for a value of printable ASCII and space and for a value holding U+00FF, and `false` for a value holding U+0001 or U+001F.

`DefaultResponse` checks header values only through `HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue`, and a test over every char from U+0000 to U+017F shows that `res.header("X", value)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` exactly when `isFieldValue(value)` is `false`.
A Kotlin source test compiles and runs `val ok: Boolean = HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue(value)` without a platform type.

records.title: UserStore SPI: five required methods, five default field methods, the default listing method and the atomic declaration

acceptanceCriteria.text: A class implementing only findByUsername(String), findById(String), create(AuthUser), update(AuthUser) and delete(String) compiles as a UserStore in Java and in Kotlin; each of the five is declared throws Exception, and each reference-typed parameter and return of the five is either annotated @Nullable or non-null through the utils.auth.user package's @NullMarked default without an annotation, with no @NonNull annotation (FR-KT-001 AC-3, CON-AUTH-004 AC-2).

UserStore declares default methods boolean updatePasswordHash(id, expectedOldHash, newHash), boolean changePassword(id, expectedOldHash, expectedVer, newHash), setEnabled, bumpTokenVersion and setRoles, and the default listing method UserPage list(int offset, int limit, @Nullable String search) throws Exception (name not final) [INFERRED:med:advisory] from 05 §3.4, whose UserPage value (name not final) exposes getItems(), getTotal(), getOffset() and getLimit() [INFERRED:med:advisory]; a store that does not override supportsAtomicFieldWrites() returns false. records.title: TypeRef captures generic types and ships consumer R8/ProGuard rules

acceptanceCriteria.text: `new TypeRef<List<User>>() {}.getType()` returns a `ParameterizedType` whose raw type is `java.util.List` and whose only argument is `User`, and `new TypeRef<String>() {}.getType()` returns `String.class`. [D-183; T08] Decision: `TypeRef` is a public abstract class with a protected no-argument constructor and the public method `Type getType()`.

Constructing a raw subclass (`new TypeRef() {}`) or a subclass whose type argument is a type variable (inside `<X> TypeRef<X> make() { return new TypeRef<X>() {}; }`) throws `IllegalStateException` whose message says that a concrete type argument is required. records.requirement: The system shall name the accessors of value objects such as `Cookie` with the Servlet-style `getX()`, `setX(value)` and `isX()` rules so that Kotlin property syntax compiles — `cookie.maxAge = 60`, `cookie.isHttpOnly = true`, `cookie.secure = true`, `res.isCommitted` and `req.isSecure` — while the Express-style short methods (`req.param`, `req.path`, `res.status`) stay ordinary methods.
records.rationale: Covers D-353 and wave decisions of waves 3 and 5 on `Cookie`; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `Cookie.java:90-151` declares `getName`, `getValue`/`setValue`, `getPath`/`setPath`, `getDomain`/`setDomain`, `getMaxAge`/`setMaxAge`, `getSecure`/`setSecure`, `isHttpOnly`/`setHttpOnly` and `getSameSite`/`setSameSite`; `docs/api/kotlin.md` already shows `isHttpOnly = true`, `secure = true`, `maxAge = 3600` and `res.isCommitted`. Pitfall: Kotlin synthesises a property from a `boolean getX()` as `x` and from `boolean isX()` as `isX`; the pair `getSecure`/`setSecure` therefore reads `secure`, not `isSecure`, and a rename to `isSecure()` would break `kotlin.md`. Pitfall: a getter without a matching setter gives a read-only `val`; a setter whose parameter type differs from the getter's return type gives no property. Rejected alternative: fluent setters (`cookie.maxAge(60)`) as in Express; they would not form Kotlin properties and C-03 requires property syntax.

records.requirement: The system shall provide a non-null reified Request.body<T>() extension using an anonymous TypeRef<T> to preserve complete nested type arguments; JSON null throws HttpException(400).
records.rationale: Covers D-354 and the module line of wave decision Kotlin reified extension of wave 5 (OPS-JSON-001 AC-3, which fixed the shape in `docs/api/kotlin.md`); supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `NaruServe-kotlin/src/main` holds only the placeholder `KotlinModule.NAME`; `NaruServe-api/src/test/kotlin/com/snoworca/naruserve/JsonDocsKotlinTest.kt:40` carries a test-local copy of the same function with the comment that the module extension arrives in wave 8; `NaruServe-kotlin` has `kotlin-stdlib` as `api` and depends on `NaruServe-api` (CON-BUILD-006). Decision: the file is `RequestExtensions.kt` and the consumer imports `com.snoworca.naruserve.kotlin.body`; the extension adds no overload on `Request` because the member `body(Class<T>)` takes an argument, so `req.body<User>()` resolves to the extension. Pitfall: `T::class.java` loses element types, so `req.body<List<User>>()` decodes a raw `List`; `docs/api/kotlin.md` says so and points to `TypeRef`. Rejected alternative: an extension that returns `T?`; it would only rename the member, and the point of D-354 is a non-null result for a caller that asked for one.

records.title: Multipart and form configuration API: app.multipart(Configurer<MultipartOptions>) and app.formLimit

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `multipart(Configurer<MultipartOptions> configurer)` returning the same `RestApp`, and the public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.MultipartOptions` declares the fluent setters `maxFileSize(long bytes)`, `maxRequestSize(long bytes)`, `maxParts(int count)`, `memoryThreshold(int bytes)` and `tempDirectory(File dir)`, each returning `MultipartOptions`; a configurer that sets all five values is applied, which a test reads back through the internal settings. Decision: the configurer is the `Configurer` functional interface of IR-APP-007. [D-231] Decision: the configurer runs on a copy of the settings that is swapped in only after it returned, so a configurer that throws propagates its exception and leaves every earlier setting unchanged. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-1]

An app that never calls `multipart` uses `maxFileSize` 33554432, `maxRequestSize` 67108864, `maxParts` 20, `memoryThreshold` 65536 and `tempDirectory` equal to `new File(System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir"))`. Decision: the default temp directory is `java.io.tmpdir`, which on Android is the app's cache directory. [D-232; D-239] Decision: `java.io.tmpdir` is read once when the app is constructed, not at each parse. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-4]

`maxFileSize` and `maxRequestSize` accept 1 to 4294967296, `maxParts` accepts 1 to 10000 and `memoryThreshold` accepts 1 to 16777216, all inclusive; `0`, a negative value or a value above the upper bound throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the setting, and `tempDirectory(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. Decision: unlimited multipart limits are not allowed, so no value means unlimited. [D-239] Decision: the message has the form `<setting> must be in <lo>..<hi>: <value>` and is thrown by that setter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-2]

`RestApp` declares `formLimit(long bytes)` returning the same `RestApp`, with default 1048576 and inclusive range 1 to 1073741824; a value outside the range throws `IllegalArgumentException` naming the setting. Decision: the urlencoded limit API is `formLimit`, mirroring `jsonLimit` and Express `express.urlencoded({ limit })`. [D-238]

The part header limits are fixed at 8192 bytes per part header line and 16384 bytes of total header size per part, and reflection finds no setter for them on `MultipartOptions` or `RestApp`. Decision: the two part header limits are not configurable. [D-235; wave decision: Oversized part headers]

`multipart(...)` and `formLimit(...)` called after `listen()` throw `IllegalStateException` from the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002, and leave the settings unchanged. [D-231; D-238] Decision: the `NEW`-state guard throws before the configurer is invoked. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-3]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.multipart { o -> o.maxFileSize(1024).maxParts(3) }` and `app.formLimit(2048)` as SAM lambdas without a DSL, and the returned `MultipartOptions` and `RestApp` are non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [D-231; D-238; C-03; T11]

records.title: Request form, file, files and parts accessors and the UploadFile interface

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Request` declares `@Nullable String form(String name)`, `@Nullable UploadFile file(String name)`, `List<UploadFile> files(String name)` and `List<UploadFile> parts()`, and reflection finds each with exactly that signature. [D-240; D-241]

The public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.UploadFile` extends `AutoCloseable` and declares `String name()`, `@Nullable String filename()`, `@Nullable String contentType()`, `long size()`, `InputStream inputStream()`, `void save(File destination)`, `void transferTo(OutputStream target)`, `byte[] bytes()` and `void close()`, the content methods declaring `throws IOException` and `close()` declaring no checked exception. Decision: `filename()` and `contentType()` return `null` when the part header has no `filename` parameter or no `Content-Type`. [D-248]

Decision: `parts()` returns every part of a multipart body in body order, text fields included (their `filename()` is `null`), as an unmodifiable `List<UploadFile>`, and returns an empty list for a urlencoded or non-form body. records.title: Lookup result contract and precedence

acceptanceCriteria.text: The result type exposes exactly six kinds and each lookup returns exactly one; the matched kind carries the handler, the path parameters, the actual method (the request method for a direct match, `GET` under automatic `HEAD` and for a WebSocket match; it does not decide the wave 3 `req.method()` value, D-398), the route kind and the automatic-`HEAD` flag, and the method-mismatch and automatic-OPTIONS kinds carry an `Allow` `MethodSet`. [D-390] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-1] A field a kind does not carry reads as null (handler, method, route kind, allow) and params reads as an empty map.

An unrecognised method token yields unsupported method even when no pattern matches the path, and a recognised method on a path no pattern matches yields no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]
On a matched path a route of the request method wins over automatic OPTIONS and automatic `HEAD`, which win over WebSocket-only, which wins over method mismatch. [wave decision: lookup result order]

The lookup takes the raw, undecoded path as received in the request target, so a lookup of `GET /files/%252e` against `GET /files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`; the path is checked with the path validator before any result is chosen, so a rejected path such as `/a%zz` fails with `IllegalArgumentException` for every method token, and "whatever the path" elsewhere in this scope means whatever accepted path. [D-051; loop W residual: validator does not decode] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-2] The `IllegalArgumentException` names the path and is thrown before the method token is read.

The upgrade flag is ignored unless the method token is `GET`; registering a route after the freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, a lookup before a successful freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, and the routing configuration error is an exception type of its own (name decided under C-07), distinct from `IllegalStateException` and `IllegalArgumentException`. [wave decision: route kind; D-058]

Decision: the data-only send is `send(String data)`, the explicit close is `close()`, and `send` returns `false` exactly when the client has ended or this send ends it (closed by `close()`, disconnected, overflowed, shut down, or a `HEAD` request), so the send that overflows the queue returns `false` as FR-SSE-002 states, and `true` otherwise, when the event was written or queued. [D-339]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.SseEvent` has no public constructor and declares the public static factory `SseEvent event(String name)` and the instance methods `id(String id)`, `data(@Nullable String data)` and `retry(long millis)`, each returning `SseEvent`; a Java test compiles `SseEvent.event("progress").id("100").data("x").retry(3000)` and reflection finds no other public method declared by `SseEvent`. [D-330]

`RestApp` declares `sse(Configurer<SseOptions> configurer)` returning the same `RestApp`, and the public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.SseOptions` declares `heartbeatInterval(long time, TimeUnit unit)` and `sendQueueSize(int bytes)`, each returning `SseOptions`; a configurer setting both is applied, which a test reads back through the internal settings, `sse(...)` called after `listen()` throws `IllegalStateException` from the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 without running the configurer, and the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `sse(Configurer)->RestApp`. Decision: the configurer runs on a copy swapped in only after it returned, so a throwing configurer leaves every earlier setting unchanged. [D-339; D-419] Decision: `requireConfigurable("sse")` runs before the null check, and the configurer runs on `copy()`, which is swapped in only after it returned. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-3]

An app that never calls `sse` uses `heartbeatInterval` 15 s and `sendQueueSize` 262144 bytes, which a test reads through the internal settings. Decision: the heartbeat interval default is 15 s. [D-339; D-332; D-419]

`heartbeatInterval` accepts 1 s to 1 h and `sendQueueSize` accepts 1 to 16777216, both inclusive; `0`, a negative value or a value above the bound throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message has the form `sendQueueSize must be in 1..16777216: <value>` for the size and `heartbeatInterval must be in 1 s..1 h: <time> <unit>` for the duration, a `null` unit throws `NullPointerException`, and no setting accepts a value meaning unlimited: every setting has a bounded range and a finite default (I-012). [D-419; D-339] Decision: the duration is converted with `unit.toMillis` (saturating) and accepted at 1000..3600000 ms, so `999 MILLISECONDS` is refused with the caller's own time and unit in the message. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-4]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.get("/events") { req, res -> val c = res.sse(); c.send("ready"); c.onClose { } }` and `app.sse { o -> o.heartbeatInterval(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS) }` as SAM lambdas without a DSL against the in-memory adapter, and `res.sse()`, `SseEvent.event("x")` and the returned `SseOptions` are non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [D-326; C-03; T11]

records.requirement: The system shall provide `SseClient Response.sse()`, the `SseClient` interface with `send(String event, String data)`, `send(String data)`, `send(SseEvent event)`, `close()`, `isOpen()` and `onClose(SseClient.CloseListener)`, the `SseEvent` type built through `SseEvent.event(name)` with `id`, `data` and `retry`, and `RestApp sse(Configurer<SseOptions> configurer)` with the settings `heartbeatInterval` and `sendQueueSize`, each bounded and defaulted as the acceptance criteria state.
records.rationale:
Covers D-326 (API part), D-330 (API part), D-339 (heartbeat, data-only send and explicit close APIs), D-419 (SSE setting name) and the C-07 choices of the authoring plan; T11/C-03 for Kotlin. Measured: `Response.java:9` says "No sse method yet; a later wave adds it", and `json` (`:55`) and `addCookie` (`:66`) are `default` methods throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`, so `sse()` follows the same add-only pattern (I-014: no changed public signature). `Request.java:47` already declares `lastEventId()` (FR-HTTP-011 AC-3), reused by FR-SSE-001. The configurer follows IR-APP-007 and IR-MULTIPART-001 (copy swapped in after it returned; message `sendQueueSize must be in 1..16777216: <value>` for the size and `heartbeatInterval must be in 1 s..1 h: <time> <unit>` for the duration, as AC-6 states), and the ranges keep I-012 (no unlimited value). Decision on defaults: heartbeat 15 s, below the 30 s to 60 s idle cutoffs of common proxies and load balancers; send queue 256 KiB from D-406. Pitfall: a `send` that throws on an ended client would force every broadcaster to catch; `send` returns `false` instead, like the `ws` library's send on a closed socket. Rejected alternative: a fluent `SseEvent` with a public constructor; the factory keeps `event` mandatory and matches `docs/api/sse.md`, reopen if data-only `SseEvent` objects are requested. Rejected alternative: Express-style `res.write` of raw event text; it leaves line splitting to the app and breaks D-329. Express mapping: `res.writeHead(200, {'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream'})` plus `res.write('event: x
data: y

')` and `req.on('close')`. Test to re-point: `HttpApiSurfaceTest` (the `LATER_WAVE_NAMES` entry `sse` and the `Response` method set) moves to IR-SSE-001.

records.title: Static mount API: app.staticFiles, StaticOptions and the engine-free ResourceResolver

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `staticFiles(String prefix, File dir)` and `staticFiles(String prefix, File dir, Configurer<StaticOptions> options)`, both returning the same `RestApp`; a prefix not starting with `/` throws `IllegalArgumentException`, a `null` argument throws `NullPointerException`, and several calls with different prefixes register several mounts. Decision: a trailing `/` on the prefix is ignored, so `/assets` and `/assets/` name the same mount. [D-256; D-258] Decision: a trailing `/` is stripped except from the prefix `/` itself, and the same prefix registered twice keeps both mounts in registration order, like two Express `static` middlewares. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-1] Decision: a `dir` that does not exist is accepted at registration; the canonical root is taken at `listen`, and a missing root serves nothing (`404`). [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-2]

The public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.StaticOptions` declares `index(String name)` (default `index.html`), `directoryListing(boolean)` (default `false`), `spaFallback(boolean)` (default `false`), `spaExclude(String... prefixes)`, `cache(String pattern, CachePolicy policy)`, `mime(String ext, String type)` and `allowSymlinks(boolean)` (default `false`), each returning `StaticOptions`. Decision: `allowSymlinks(true)` serves symbolic links below the root while the canonical-root containment still applies, `spaExclude` adds prefixes to the always-excluded `/api/` and `/ws/`, and `mime(ext, type)` accepts `ext` with or without the leading dot (a leading dot is stripped), like `MimeTypes.register`. [D-261; D-272; D-267; D-275] Decision: `index` with an empty name or a name holding `/`, and `spaExclude` with a prefix not starting with `/`, throw `IllegalArgumentException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-3]

The public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.ResourceResolver` in `NaruServe-api` declares `open`, `length`, `etag` and `modified` and names only `java.io` and `java.lang` types; the built-in `java.io.File` resolver is an internal class and the only implementation in v1, and reflection finds no public or protected method of `RestApp`, `StaticOptions` or `Response` that accepts a `ResourceResolver`. Decision: `InputStream open(String path)`, `long length(String path)`, `String etag(String path)` and `long modified(String path)` take the mount-relative path; for `res.file` and `res.download`, which have no mount, the built-in resolver is rooted at the canonical absolute parent of the named file (FR-STATIC-006 AC-5) and the path is the file's name; the SAF resolver is a post-v1 P5 item under D-380. [D-409; wave decision: The root of res.file and res.download] Decision: a resolver method that cannot read the path throws `IOException`, and `FileNotFoundException` for a missing or refused path. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-4]

No public or protected signature of `StaticOptions`, `ResourceResolver`, `CachePolicy` or `MimeTypes` names a `java.nio.file` type (reflection test), and the API 21 animal-sniffer check of CON-BUILD-012 passes on `NaruServe-api`. [D-409; D-270]

`AppLifecycleGuardTest#sdsAc4_FR_APP_002_AC4_reflectionFindsEveryRestAppAndRouteBuilderRegistrationRefusedInRunning`, re-pointed to this requirement, covers the new `RestApp` setters `multipart`, `formLimit`, both `staticFiles` overloads and `defaultCache`, each throwing `IllegalStateException` under the `NEW`-state guard when called after `listen()`, and `mimeTypes().register(...)` after `listen()` also throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-231; D-238; D-256; D-410; D-277]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.staticFiles("/", dir) { o -> o.index("main.html").spaFallback(true) }` and `app.staticFiles("/assets", File("public"))` without a DSL, then requests `/` and receives `main.html`, with `StaticOptions` a non-platform type. [D-256; D-261; C-03; T11]

records.title: CachePolicy, MimeTypes, res.cache, res.file, res.download and app.defaultCache API

acceptanceCriteria.text: The public final class `com.snoworca.naruserve.CachePolicy` has no public constructor and no setter, provides the static factories `noStore()`, `noCache()`, `privateFor(long amount, TimeUnit unit)` and `publicFor(long amount, TimeUnit unit)`, and `immutable()` returns a new `CachePolicy` while the receiver keeps its value. Decision: the header value is read through `String getHeaderValue()`, so Kotlin reads `policy.headerValue`. [D-278] Decision: `privateFor` and `publicFor` with a negative amount throw `IllegalArgumentException`, and `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` follow `getHeaderValue()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-5]

`RestApp mimeTypes()` returns a `MimeTypes` whose `MimeTypes register(String ext, String type)` returns the same registry for chaining; two apps get two independent registries. Decision: `ext` is accepted with or without the leading dot, and a leading dot is stripped, the same rule as `StaticOptions.mime`. [D-277]

`Response` declares `cache(CachePolicy policy)` returning the same `Response` and the terminal methods `file(File file)` and `download(File file, String filename)`, which end the response like `send`. Decision: `res.file` sends no `Content-Disposition`, like Express `res.sendFile`. [D-280; D-292; D-293] Decision: `cache` on a committed response throws `IllegalStateException`, like `header`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-6]
`RestApp` declares `defaultCache(@Nullable CachePolicy policy)` returning the same `RestApp`. Decision: the default is `null`, which adds no `Cache-Control` header. [D-410]

`HttpApiSurfaceTest`, re-pointed to this requirement, checks the wave 6 `RestApp` set (the wave 5 set plus `multipart`, `formLimit`, both `staticFiles` overloads, `mimeTypes` and `defaultCache`, with `create()` and `builder()` still the only static methods and the only new `@Nullable` position the parameter of `defaultCache`) and the wave 6 `Response` set (the wave 5 set plus `cache`, `file` and `download`), with every earlier signature unchanged, and `LATER_WAVE_NAMES` keeps only `sse`. [D-256; D-277; D-280; D-292; D-410; I-014] Amended by FR-DX-012 (target start-api): the static methods of `RestApp` are `builder()`, `create()` and `start(int, Configurer)`, and `HttpApiSurfaceTest` asserts exactly that set.

records.title: NaruServe-servlet public surface: ServletAdapter, ServletConfigurer, NaruServeInitializer and the init-parameters

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `ServletAdapter` public, final, implementing `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.HttpAdapter` with a public no-argument constructor; `ServletConfigurer` a public interface annotated `@FunctionalInterface` whose only abstract method is `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder)` declared `throws Exception`; `NaruServeInitializer` a public class implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`; and package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet` annotated `@NullMarked`. [D-358; D-363]

The built module jar holds `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer` whose only line is `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet.NaruServeInitializer`, read from the jar as `DefaultAppFactoryTest` reads the bootstrap services file, through a new system property that `build.gradle` sets for `:NaruServe-servlet` tests (as it does `naruserve.bootstrapJar` for `:NaruServe`). [D-363] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-8-4 SDS-AC-2] Decision: the new system property is named `naruserve.servletJar` and names the module jar.

On an embedded Jetty 9.4 `WebAppContext` started with its annotation configuration (the `jetty-webapp` and `jetty-annotations` test dependencies of CON-SVL-001), the initializer is discovered from the services file without any test code naming it; a web application with the init-parameter `naruserve.configurer` registers exactly one servlet named `naruserve` mapped to `/*`, with `isAsyncSupported() == true` and no multipart configuration, and a web application without the init-parameter registers nothing and every request is answered by the container (`404`). Residual gap: other Servlet 3.1 containers are not exercised and `docs/api/servlet.md` says so. [D-363; r4 W2-005]

The init-parameter `naruserve.urlPattern` accepts `/*`, `/` and `/api/*` (mapping the servlet accordingly) and any other value (`api/*`, `*.json`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-363]

The init-parameter `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` is an integer from 1 to 300 with default 10 and is the timeout of the `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` call that the container's destroy callback makes; any other value (`0`, `301`, `ten`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-359; D-363; I-012]

The initializer instantiates the class named by `naruserve.configurer` through its public no-argument constructor and hands it a `RestApp.Builder` that already holds a `ServletAdapter`; a missing class, a class that does not implement `ServletConfigurer`, a class without a public no-argument constructor, a `configure` that throws and a `configure` that returns `null` each make context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the class. [D-359; r4 W2-003]

The build adds the class-reference prefix `jakarta/servlet/` for `:NaruServe-servlet` to the `classRefPrefixes` closure of `build.gradle` as a separate `if (path == ':NaruServe-servlet')` branch, leaving the pinned `:NaruServe-api` prefix line of `BuildLayoutTest` unchanged, so the existing `checkClassReferences` task fails the build, naming `Class -> jakarta/servlet/...`, when a main class of `NaruServe-servlet` references it; a negative fixture proves the check fails, and `settings.gradle` includes no module for `jakarta.servlet`. records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-servlet`, package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet`, the public final class `ServletAdapter` implementing `HttpAdapter`, the public `@FunctionalInterface ServletConfigurer` with `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder builder) throws Exception`, and the public `NaruServeInitializer` implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, registered in `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, which reads the context init-parameters `naruserve.configurer`, `naruserve.urlPattern` and `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds`; the module has no `jakarta.servlet` counterpart in v1.
records.rationale: Covers D-358, D-363 (container registration and class names), wave decisions Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007), Who builds the app on the Servlet adapter (r4 W2-003) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005); answers Q-4. Measured (2026-10-20): `NaruServe-servlet/src/main` holds only `package-info.java`; `build.gradle` declares `javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket:javax.websocket-api:1.1` `compileOnly` for the module; a built `RestApp` has no adapter setter and `RestApp.Builder` takes `httpAdapter`, `jsonCodec` and `logger` (`RestApp.java:226-267`). Decision (C-07): the names are `ServletAdapter`, `ServletConfigurer`, `NaruServeInitializer` and the package-private `NaruServeServlet`; the initializer is discovered through the Servlet 3.0 service file, so an application only sets the init-parameter; `naruserve.urlPattern` defaults to `/*` and accepts `/*`, `/` or `/prefix/*`; the servlet is named `naruserve` and registered with `asyncSupported=true` and no `MultipartConfig`. Decision (C-07): the container's destroy callback calls `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` because `RestApp` has only `shutdown(long, TimeUnit)`; the timeout is `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds`, an integer from 1 to 300 with default 10 (the value `docs/api/app.md` uses; a bound exists because no limit may default to unlimited, I-012). When `naruserve.configurer` is absent the initializer does nothing, because the jar may sit in `WEB-INF/lib` of an application that does not use NaruServe. Pitfall: `@HandlesTypes` is not used, so no classpath scan runs at container start. Pitfall: `jetty-servlet` alone does not run `ServletContainerInitializer`s; the tests use a Jetty `WebAppContext` with the annotation configuration so that the services file is discovered, and containers other than Jetty 9.4 are not exercised (recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md`). Rejected alternative: a `ServletContextListener` declared in `web.xml` or by `@WebListener`; it needs the application to list it and `@WebListener` needs annotation scanning, which a jar in `WEB-INF/lib` loses when `metadata-complete=true`.

records.title: Authenticator SPI with built-in password, Bearer JWT and API key authenticators

acceptanceCriteria.text: A Kotlin lambda and a Java lambda each compile as an Authenticator and can replace the built-in password authenticator through the builder (name not final)

The built-in password authenticator returns no user for an unknown username, a wrong password, a disabled user and a service account, and (for the wrong-password and disabled users, each with a stored iteration count equal to the current target) all four cases each run exactly one target-cost PBKDF2 computation inside one slot (SEC-TOKEN-009 AC-1)
The built-in password authenticator returns the user for the correct password and passes a needed rehash to the rehash queue

The built-in Bearer authenticator accepts only access tokens (typ at+jwt under the default HS256 codec) and yields a principal id equal to the token sub; a refresh token, or a token that the configured TokenCodec (IR-TOKEN-002) fails to decode as an access token, yields no principal

Without .apiKeys(store) the API key authenticator is not installed and an Authorization: ApiKey header is treated as no credentials; with it, ApiKey-scheme requests are routed to the API key verification path
An exception thrown by a custom Authenticator is reported as 503 JSON, not as a stack trace and not as a successful login

The public API surface holds one authenticator seam (open question Q35, decided 2026-11-02): a reflection test over the public types of com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth.spi finds exactly one authenticator interface, Authenticator, whose single abstract method takes a username String and a char[] password, and no public type or Auth builder option accepts a replacement for the Bearer or the API key authenticator.

records.title: TokenCodec SPI with the default HS256 codec

acceptanceCriteria.text: NaruServe-api contains the public interface com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth.spi.TokenCodec; with no codec configured, the effective codec is the default HS256 codec and the tokens a login issues have the SEC-TOKEN-005 format (HS256 header with kid, typ at+jwt / rt+jwt, purpose-derived keys).

With a custom TokenCodec configured on the builder (option name not final; 00 §4.1 row 3 writes .tokens(TokenCodecs...), 05 §3.8 proposes .tokenCodec(codec)), a login issues the access and refresh tokens that the custom codec's encode returns, and a protected request is authenticated from the claims its decode returns; when decode throws, the request gets the same 401 invalid_token as for a bad signature (the failure reason is logged only, never in the response).

TokenCodec methods follow 05 §3.8 [INFERRED:med:advisory]: encode(claims) and decode(token, expectedType), both with non-null parameters and returns through the utils.auth.spi package's @NullMarked default (no @Nullable, and no @NonNull annotation, FR-KT-001 AC-3) and allowed to throw Exception (names and the claims type not final); the default codec's decode with expectedType access rejects a refresh token and vice versa (SEC-TOKEN-005 typ separation).

records.title: Public WebSocket API: app.ws, WebSocketHandler, WebSocketSession, listeners and app.webSocket(Configurer<WebSocketOptions>)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `ws(String path, WebSocketHandler handler)` returning the same `RestApp`, and `com.snoworca.naruserve.WebSocketHandler` is a `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Request req, WebSocketSession ws) throws Exception`; a Java test registers `app.ws("/ws/rooms/:room", (req, ws) -> ...)` and reflection confirms both signatures, and the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `ws(String,WebSocketHandler)->RestApp`. Decision: `ws` returns `RestApp` like `get`, and the callback interface is named `WebSocketHandler`. [D-294]

A path passed to `ws` follows the HTTP route pattern syntax and its registration-time validation: `app.ws("/a/:id", h)` registers and resolves `req.param("id")` in the handler, an invalid pattern throws the same exception type as `app.get` with that pattern, and `ws(null, h)` or `ws("/a", null)` throws `NullPointerException`. Decision: registration goes through the internal `Router.addWebSocket` path, which the internal `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute` hook already uses. [D-294]

`ws(...)` and `webSocket(...)` called after `listen()` throw `IllegalStateException` from the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 before the handler is recorded or the configurer runs, leaving routes and settings unchanged. [D-294; D-323] Decision: `requireConfigurable("ws")` or `requireConfigurable("webSocket")` runs first and the null checks after it, so the `IllegalStateException` wins over a null argument after `listen()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-2]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.WebSocketSession` declares `String id()`, `void sendText(String)`, `void sendBinary(byte[])`, `void sendJson(@Nullable Object)`, `void ping()`, `void close()`, `void close(int code, String reason)`, `boolean isOpen()`, `void onText(TextListener)`, `void onBinary(BinaryListener)`, `<T> void onJson(Class<T> type, JsonListener<T>)`, `void onClose(CloseListener)`, `void onError(ErrorListener)`, `void attribute(String key, @Nullable Object value)` and `<T> @Nullable T attribute(String key, Class<T> type)`, which a reflection test lists. Decision: `close()` equals `close(1000, "")`, and the attribute overloads follow the `Request.attribute` overload rule. [D-311]

The nested types `WebSocketSession.TextListener.onText(String)`, `BinaryListener.onBinary(byte[])`, `JsonListener<T>.onJson(@Nullable T value)`, `CloseListener.onClose(int code, String reason)` and `ErrorListener.onError(Throwable error)` are each annotated `@FunctionalInterface` and declare `throws Exception`, which a reflection test asserts; two listeners of one kind registered on one session both run, in registration order. [D-311]

`RestApp` declares `webSocket(Configurer<WebSocketOptions> configurer)` returning the same `RestApp`, and the public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.WebSocketOptions` declares the fluent setters `allowedOrigins(String... origins)`, `maxMessageSize(int bytes)`, `sendQueueSize(int bytes)`, `pingInterval(long time, TimeUnit unit)` and `idleTimeout(long time, TimeUnit unit)`, each returning `WebSocketOptions`; a configurer setting all five is applied, which a test reads back through the internal settings, and the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `webSocket(Configurer)->RestApp`. Decision: the configurer runs on a copy that is swapped in only after it returned, so a throwing configurer leaves every earlier setting unchanged. [D-419; D-323; D-303]

An app that never calls `webSocket` uses no configured origin allowlist, `maxMessageSize` 1048576, `sendQueueSize` 1048576, `pingInterval` 30 s and `idleTimeout` 300 s; `allowedOrigins()` with no argument resets the allowlist to that default, and a second `allowedOrigins("https://b.example")` after `allowedOrigins("https://a.example")` leaves only `https://b.example` allowed, which a test asserts. Decision: ping interval default 30 s and idle timeout default 5 min; each `allowedOrigins` call replaces the allowlist (like the `origin` option of Express `cors`). [D-303; D-323; D-419] Decision: `allowedOrigins` with a null array or a null entry throws `NullPointerException` and keeps the previous list; otherwise it stores a defensive copy in the given order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-5]

`maxMessageSize` accepts 1 to 16777216, `sendQueueSize` accepts 1 to 67108864, `pingInterval` accepts 1 s to 1 h and `idleTimeout` accepts 1 s to 24 h, all inclusive; `0`, a negative value or a value above the bound throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message has the form `<setting> must be in 1..<max>: <value>` for a size (for example `maxMessageSize must be in 1..16777216: 0`) and `<setting> must be in 1 s..<max>: <time> <unit>` for a duration (for example `pingInterval must be in 1 s..1 h: 0 SECONDS`), a `null` unit or origin entry throws `NullPointerException`, and no setting accepts a value meaning unlimited: every setting has a bounded range and a finite default (I-012). [D-419; D-323] Decision: a duration is converted with `unit.toMillis` (saturating) and compared against 1000..3600000 ms or 1000..86400000 ms, so `999 MILLISECONDS` and `Long.MAX_VALUE DAYS` are refused with the caller's own time and unit in the message. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-4]

Reflection finds no handshake-timeout setter and no pong-timeout setter on `WebSocketOptions` or `RestApp`. Decision: the handshake is bounded by the server-wide `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout`, and the pong timeout equals the ping interval. [residual: WebSocket handshake timeout (r5 W2-002)] [D-424]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.ws("/ws") { req, ws -> ws.onText { m -> ws.sendText(m) }; ws.onClose { code, reason -> } }` and `app.webSocket { o -> o.maxMessageSize(1024).pingInterval(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS) }` as SAM lambdas without a DSL, and the returned `RestApp`, `WebSocketOptions` and `ws.id()` are non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [D-294; D-311; C-03; T11]

The configurer follows IR-APP-007 and IR-MULTIPART-001 (copy swapped in after it returned); range messages follow the existing forms `<name> must be in 1..<max>: <value>` (`DefaultServerOptions.java:23`) and `<name> must be in 1 ms..1 h: <time> <unit>` (`DefaultServerOptions.java:35`), with the 1 s lower bound for WebSocket durations. Pitfall: an unlimited value would contradict I-012, so no setting accepts a value meaning unlimited and every setting has a bounded range and a finite default. Decision: each `allowedOrigins` call replaces the allowlist (Express `cors` `origin` style), although TinyHttpd's own `allowedOrigins` appends; the core does the Origin check (FR-WS-003). No handshake-timeout setting exists (residual r5 W2-002: TinyHttpd at 46b973e has no upgrade deadline, so a setting would have no effect) and no pong-timeout setting exists (D-424: pong timeout equals the ping interval). Test to re-point: the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `ws` and `webSocket` (AC-1, AC-6). Rejected alternative: `ws` returning a route builder like `route()`; reopen if per-route WebSocket middleware is requested. Rejected alternative: a listener interface with all callbacks (express-ws style `ws.on(...)`); Java SAM per event keeps Kotlin lambdas without a DSL. Express mapping: express-ws `app.ws(path, (ws, req) => ...)` with argument order reversed.

records.title: Add-only WebSocket SPI: WebSocketEndpoint, WebSocketChannel, WebSocketSettings and HttpExchange.webSocket

acceptanceCriteria.text: `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.WebSocketEndpoint` declares `void onOpen(WebSocketChannel channel)`, `void onText(String text)`, `void onBinary(byte[] data)` and `void onClose(int code, String reason)`, which a reflection test lists; the core implements it and no adapter class implements it. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: none of the four callbacks declares a checked exception, and no class under `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` or the test fixtures implements the interface. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-4]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.WebSocketChannel` declares `void sendText(String)`, `void sendBinary(byte[])`, `void ping(byte[] payload)`, `void close(int code, String reason)`, `void abort()` and `boolean isOpen()`, which a reflection test lists. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] [wave decision: Ping (r2 W2-001)] Decision: `sendText`, `sendBinary` and `ping` declare `IOException`; `close`, `abort` and `isOpen` declare no checked exception. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-3]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.WebSocketSettings` exposes the configured message limit in bytes and the ping interval, and the core builds it from the `WebSocketOptions` of IR-WS-001; a test reads back a non-default `maxMessageSize` 4096 and `pingInterval` 2 s from the settings passed to `webSocket`. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] [D-419; D-423] Decision: `WebSocketSettings` is a final class with the public constructor `(int maxMessageBytes, long pingIntervalMillis)` and, besides it, only the getters `maxMessageBytes(): int` and `pingIntervalMillis(): long`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-6]

`HttpExchange` declares `default void webSocket(WebSocketSettings settings, WebSocketEndpoint endpoint) throws IOException`, and calling it on an exchange class that does not override it throws `UnsupportedOperationException`; the method returns only after the connection has closed. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: the message is `webSocket is not supported by this adapter` and the exchange is not touched. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-5]

A signature comparison test finds every method of every type of `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` present at the wave 6 close (`9ce5cc4`; the SPI is unchanged since `40b9665`), namely `AppFactory`, `ErrorRenderer`, `ExchangeHandler`, `HttpAdapter`, `HttpExchange`, `JsonCodec`, `ServerSettings`, `StreamDrain` and `UpgradeHandler`, unchanged, with `webSocket` the only added `HttpExchange` method and `attach(OutputStream)` the only added `StreamDrain` method (the SSE hand-over of IR-HTTP-007 AC-4). Deviation (recorded): D-106 reads "without changing the SPI"; wave 7 adds types and `default` methods only, read as "without breaking the SPI"; W2-001's "one default method" becomes two with `StreamDrain.attach`, still add-only. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)]

When `webSocket` refuses a handshake before `101` it throws a NaruServe `HttpException` carrying the status and headers of the rejection and leaves the exchange unstarted, so the dispatcher's error path then calls `commit(...)` on that exchange without an `IllegalStateException` and the client receives the rejection status; the exchange is marked started only once `101` has been written. [wave decision: Start state on a refused handshake (r2 W2-002)]

No class under `com.snoworca.naruserve` in `NaruServe-api` or `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` parses or writes WebSocket frames: a source scan finds no frame-opcode or masking-key handling, and the TinyHttpd upgrade class delegates framing to `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd.websocket`. [D-302] Decision: the scan reads every `.java` file under `NaruServe-api/src/main` and `NaruServe-tinyhttpd/src/main` and fails on the words `opcode` or `masking` in any case. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-10]

The test-fixture `InMemoryHttpAdapter` exchange overrides `webSocket`, records the settings and endpoint, calls `onOpen` with an in-memory `WebSocketChannel` that records sent text, binary, ping and close calls, and lets a test inject text, binary and close events; a core test uses it to open a session and receive a recorded `sendText`. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: the in-memory exchange marks itself started with status `101`, calls `onOpen` on its worker thread, delivers queued peer events from that thread in order and returns only after `onClose` ran. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-7] Decision: `close(code, reason)` is recorded and echoed by the peer so `onClose` gets `(code, reason)`; `abort()` sets aborted and delivers `onClose(1006, "")`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-8]

records.requirement: The system shall extend the `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` package for WebSocket only by adding the types `WebSocketEndpoint`, `WebSocketChannel` and `WebSocketSettings` and the `default` method `HttpExchange.webSocket(WebSocketSettings, WebSocketEndpoint)`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` unless an adapter overrides it, beside which wave 7 adds only the SSE `default` method `StreamDrain.attach(OutputStream)` of IR-HTTP-007, so that an adapter supplies RFC 6455 framing and the core owns every WebSocket callback without any existing SPI signature changing.
records.rationale:
Covers wave decision WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001; D-106, D-302, D-429, D-435, D-444, D-419, D-423), Ping (r2 W2-001; D-309, D-311), Start state on a refused handshake (r2 W2-002, SPI part) and D-302 (no NaruServe frame codec). Deviation note: D-106 says the upgrade extension point works "without changing the SPI"; the wave reads it as "without breaking it" (add-only types and one default method), which `docs/api` records; IR-HTTP-007 (the successor of IR-HTTP-004 in the HTTP scope) restates the SPI-surface AC accordingly. Measured: `spi/HttpExchange.java:85` declares `upgrade(List<Map.Entry<String,String>>, UpgradeHandler)` and `:89` `eventStream(...)`; the existing raw `upgrade` stays for raw upgrades and keeps its signature. Pitfall: putting TinyHttpd's `WebSocket`/`WebSocketListener` types on the SPI would leak an engine type into the core (CON constraints of wave 1); rejected. Rejected alternative: driving WebSocket through the raw `UpgradeHandler` and a NaruServe frame codec; contradicts D-302, reopen never in v1. The in-memory test adapter implements `webSocket` so core-level tests of FR-WS-001, FR-WS-003, FR-WS-006, FR-WS-007 and FR-WS-009 run without sockets.
- [2026-10-20] Correction (feasibility F-03/F-05): the SPI now gains two default methods, HttpExchange.webSocket and StreamDrain.attach (committee decision B-1), replacing the earlier "one default method" wording. AC-5's signature test names StreamDrain.attach, which IR-HTTP-007 AC-4 owns; IR-HTTP-007 depends_on this requirement, so the two are built and verified together as one group (no reverse edge, to keep the graph acyclic).

records.title: Doctor checks for API keys

acceptanceCriteria.text: The MULTI_INSTANCE key fixture of AC-7 with only the ApiKeyStore changed to a custom store whose `supportsAtomicLimitInsert()` is false (the UserStore still returns true from `supportsAtomicFieldWrites()`): `build()` succeeds, then doctor reports a FAIL naming `supportsAtomicLimitInsert` and no FAIL naming `supportsAtomicFieldWrites`, and the app does not start.

`.allowAdminScopesOnApiKeys(true)`: doctor WARN at each start containing the persistence-of-effects text (proposed: `API keys may hold auth-* admin scopes; role grants and reactivations made by a key persist after the key is deleted. Review audit events by apiKeyId.`).
Opt-in off, store with three `*` keys and one `auth-users:read` key: doctor WARN reports count 1.
Opt-in off, store returning -1: no start-time count WARN; two different keys whose `auth-*` scopes are ignored within one minute produce one WARN containing only the first key id.
`SINGLE_INSTANCE` with a store whose `supportsAtomicLimitInsert()` is false: no FAIL for that check.

The `.allowAdminScopesOnApiKeys` Javadoc states the same lasting-effects risk as the AC-2 WARN (role grants and reactivations made by a key persist after the key is deleted; review audit events by apiKeyId) (00 R47 (5)); a docs test reads the Javadoc of the builder method and asserts that sentence is present.

MULTI_INSTANCE key fixture (used by AC-1 here and by SEC-APIKEY-006 AC-4, SEC-APIKEY-011 AC-7, IR-APIKEY-003 AC-5 and REL-APIKEY-003 AC-5): `deployment(MULTI_INSTANCE)` and `.apiKeys(store)`, with every store that FR-AUTH-003 AC-3 requires shared (app-provided test implementations that are not built-in in-memory or file stores, for users, refresh tokens, throttle, device trust and API keys, and for groups when configured), where the UserStore returns true from `supportsAtomicFieldWrites()` (the test fake declares it, REL-IAM-003 AC-5) and the ApiKeyStore returns true from `supportsAtomicLimitInsert()` (the test fake declares it). With this fixture `build()` succeeds, doctor reports no FAIL naming `supportsAtomicFieldWrites` (REL-IAM-003 AC-1) or `supportsAtomicLimitInsert` (AC-1), and the app starts.

[SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-10 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: doctor startup check suite and proxy-trust warnings

acceptanceCriteria.text: A doctor report lists every finding with its level FAIL or WARN and a message; with at least one FAIL, RestApp start fails before the port is bound and the exception message names each FAIL; with only WARNs start continues and each WARN is logged once.

The suite covers at least: store connectivity, secret strength, public path list, pre-install middleware list (R28), registration enabled, measured hash cost on this device, clock, proxy trust (R32), deployment vs stores (R35), null-password .user (R41), file state (R42), errors() placement (R30), cookie-mode WebSocket wildcard origin (R40), WebSocket wrapper count vs WEBSOCKET registrations (R40), UserStore.supportsAtomicFieldWrites (R37), ApiKeyStore.supportsAtomicLimitInsert, admin-scope key counts, admin-scope opt-in and LoginThrottle.usesLimitArguments (R47). A table-driven test sets up, for each item with a trigger, the configuration that makes that item report (one app per item, or per group of compatible items; the cookie-mode WebSocket origin item in COOKIE mode; the admin-scope key-count item with .allowAdminScopesOnApiKeys false and the admin-scope opt-in item with it true, in separate apps) and asserts that the item's FAIL or WARN appears in that app's doctor report (for a FAIL item, also named in the start exception message of AC-1). Triggers 00 does not give are taken from 04 §6.2 [INFERRED:med:advisory]: store connectivity = findByUsername("__naru_probe__") throwing gives FAIL; registration enabled = .register(true) in PROD gives WARN; clock = a TimeSource earlier than the module build-date floor (a fixed date at or before the release build, currently 2025-01-01T00:00Z) gives WARN. Secret strength appears only in DEV (in PROD a weak key is the build() AuthConfigException of SEC-AUTH-001 AC-2 to AC-4, so no doctor runs); whether its DEV WARN is emitted by build() or by doctor is an open question, so the test asserts only the WARN of SEC-AUTH-001 AC-8. The public path list item is a listing: the test asserts that the report lists the permitted paths and asserts no FAIL or WARN for it. The measured hash cost item is asserted to be present with the measured time; its FAIL or WARN threshold is an open question (00 R41 implies a PROD FAIL, 04 §6.2 gives a WARN over 1 s or under 100,000 iterations), so no level is asserted for it here.

PROD with legacy trustProxy(true) is doctor FAIL; MULTI_INSTANCE with no proxy trust configured is doctor WARN; hop mode (trustProxyHops) under MULTI_INSTANCE or STRICT is doctor WARN recommending CIDR mode.

With no proxy trust configured, the first request carrying X-Forwarded-For logs exactly one runtime WARN telling to set trustProxyHops because all users share the LB IP; later such requests log nothing more.

The two R40 WebSocket items named in AC-2 report the levels FR-FLOW-008 AC-5 (cookie-mode origin: WARN while C5 is absent) and AC-6 (wrapper count: WARN) specify; FR-FLOW-008 owns those checks and this block only requires that they run inside this doctor report.

Under SINGLE_INSTANCE, with a custom UserStore and any of the refresh, throttle or device-trust storage left unset (in-memory fallback, R42), the doctor report holds exactly one WARN stating that a restart logs every user out, however many of the three fall back; with all three set, or with InMemoryUserStore or FileUserStore, no such WARN. Under MULTI_INSTANCE the same set-up makes build() fail instead (FR-AUTH-003 AC-3, FR-TOKEN-002 AC-6; 00 R35 x R42). FR-TOKEN-002 AC-3 and REL-FLOW-001 AC-5 defer to this AC.

records.title: TinyHttpd composite build through a Gradle property

records.title: Wave 5 cookie decisions recorded in docs/api and their markers removed

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/cookie.md` states that `getMaxAge()` defaults to `-1`, that every negative value omits `Max-Age` (a session cookie), that `0` deletes and that a positive value is seconds, with its reason (the Servlet `Cookie` model), and the `getMaxAge()` row has no (미확정) marker. [D-208; I-013]

`docs/api/cookie.md` states that v1 writes no `Expires` attribute (lifetimes use `Max-Age`) and has no signed cookies (an app signs values itself, for example with an HMAC in middleware), each with its reason, and the `Expires` marker line is gone. [D-208; I-013]

`docs/api/cookie.md` states that NaruServe neither encodes nor decodes cookie values, unlike Express's `res.cookie`, that an app encodes other characters itself (for example with `URLEncoder`), that request cookies with an invalid name or without `=` are skipped instead of failing the request, and that `res.addCookie` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an invalid name or value. [wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; D-205]
The `cookie-parser` row of `docs/api/express-migration.md` states that signed cookies and automatic value encoding are not provided in v1 instead of carrying a (미확정) marker. [D-208]

The Java blocks of `docs/api/cookie.md` are compiled by the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 with no skip entry whose reason is `Cookie`, `req.cookie`, `req.getCookies` or `res.addCookie`, and a docs test fails when `docs/api/cookie.md` contains a (미확정) marker. [I-008; I-009]

records.title: request.md and app.md document the raw request API: bodyStream and its limits, the two over-limit forms for onError, headerNames, rawHeaders, isFromTrustedProxy, rawBodyLimit and the 0.12.0 compatibility changes

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/request.md` documents `req.bodyStream()` and `req.bodyStream(maxBytes)` with their Express counterparts (the `req` stream, and `express.raw({ limit })` for a per-route limit): the raw body as received, an empty non-null stream without a body, the one-read rule with `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` against `body(...)`, `form(...)` and `parts()`, the repeated-call rule, that `bodyStream()` uses `rawBodyLimit` and `bodyStream(maxBytes)` takes `1..1073741824` or throws `IllegalArgumentException`, and that the framework cleans up an unclosed stream, with a Java and a Kotlin example.

`docs/api/request.md` states that an over-limit body read through `bodyStream` arrives in two forms, `HttpException` with status 413 when the declared `Content-Length` exceeds the limit (thrown by the `bodyStream` call before any byte is read) and `BodyTooLargeException` from the stream while reading a body without a declared length, that an `onError` handler that wants to recognise an over-limit body must check both forms, that an unwrapped `BodyTooLargeException` leaving the handler becomes a 413 response, and that one wrapped in another exception is handled as an ordinary exception.

`docs/api/request.md` documents `req.headerNames()` as the counterpart of Express `Object.keys(req.headers)` and `req.rawHeaders()` as the counterpart of Express `req.rawHeaders`: lowercase names and name-value pairs in the order the adapter reported, case and duplicates kept by `rawHeaders()`, both results unmodifiable (`UnsupportedOperationException`), and the servlet adapter grouping values by name in the container's enumeration order, with a Java and a Kotlin example.

`docs/api/request.md` documents `req.isFromTrustedProxy()` with its Express counterpart `app.get('trust proxy fn')(req.socket.remoteAddress, 0)` and the result table of the request (no trust setting, `trustProxyHops(0)` and an empty `trustProxyCidrs()` give `false`; `trustProxyHops(n)` with n ≥ 1 and the legacy `trustProxy(true)` give `true`; `trustProxyCidrs(...)` gives `true` only when the direct peer lies inside a listed CIDR), with a Java and a Kotlin example.

records.title: response.md documents the raw response API: res.append, res.onAbort with the custom-adapter limit, res.relay and HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/response.md` documents `res.append(name, value)` with its Express counterpart `res.append`: it adds a header line and returns the `Response`, it applies the same name and value check as `res.header`, and `res.header` keeps replacing a header of the same name (Express `res.set`), with a Java and a Kotlin example that sends two `Set-Cookie` lines.

`docs/api/response.md` documents `res.onAbort(listener)`: it returns `void`, a `null` listener throws `NullPointerException`, the listener runs once when the client disconnects or the app calls `res.abort` and never for a response that completed normally, a listener registered after the abort runs at once, a listener may run on a thread other than the request thread, an exception of one listener does not stop the others, and an adapter may report a disconnect during idle time only at the next I/O; with its Express counterpart (`res.on('close')` with a check that the response did not finish) and a Java and a Kotlin example.

`docs/api/response.md` states that the SPI default of `HttpExchange.onAbort` checks its argument and does nothing, so with a custom `HttpAdapter` whose exchange does not override it an `onAbort` listener may never be called when the client disconnects, while the TinyHttpd and servlet adapters report disconnects.

`docs/api/response.md` documents `res.relay(in, contentLength)` and how it differs from `res.stream(in, contentType)`: it adds or changes no `Content-Type`, sends only the headers set before it besides `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`, applies no `defaultCache`, sends exactly `contentLength` bytes for a length of 0 or more and aborts when the stream ends early, sends with an undetermined length for -1, throws `IllegalArgumentException` below -1, keeps a non-negative length as `Content-Length` without a body for HEAD and 304, sends neither body nor `Content-Length` for 204, and owns the stream as `res.stream` does; with its Express counterpart or a statement that Express has none, and a Java and a Kotlin example.

`docs/api/response.md` documents `HttpHeaderValues.isFieldValue(value)` in `com.snoworca.naruserve.common` as the value half of the header check that `res.header` and `res.append` apply, next to the existing `HttpHeaderValues.isToken` for names: `true` for an empty string and for HTAB, `false` for CR, LF, NUL, DEL and any character above U+00FF; with its Express counterpart or a statement that Express has none, and a Java and a Kotlin example.

`docs/api/en/response.md` states the same facts as the Korean page for every item of AC-1 to AC-5, every Java block added to the two pages compiles in `DocsExamplesCompileTest` or sits on its skip list with a reason, and every Kotlin block added has exactly one compiled and run marker that `KotlinDocsMarkersTest` accepts.

`docs/api/response.md` and its English mirror state that on a `304` response `res.relay` hands its length to the adapter and the client sees that `Content-Length` only where the adapter writes it: TinyHttpd 3.1.1 omits it (allowed by RFC 9110 §8.6), the servlet adapter hands it to the container, and a `HEAD` response keeps it on every built-in adapter.
