records.requirement: The system shall, after `app.trustProxyHops(n)` with n ≥ 1, treat the direct socket peer as trusted and make `req.remoteAddress()` return the nth entry from the right of the request's `X-Forwarded-For` entries, so that an entry a client places on the left cannot become the client address, with the decision made in the core request object for every adapter.
records.rationale: 00 §8 C6b ("`X-Forwarded-For`를 오른쪽에서 n홉 ... 해석", required; "이 결함은 auth와 무관하게 Core 전체의 보안 문제다") and R32 (hop mode trusts the socket peer when n ≥ 1; precondition that the node is reachable only through the load balancer, 7th edition Q-5). §6.4 row "R32 × R33": with `trustProxyHops(1)` behind a TLS-terminating LB the IP limit uses the real client IP. R34 IP limits consume this address.
records.research:
- Decisive fact: `ProxyTrust.remoteAddress` takes the left-most entry of only the first `X-Forwarded-For` header (`ProxyTrust.java:6-7`, L17-L20); the left-most entry is whatever the client sent, so under `trustProxy(true)` a client can pick any address (06 S4 (b): IP limits become unbounded). Counting from the right takes the entries the trusted proxies appended.
- Reopen of FR-ENGINE-008's rejected alternative: its rationale rejected hop counting "reopen if a deployment needs hop counting". 00 §8 reopens it because the left-most rule is a Core-wide security defect independent of auth (any app doing IP limits or audit behind a proxy is spoofable); `trustProxy(boolean)` stays unchanged for compatibility.
- Decision: combine all `X-Forwarded-For` lines (HTTP field-line combination) before counting from the right. Pitfall: reading only the first line, as today, lets a client add its own first line while the proxy's appended value sits in a later line.
- Hop-mode precondition (R32 7th edition Q-5): a client that reaches the node directly can forge both XFF and XFP; this is a documented mandatory condition (IR-ENGINE-003 AC-7), and auth's doctor recommends CIDR mode for `MULTI_INSTANCE`/`STRICT` (auth scope).
- Open (00 silent): the result when there are fewer than n entries, and blank or malformed entries; decide during implementation (fail toward the socket peer or the left-most entry) and document.
- Rejected alternative: interpreting `Forwarded` (RFC 7239). FR-ENGINE-008 AC-3 keeps it unread in v1, as Express; reopen with that requirement.
records.implementationNotes:
- Replace or extend `internal/ProxyTrust.java` (L1-L38) with a resolver that takes the immutable trust setting, the socket address and all `X-Forwarded-For` lines (`req.headers("X-Forwarded-For")`); call it from `DefaultRequest.remoteAddress()` (L486-L500).
- Both request-construction sites in `Dispatcher` (L214 and L263-L266) must pass the new setting instead of the boolean.
- Extend `ProxyTrustAcceptanceTest` and `NaruServe-tinyhttpd/.../CrossAdapterTest`.

records.title: CIDR mode: after app.trustProxyCidrs(...), a trusted peer's req.remoteAddress() is the first X-Forwarded-For entry from the right outside the trusted CIDRs

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`, peer `10.0.0.1` and `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.2`, `req.remoteAddress()` is `203.0.113.7` (the trusted `10.0.0.2` is skipped).

With the same setting, peer `198.51.100.20` (outside `10.0.0.0/8`) and `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7`, `req.remoteAddress()` is `198.51.100.20` and `req.isSecure()` is the adapter value: an untrusted peer's forwarding headers are ignored.
Spoofing is defeated: with peer `10.0.0.1` and `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 203.0.113.7`, `req.remoteAddress()` is `203.0.113.7`, not the client-supplied left entry `1.2.3.4`.

IPv6 works: with `app.trustProxyCidrs("fd00::/8")`, peer `fd00::1` and `X-Forwarded-For: 2001:db8::5`, `req.remoteAddress()` is `2001:db8::5`; several CIDRs (`"10.0.0.0/8", "fd00::/8"`) are each honoured.
Several `X-Forwarded-For` lines are combined in arrival order before the right-to-left scan, as in hop mode.

The in-memory adapter and the TinyHttpd adapter give identical results for the same CIDR setting, peer and headers, and no adapter class reads `X-Forwarded-*` itself (FR-ENGINE-008 AC-4 extended to CIDR mode).

Trusted peer without X-Forwarded-For: with `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")` and peer `10.0.0.1`, a request with no `X-Forwarded-For` header has `req.remoteAddress()` = `10.0.0.1`, and a request whose only forwarding header is `Forwarded: for=198.51.100.1;proto=https` (no `X-Forwarded-*`) has `req.remoteAddress()` = `10.0.0.1` and `req.isSecure()` equal to the adapter value (`false` on `InMemoryHttpAdapter(..., false)`): `Forwarded` is not read in CIDR mode (as FR-ENGINE-008 AC-3 for legacy trust and SEC-ENGINE-001 AC-4/AC-5 for hop mode; the isSecure() value matches SEC-ENGINE-003 AC-6).

records.rationale: 00 §8 C6b ("신뢰 CIDR 밖의 첫 주소로 해석", required) and R32 ("CIDR 모드는 소켓 주소가 신뢰 CIDR 안일 때 신뢰한다"). records.research:
- Decisive fact: in CIDR mode the trust decision depends on the real socket address, so a client that reaches the node directly (outside the trusted ranges) cannot forge XFF/XFP; this is the stronger mode for multi-node deployments (R32 Q-5).

- Open (00 silent): the result when every XFF entry lies inside the trusted CIDRs; whether an IPv4-mapped IPv6 peer (`::ffff:10.0.0.1`) matches an IPv4 CIDR; malformed XFF entries. Decide during implementation and document; listed in the open questions of this run.

records.title: X-Forwarded-Proto rule for req.isSecure() in hop and CIDR modes, read only from a trusted peer and failing closed on ambiguous lists

acceptanceCriteria.text: Single value: with `app.trustProxyHops(1)`, a trusted peer on a non-TLS exchange and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, `req.isSecure()` is `true`; with `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` it is `false`; with `app.trustProxyHops(2)`, `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.9, 203.0.113.7` and the single value `https` it is `true`.

Hop mode list: with `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.9, 203.0.113.7` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https, http`, `app.trustProxyHops(2)` gives `true` (second from the right) and `app.trustProxyHops(1)` gives `false` (first from the right).

CIDR mode list: with `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`, peer `10.0.0.1`, `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.2` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https, http`, the first untrusted entry is second from the right, so `req.isSecure()` is `true`.
Fail closed on count mismatch: with `app.trustProxyHops(1)`, `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.9, 203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.2` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https, https`, `req.isSecure()` is `false`.
Fail closed on a missing position: with `app.trustProxyHops(3)`, `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.9, 203.0.113.7` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https, https`, `req.isSecure()` is `false`.

Untrusted peer: with `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`, peer `198.51.100.20` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, and with `app.trustProxyHops(0)` and the same header, `req.isSecure()` is the adapter's value (`false` on `InMemoryHttpAdapter(..., false)`); a trusted peer without any `X-Forwarded-Proto` also keeps the adapter's value.
The in-memory adapter and the TinyHttpd adapter give identical `isSecure()` results for the same setting, peer and headers.

WebSocket upgrade requests use the same trust setting as ordinary HTTP requests (both request-construction sites in `Dispatcher` pass it, 00 §8 C6b, R33 (a), R40): for an upgrade request with `app.trustProxyHops(1)`, peer `10.0.0.1`, `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, middleware before 101 reads `req.remoteAddress()` = `203.0.113.7` and `req.isSecure()` = `true`; the same holds under `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`; the results equal those of the same headers on an ordinary HTTP request.

records.requirement: The system shall, in hop and CIDR modes, read `X-Forwarded-Proto` for `req.isSecure()` only when the direct socket peer is trusted; a single value is used as is, several values are resolved by position (hop mode: the nth from the right; CIDR mode: the position, counted from the right, of the first untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` entry), and when there are two or more values whose count differs from the `X-Forwarded-For` count, or the position does not exist, `req.isSecure()` is `false`.
records.rationale: 00 §8 C6b ("`X-Forwarded-Proto`는 R32의 규칙으로 해석") and R32 (6th edition P-4 replacing the 5th-edition rule; 7th edition Q-6 fail-closed). R33 (a) accepts an auth request in PROD when `req.isSecure()` is true through direct TLS or a C6b-trusted proxy's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`; a spoofed `https` would let credentials travel in plain text, so the rule fails closed.
records.research:
- Decisive facts (R32): XFP is read only when the socket peer is trusted (hop mode: n ≥ 1; CIDR mode: socket inside a trusted CIDR). One XFP item is the usual case where the proxy overwrites the header (nginx `$scheme`, AWS ALB); several items are matched by position to the XFF entry that was chosen as the client; two or more items with a different count than XFF, or a missing position, give `false` (Q-6).
- Pitfall: a proxy that passes XFP through without overwriting it cannot be told apart from a client-supplied value; this is documented as an unsupported setup (IR-ENGINE-003 AC-7), not detected.
- Decision: the position in CIDR mode is the 1-based index from the right of the first untrusted XFF entry, applied to XFP counted from the right (R32 wording "오른쪽부터 센 같은 위치").
- Open (00 silent): case-insensitive comparison of `https` (the legacy rule compares case-insensitively, FR-ENGINE-008 AC-2) and how several XFP header lines combine; decide during implementation, keeping fail-closed behaviour for anything ambiguous.
- Rejected alternative: the 5th-edition rule (replaced by P-4); reopen never, R32 is final.
records.implementationNotes:
- Same resolver as the hop and CIDR requirements; `DefaultRequest.isSecure()` (L486-L500) calls it with all `X-Forwarded-Proto` lines and the position chosen by the address resolution.
- Legacy `trustProxy(true)` keeps `ProxyTrust.isSecure` first-value behaviour (FR-ENGINE-008 AC-2); this rule applies only to hop and CIDR modes.
- WebSocket Origin checks use `req.isSecure()` (`WebSocketUpgrade.java:90`); the new rule flows there unchanged.

records.requirement: In PROD mode the auth middleware shall process an authenticated request or any of the eight credential endpoints only when req.isSecure() is true or the request is local (req.socketAddress() is a loopback address and no X-Forwarded-* or Forwarded header is present), and shall otherwise answer 403 insecure_transport before reading any credential; public paths shall be exempt and handled as anonymous without reading a token.
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R33 (editions 5, 8, 10, 21, 24, 26, 29) makes transport security a per-request decision instead of a bind-address decision (R21 withdrawn); §6.4 rows "R33 × 로그인", "R47 × 평문과 헤더 둘", "R29 × R33" and "R32 × R33" fix the outcomes.
records.research: - Decisive facts: "local" means loopback socket address AND zero proxy headers (X-Forwarded-*, Forwarded); a TLS-terminating LB passes through C6b trust (trustProxyHops/trustProxyCidrs) alone. The check is the very first step, before multiple-credential parsing (26th ed.), so a plain-text request never gets 400 invalid_request. Credential endpoints are never public paths even if listed in .permit (8th ed., S-3). Pitfall: when v2 adds self password reset or email verification endpoints they must be added to the credential-endpoint list, otherwise reset tokens travel over plain text as anonymous public requests (10th ed.). Residual risk (K-12): a same-host proxy that adds no headers makes every request look local; docs make the recommended proxy config a mandatory step and /auth/setup independently requires the one-time setup token (AUTH scope). Rejected: R21 bind-address check - reopen only if C5 lands and a deployment cannot send proxy headers.

records.title: Credential endpoint classes: anonymous-entry and subject-required

acceptanceCriteria.text: BOTH, POST /auth/refresh with an expired Authorization: Bearer token and a valid naru_rt cookie (matching X-CSRF-Token, same-origin Origin) -> 200; the expired JWT is read and ignored and no 401 invalid_token is sent. COOKIE, the same request with an expired naru_at cookie instead of the Bearer token -> 200.
POST /auth/login with an expired Bearer token and valid credentials -> 200 regular login; no 401 invalid_token.
POST /auth/login, /auth/register, /auth/setup and /auth/refresh carrying a valid access token -> the handler sees no principal (auth.userOrNull(req) returns null).

POST /auth/password with an expired Bearer token -> 401, code invalid_token, header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"; the handler does not run. With API keys enabled, POST /auth/me/apikeys with the same token and POST /auth/admin/apikeys with a bad-signature Bearer give the same 401 with ", ApiKey" appended to the challenge.

On an anonymous-entry endpoint, two Authorization headers -> 400 invalid_request, and with API keys enabled (.apiKeys(store)) a valid API-key Authorization header on POST /auth/refresh -> 403 api_key_not_allowed; multiple credentials (SEC-FLOW-004, except two or more naru_at cookies in COOKIE or BOTH mode, which count as no access cookie) and the key procedure are the only credential judgments on anonymous-entry endpoints that follow protected-path rules. With API keys enabled (.apiKeys(store)), an API-key header is still authenticated by the key procedure first, so a wrong key on POST /auth/refresh -> 401 invalid_api_key (owned by SEC-APIKEY-004 AC-2). Without .apiKeys(store) the key-scheme header is no credential (IR-TOKEN-001 AC-5) and the request is decided by its refresh token alone (FR-FLOW-005 statement; with no refresh token, FR-FLOW-005 AC-4).

With .permitPrefix("/auth") configured, POST /auth/password with an expired Bearer token still -> 401 invalid_token, and POST /auth/login with two Authorization headers still -> 400 invalid_request. The two key endpoints are judged the same way under a permit that covers them (00 R29 29th edition: credential endpoints are judged independently of .permit, and the three subject-required endpoints are judged exactly like protected paths and not passed to the handler). HEADER mode, .apiKeys(store), over a secure or local connection, Content-Type: application/json and the body {}: (a) with .permitPrefix("/auth"), POST /auth/me/apikeys with an expired Bearer token -> 401 code invalid_token with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", ApiKey, and with no credential (no Authorization header, no cookies) -> 401 code unauthenticated with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, ApiKey; (b) with .permit(Method.POST, "/auth/admin/apikeys"), the same two requests to POST /auth/admin/apikeys get the same two responses; in every case of (a) and (b) the handler does not run and no key is issued.

With .mountPath("/api/auth") (FR-AUTH-005) the classes follow the configured mount path: (a) PROD with .permitPrefix("/api/auth"), a plain-text non-local POST /api/auth/login -> 403 insecure_transport and the login handler does not run (00 R33: credential endpoints are never public paths); (b) HEADER over a local connection, POST /api/auth/refresh with an expired Authorization: Bearer token and a valid JSON body refreshToken -> 200, with no 401 invalid_token; (c) HEADER over a local connection, POST /api/auth/password with an expired Bearer token -> 401 invalid_token with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", and the handler does not run.

Access cookie on a subject-required endpoint and a protected path (00 R29 29th edition: expired or invalid Bearer and cookie access tokens are 401 invalid_token there). COOKIE mode, API keys disabled, over a secure or local connection, no Authorization header: (a) POST /auth/password with a well-formed JSON body, a same-origin Origin, naru_csrf and X-CSRF-Token both built from the cookie token's sub and fam, and only an expired naru_at -> 401 code invalid_token with header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", and the handler does not run (changePassword is not called); (b) the same request with a naru_at whose signature is altered -> the same 401 invalid_token response and the handler does not run; (c) the expired naru_at of (a) on a protected GET /api/x -> 401 invalid_token with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token" (IR-FLOW-001 statement), not 401 unauthenticated with a plain Bearer challenge, and the route does not run.

No credential on a subject-required endpoint (00 R29 29th edition, replacing the 28th edition's "a handler that needs a subject answers 401 itself": the three subject-required endpoints are judged exactly like protected paths and the request is not passed to the handler; §6.4 row "R47 × 자격 증명 없음 코드" for the challenge with keys on). HEADER mode, API keys disabled, over a secure or local connection, no Authorization header and no cookies: POST /auth/password with Content-Type: application/json and the body {} (no current-password field) -> 401 code unauthenticated with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer (no error attribute), not 400, and the handler does not run (changePassword is not called and no password hash runs); the same request with .permitPrefix("/auth") configured -> the same 401 unauthenticated. With .apiKeys(store), POST /auth/me/apikeys and POST /auth/admin/apikeys with Content-Type: application/json, the body {} and no credential -> 401 code unauthenticated with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, ApiKey, and neither handler runs (no key is issued).

The /auth prefix here is the default mount path; the account endpoints are classified under the configured mount path (.mountPath(String), FR-AUTH-005), and the admin endpoint is classified where auth.adminRoutes() is mounted (whether that follows a configured mount path is open).
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R29 (editions 27–30) and R33 (29th edition list of eight credential endpoints); R47 (1). §6.4 rows "R29 × 자격 증명 엔드포인트의 만료 토큰", "R29 × 자격 증명 엔드포인트의 키와 헤더 둘", "R29 × 주체 필요 자격 증명 엔드포인트의 만료 토큰".
records.research: - Ground truth: the credential-endpoint list in R33 is the single list (8 entries); R29 and R47 (1) refer to it. Anonymous-entry endpoints judge only two things like protected paths: multiple credentials (400 invalid_request) and the API-key procedure (401 invalid_api_key, 403 api_key_not_allowed); expired or invalid JWT and access cookies are ignored. The single exception is logout?all=true with tokens but no valid one (401 invalid_token; no tokens -> 401 unauthenticated). A valid access token is used as identity only by logout. Rejected alternatives: 27th ed. "credentials make anonymous-entry endpoints protected" - broke refresh for clients whose access token had expired; 28th ed. "subject-needing handlers answer 401 themselves" - clients got a handler 401 instead of invalid_token and could not tell that they should refresh; attaching a valid access cookie as principal on login - would make CSRF depend on access cookie state.
records.implementationNotes: - Endpoint classification is a fixed table inside the auth middleware keyed by method + path under the mount path (utils.auth); it is consulted before the public-path matcher (AUTH scope) so .permit cannot reclassify. API-key handling inside the chain is APIKEY scope.

COOKIE, protected GET /api/x with a valid naru_at and a Bearer token -> authenticated by naru_at (200), not 400.

BOTH, protected GET /api/x with a valid Bearer token and a valid naru_at -> 400 invalid_request. COOKIE, two naru_at cookies: POST /api/posts -> 400 invalid_request; GET /health with .permit("/health") -> anonymous 200; POST /auth/password -> 400 invalid_request; POST /auth/refresh with one valid naru_rt, its matching X-CSRF-Token and a same-origin Origin -> judged by the refresh cookie (200), not 400; POST /auth/login with a same-origin Origin and valid credentials -> regular login (200), not 400; POST /auth/logout treats them as no access cookie (owned by SEC-FLOW-010 AC-8).

[INFERRED:med:advisory] (05 §1 item 7; 00 is silent on the default), and the auth middleware shall read access credentials according to the effective TokenTransport (HEADER reads only Authorization: Bearer, COOKIE reads only the naru_at cookie, BOTH reads both and treats their co-presence as multiple credentials), shall treat unread credentials as absent, shall, when .apiKeys(store) is set, read the configured API-key scheme header in every mode (without .apiKeys(store) such a header is no credential, IR-TOKEN-001 AC-5), shall treat two or more Authorization headers as multiple credentials in every mode, whatever their schemes (00 R29 (g), R47 (1)), and shall answer 400 invalid_request for multiple credentials on protected paths and credential endpoints while treating them as anonymous on public paths, except that the five anonymous-entry endpoints (login, register, setup, refresh, logout) treat two or more naru_at cookies as no access cookie instead of answering 400 (00 R29 (d), edition 33).
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R29 (g) edition 33 (per-mode reading follows the access location table of 05 §7) and R29 (d) editions 32–33 for duplicate naru_at; R47 (1) for duplicate Authorization headers and API key with naru_at; §6.4 rows "R29 × 모드별 자격 증명", "R29 × access·CSRF 쿠키 겹침", "R29 × 익명 진입의 access 쿠키 겹침".
records.research: - Ground truth (33rd ed.): a credential the mode does not read is absent, so it never produces 400 multiple credentials nor 401 invalid_token; up to 32nd ed. COOKIE-mode Bearer was unspecified. Authorization is not a list header (RFC 9110 §5.3), so two headers are always multiple credentials regardless of mode. Duplicate naru_at (cookies planted with other Path/Domain) is multiple access credentials on protected paths and subject-required endpoints, but the five anonymous-entry endpoints treat it as no access cookie so re-login and logout can repair the browser state (33rd ed.). Pitfall: a proxy that merges two Authorization headers into one comma-joined line is seen as one malformed credential -> 401 (invalid_token for Bearer, invalid_api_key for the key scheme), not 400; this is fail-closed and accepted (R47 (1), 23rd ed.). naru_rt is not an access credential (R47 (1)), so it never counts toward multiple credentials.
records.implementationNotes: - Credential extraction step of the auth middleware (utils.auth), after the transport check (SEC-FLOW-001). Use req.headers("Authorization") (list) to detect duplicates and the Core cookie API (req.getCookies) to detect duplicate naru_at. The API-key scheme parsing and verification chain belong to the APIKEY scope. TokenTransport enum name from 00 §5 (transport(HEADER | COOKIE | BOTH)).

records.title: Login throttling keys, limits and enumeration-resistant 429

acceptanceCriteria.text: 5 failed logins for alice from IP A within 15 minutes -> the 6th attempt from A, even with the correct password, -> 429 code too_many_attempts with a Retry-After header holding a positive number of seconds.
The same sequence for the unknown name nobody -> 429 at the same attempt number with the same status, code and header set.

20 failures from IP A spread over different names (at most 4 per name) -> the next attempt from A without a trusted device -> 429; an attempt from A carrying a valid trusted-device token for a real user is not limited by the IP key.

10 failures for admin from 10 distinct IPs within 15 minutes -> the 11th attempt from a new IP without a trusted device -> 429; the admin's trusted device from that IP is not limited by the user-only key.

A 429 response is written without sleeping: the handler never calls Thread.sleep (a TimeSource-driven test sees the 429 written without waiting); that a 429 runs no hash and is not held to the 1.25T floor is owned by SEC-TOKEN-009 AC-3.
The IP part of the key is req.remoteAddress() as resolved by C6b proxy trust, and IPv6 addresses in one /64 share a key: failures from 2001:db8::1 and 2001:db8::ffff count together.
Builder-configured limits replace the defaults: with the (user, IP) limit set to 3 (builder method name not final) the 4th attempt from the same IP -> 429.
Login throttling applies only to password login: failures for a service account's name do not block API-key authentication of that account.

Throttle keys use the normalized login name (NFKC then toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT), the rule of FR-IAM-003 AC-1; 00 R34 (1)): with the default limits, 5 failed logins for the existing user alice from IP A within 15 minutes spelled "alice", "Alice", "ALICE", "ＡＬＩＣＥ" (fullwidth) and "aLiCe" (one each) -> the 6th attempt from A as "alice", even with the correct password, -> 429 too_many_attempts with Retry-After (one (user, IP) counter, not five); 10 failed logins without a device token from 10 distinct IPs within 15 minutes, alternating "admin" and "ADMIN" -> the 11th attempt as "admin" from a new IP without a trusted device -> 429 (one user-only counter).

records.research: - Decisive facts: the "user" key is the normalized login name and unknown names are counted the same, so 429 never reveals whether an account exists (5th ed., K-6). The IP key exempts trusted devices so an enterprise NAT does not lock out every employee; the user-only key applies only to non-trusted devices so an attacker flooding admin cannot lock out admin's known devices. 429 is answered with Retry-After only; sleeping would exhaust worker threads. Rejected: 05 §8.1 two-key exponential delay with no IP exemption (replaced by R23/R34); progressive delay (R23 withdrawn). records.title: Throttle check order combined with device trust

acceptanceCriteria.text: An attacker exhausts admin's user-only key (10 failures from rotating IPs); admin then logs in from a device holding a valid device token with the correct password -> 200.
Without a device token, an attempt from an IP whose IP key is exhausted -> 429 before UserStore.findByUsername is called (store call counter stays 0).
An attempt whose (user, IP) key is exhausted -> 429 before findByUsername, with or without a trusted-device token.

A device token passing signature, expiry and fingerprint whose user id or ver differs from the findByUsername result, or whose user no longer exists -> treated as no device token: the deferred IP key and the user-only key are checked.
An attacker attaching a device token of their own account while guessing another name -> fingerprint mismatch -> the IP key is checked first.

During the attack in the first criterion, admin from a new device without a device token -> 429 from the user-only key (documented residual risk, 00 §6.4 row 'R34 × 새 기기 admin'); logging in from an existing trusted device (AC-1) still works. The row's other way out, another admin's lockout release, ends this 429: after another admin's DELETE /auth/admin/users/:id/lockout (with or without a configured Lockout), which clears admin's user-only throttle key (FR-FLOW-009 AC-5), the same new-device login with the correct password from an IP whose IP key and (user, IP) key are not exhausted -> 200, while the attacker's IPs stay limited by their IP and (user, IP) keys.

records.title: DeviceTrust signed device token with name fingerprint and per-token failure limit

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decoding an issued device token shows the user id, ver, fingerprint, random value and expiry, and no raw login name.

A token issued at login as alice is trusted for the next login as alice; when the store also resolves alice@example.com to the same user, a login as alice@example.com with that token is not trusted (fingerprint differs).
After logout ?all=true (ver++) or a password change, the old device token is no longer trusted, and the password-change response carries a new device token.
After alice is renamed to alice2 the old token is not trusted for alice2; if another user later takes the name alice, the old token is not trusted for that user either (user id differs).
A token signed under kid k1 stays trusted after the signing key rotates to k2 while k1 remains in the verification set, and is not trusted once k1 is removed.

Per-device-token failure limit (00 R34 (2): 5 failures per 15 minutes, then the token is invalid; §6.4 row 'R34 × 기기 토큰 탈취'). Default limits (SEC-FLOW-011), no Lockout, all requests within one 15-minute window: first exhaust the IP key of IP A6 with 20 failed logins without a device token from A6 for five other names u1..u5, 4 each (SEC-FLOW-011 AC-3; no (user, IP) key reaches 5 and none of alice's keys is touched). Then send 5 failed logins as alice carrying alice's valid device token D from IPs A1..A5, one each (D is trusted, so the IP and user-only keys do not apply, SEC-FLOW-012 step ③, and each (alice, Ai) key holds one failure). Then a login as alice with D and the correct password from A6 -> 429 too_many_attempts from A6's IP key, because D was invalidated by its 5th failure and the request is handled as one without a device token (the same answer as that login sent with no device token). Control: the same sequence with only 4 failures carrying D -> the A6 login with D and the correct password gets 200, because D is still trusted and exempt from the IP key (SEC-FLOW-011 AC-3). In both runs (alice, A6) holds no failure and alice's user-only key holds at most 5 of its 10, so only A6's IP key can answer 429, and it applies only once D has lost trust.

Transport per mode: COOKIE uses the naru_device cookie, which is set only by a response that passed the Origin check (a login that passed it by its Origin, or by its Referer when Origin is absent, being the request's own origin or in trustedOrigins, SEC-FLOW-007 AC-4/AC-5, or a password change with cookie delivery, SEC-FLOW-014 AC-5); HEADER returns body deviceToken and reads only the Naru-Device request header, never the naru_device cookie (00 §5, 33판; R29 (g)); BOTH delivers the device token the way that response delivers its tokens and on read prefers the Naru-Device header, else the naru_device cookie (00 R34, 32판). HEADER, a login carrying only a valid naru_device cookie and no Naru-Device header -> handled as a request without a device token (no trust exemption from the IP and user-only keys).
A token whose 90-day expiry has passed (TimeSource advanced by 90 days plus one second) is not trusted.

records.title: Secret values in auth files stored as enc(...) with AES-256-GCM under an app-supplied master key

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a 32-byte master key, after auth.users().create("alice", "pw-1234567890") the users file holds a passwordHash value matching ^enc\([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\)$; base64url-decoding the payload gives first byte 0x01 and a length of 1 + 12 + (UTF-8 length of the hash string) + 16; the plain hash string occurs nowhere in the file; a new FileUserStore over that file with the same key loads it and a password login as alice with pw-1234567890 succeeds.
Encrypting the same hash value twice gives two different enc(...) strings, and 1,000 encryptions of one value carry 1,000 distinct 96-bit IVs (random IV per write from SecureRandom).

Keys are separated by purpose and values are bound to their place: the key derived for the users-file passwordHash purpose differs from the key derived for the signing-key purpose (package-private derivation test with a fixed master key and a known-answer vector recorded in the test); an enc(...) value copied from the key file into a users-file passwordHash, or from user A's record into user B's record, fails to authenticate and makes the store refuse to load.

Fail closed for the users file: one flipped payload byte, a different master key, a version byte other than 1, or a malformed payload (bad base64url, too short) each make the FileUserStore constructor throw an IOException whose message names the file and the field passwordHash but contains neither the stored value nor key material; start stops with the REL-IAM-004 unreadable-file FAIL, the file is byte-for-byte unchanged, and no login ever reaches the wrong-password path for that record.

Fail closed for the key file: a KeySources.fromFile key file holding a tampered enc(...) value, or opened with a different master key, makes the key read throw an IOException naming the file, Auth build or start fails, the file is unchanged and no new key is generated in its place.

Only JDK APIs present on Android API 21 are used: javax.crypto.Cipher with AES/GCM/NoPadding and GCMParameterSpec(128, iv), javax.crypto.Mac HmacSHA256, java.security.SecureRandom and the internal Base64Url; the animalsnifferMain API 21 check passes, NaruServe-api main dependencies stay [:] and no java.util.Base64 or java.nio.file reference appears (CON-AUTH-003 AC-2).

AuthFileKey (public final class in com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth, name not final): of(byte[]) copies its argument and throws IllegalArgumentException for fewer than 32 bytes; of(String) accepts standard or URL-safe base64 with or without padding that decodes to at least 32 bytes and otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException whose message states the rule without echoing the input; fromEnv() reads the environment variable named by its ENV_VARIABLE constant (NARU_AUTH_FILE_KEY, name not final), returns null when the variable is unset or empty, and throws IllegalArgumentException naming the variable but not its value when the value is invalid.

The master key is never disclosed: AuthFileKey.toString() returns a fixed text without key material, AuthFileKey is not Serializable, and after a test run that creates users, rewrites files and triggers each AC-4 failure, no captured log line, no exception message and no file in the data directory contains the raw key bytes or their base64, base64url or hex encodings, nor any derived key.

records.title: Proxy path and request-target checks: dangerous raw paths answer 400 before any backend connection, and the target origin is pinned

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a mount `app.use("/api/orders", Proxy.to(url))`, the requests `/api/orders/../other/x`, `/api/orders/%2e%2e/other/x`, `/api/orders/%2E%2E/other/x`, `/api/orders/..;/other/x`, `/api/orders/.;x/other/x` and `/api/orders/./x` each get 400 and no backend connection is opened.

The requests `/api/orders/a%2fb`, `/api/orders/a%2Fb`, `/api/orders/a%5cb`, `/api/orders/a%00b` and a path holding one raw backslash byte (0x5C) between `a` and `b` each get 400 and no backend connection is opened.
The requests `/api/orders/%70rivate/x`, `/api/orders/%7Ex`, `/api/orders/%41` and `/api/orders/private;x/y` each get 400 and no backend connection is opened.
The double encodings `/api/orders/%252e%252e/other/x`, `/api/orders/a%252fb` and `/api/orders/%2570rivate` each get 400 and no backend connection is opened.
The empty segments `/api/orders//private/x` and `/api/orders/private//x` each get 400 with no backend connection, while `/api/orders/x/` arrives at the backend as `/api/orders/x/`.

A path or query holding a control character, a space, the byte 0x7F, a non-ASCII byte, `#` or a `%` not followed by two hexadecimal digits (for example `?q=%zz` or a path ending in `%`) gets 400 with no backend connection, while `?x=1&y=%ED%95%9C`, `@`, `:`, `!` and `$` in the path or query arrive at the backend byte for byte.

`/api/orders/@evil.example/x` is forwarded to the configured target host, `/api/orders//evil.example/x` and `/api/orders/%2F%2Fevil.example` get 400, and in no case does the proxy open a connection to any host other than the configured target.

On both the TinyHttpd adapter and the servlet adapter an absolute-form request `GET http://evil.example/api/orders/x` either gets 400, gets 421 from the adapter's default host allowlist before middleware, or is forwarded only to the configured target host, with no connection to `evil.example`, and `GET http://h/api/orders/%2e%2e/x` gets 400 whenever the adapter admits it to middleware.
With `.stripPrefix(true)` every request rejected by AC-1 to AC-7 is still rejected with 400, because the checks run on the raw `originalUrl()` path and query and not on the stripped `url()`.

records.title: Proxy X-Forwarded-* trust rules: X-Forwarded-For appended only for a trusted peer, X-Forwarded-Proto from isSecure(), X-Forwarded-Host from the received Host, other forwarding headers dropped

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-b, proxy, security, forwarded-headers, proxy-trust

acceptanceCriteria.text: On an app with no proxy trust setting, a client sending `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example` over plain HTTP from `127.0.0.1` with `Host: gw.example` makes the backend receive exactly `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` and `X-Forwarded-Host: gw.example`.

For a client connected from the IPv6 loopback address, the `X-Forwarded-For` value the backend receives holds no `[`, `]` or `%`, even when the adapter reports the socket address with brackets or a zone id.
On an app with `trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`, a client outside the CIDR sending `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` makes the backend receive only its socket address as `X-Forwarded-For`.

On the same app a client inside the CIDR sending `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` makes the backend receive `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, <socket address>`, and one sending the two lines `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` and `X-Forwarded-For: 5.6.7.8` makes it receive the single line `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 5.6.7.8, <socket address>`.
On the same app a client inside the CIDR that connects over plain HTTP and sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` makes the backend receive `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, the value of `req.isSecure()`.
On apps with `trustProxyHops(1)` and with the legacy `trustProxy(true)`, AC-4 and AC-5 give the same results as for a client inside the CIDR.

Under every trust setting, including a trusted peer, a client `X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example` is replaced by the received `Host`, and the client's `Forwarded`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Port` and `X-Forwarded-Prefix` headers do not arrive at the backend.

When the socket address is not usable — empty, `unknown` or a host name such as `client.example`, none of which parses as an IPv4 or IPv6 literal after surrounding brackets and a `%zone` suffix are removed — the backend receives no `X-Forwarded-For` line, whether or not the peer is trusted and whether or not the client sent one.

`X-Forwarded-Host` and a preserved `Host` come only from the `Host` header the adapter reports; the proxy never derives them from the request target's authority, so a request the adapter reports with raw path `/api/orders/x` and `Host: a.example` sends `X-Forwarded-Host: a.example`.

Express users know the shape as `xfwd: true` of `http-proxy-middleware`, and the IPv6 form follows Express `req.ip`.

records.title: Proxy request framing checks: ambiguous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding answer 400 or 501 before any backend connection

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-b, proxy, security, framing, smuggling

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request carrying both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` gets 400 and no backend connection is opened.

Requests with two `Content-Length` lines `5` and `6`, with `Content-Length: 5, 6`, with `Content-Length: abc`, with `Content-Length: -1` and with `Content-Length: 99999999999999999999` each get 400 and no backend connection is opened.

Requests with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip`, with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked, chunked` and with the two lines `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` each get 400 and no backend connection is opened.
A request with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked` gets 501 and no backend connection is opened.

Requests with `Content-Length: 5, 5`, with `Content-Length:  5 ` and with the two lines `Content-Length: 5` and `Content-Length: 05` are forwarded with the single line `Content-Length: 5`, and requests with `Transfer-Encoding: CHUNKED` and with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked,` are forwarded chunked.

Requests with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked;x=1` and with an empty `Transfer-Encoding` value get 400, and a request with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip;q=1, chunked` gets 501, all without a backend connection.

The proxy decides framing only from the `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` headers the adapter reports and never from the request's HTTP version, so the same header values give the same answer whatever version the client used.

records.title: Proxy backend response parser: ISO-8859-1 status line and headers, RFC 9112 §6.3 framing stricter than the RFC, interim 1xx skipped, and every malformed response an INVALID_RESPONSE

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-b, proxy, security, response-parser, framing, smuggling

acceptanceCriteria.text: Backends answering `HTTP/1.1 2000 OK`, `HTTP/1.1 20 OK`, `HTTP/1.1 abc OK`, `FOO 200 OK`, `HTTP/1.1 600 X` and `HTTP/1.1 099 X` each make the client receive 502 and `onError` receive a `ProxyException` whose `kind()` is `INVALID_RESPONSE`.

A backend response whose status line and headers together exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`, where the count includes each line's terminator but not the blank line ending the head, interim 1xx heads share the bound with the final head, and the bound is charged before the status line is parsed, so an over-bound malformed status line also fails on the bound.

A response holding an obs-fold continuation line (a header line starting with a space or a horizontal tab), a header value holding the byte 0x00 or 0x7F, or a header name that is not an RFC 9110 token (for example `X A: 1`) gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`.

A final response that can carry a body (not an answer to a HEAD request and not 204 or 304) carrying both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, the two lines `Content-Length: 5` and `Content-Length: 6`, `Content-Length: -1` or `Content-Length: abc` gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`; HEAD, 204 and 304 responses are bodyless first in the RFC 9112 §6.3 order and follow FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 instead.

A final response that can carry a body (not an answer to a HEAD request and not 204 or 304) with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked`, `Transfer-Encoding: identity`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked;x=1` or an empty `Transfer-Encoding` value gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`; HEAD, 204 and 304 responses follow FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 instead.

A backend `101 Switching Protocols` gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`, while a `100 Continue` or `103 Early Hints` interim response followed by a final 200 makes the client receive only the 200 and none of the interim responses.

Responses with `Content-Length: 5, 5` and with the two lines `Content-Length: 5` and `Content-Length: 05` are read as 5-byte bodies and relayed with `Content-Length: 5`, and responses with `Transfer-Encoding: CHUNKED` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked,` are decoded as chunked.
A backend that closes the connection, or resets it, before sending a status line, or after sending only part of the header block, gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`.

A backend header value holding the byte 0xE9 is read as the character U+00E9, because the status line and headers are read as ISO-8859-1, and the proxy hands that character unchanged to the adapter, so through an adapter that writes header characters as ISO-8859-1 (the in-memory test adapter) the client receives the single byte 0xE9; over TinyHttpd 3.1.1, which writes header characters as UTF-8, the client receives 0xC3 0xA9, an adapter-dependent limit this target does not change because the TinyHttpd library is not modified.

During a chunked body, a chunk-size line longer than 4 KiB with its extensions, a chunk size that is not hexadecimal, or a trailer section larger than 64 KiB is an `INVALID_RESPONSE` failure after the response started, while a trailer section within 64 KiB is read and discarded and the decoded body reaches the client.
Every malformed input of AC-1 to AC-5, AC-6's 101, AC-8 and AC-10 has its own automated test whose backend is a raw `java.net.ServerSocket` in test scope writing the exact bytes.

records.requirement: The system shall make the proxy's HTTP/1.1 client parse the backend status line and headers as ISO-8859-1, skip every 1xx interim response other than 101 and read the next one, determine the body length in the order of RFC 9112 §6.3 — a response to a HEAD request and a 204 or 304 response being bodyless before any framing header is considered (FR-PROXY-014) — while, for every other final response, rejecting every transfer coding other than a single `chunked`, reading `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` with the same list parsing as requests, and reading and discarding chunked trailers; and shall treat as `INVALID_RESPONSE` a malformed status line or a status outside `100..599`, a status line and headers together larger than 64 KiB, an obs-fold line, a header name or value failing the header check, a 101 response, a connection closed or reset before the header block is complete, a malformed chunk (including a chunk-size line longer than 4 KiB with its extensions and a trailer section larger than 64 KiB), and, on a final response that can carry a body, both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Length` elements that are not digits or differ, or any `Transfer-Encoding` other than a single `chunked`.

records.title: Proxy https backends: plain connect with the connect timeout, TLS wrap with SNI, certificate and host name verification always on and API 21 safe, TLS failures reported as CONNECT_FAILED

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-b, proxy, security, tls, api21

acceptanceCriteria.text: An https backend with a certificate from an untrusted CA, an https backend whose certificate names a host other than the target host, and an https backend that closes the connection during the TLS handshake each give 502 with `kind()` `CONNECT_FAILED`, and with `.retries(2)` each of the three backends sees exactly one TCP connection.

With `.sslSocketFactory(factory)` whose trust store holds that private CA, a request reaches the first backend of AC-1, while the backend whose certificate names another host still gives 502 with `kind()` `CONNECT_FAILED`.

The proxy layers TLS with `createSocket(plainSocket, targetHost, port, true)` for every https target, which a recording `.sslSocketFactory` observes with the target host name for a target such as `https://localhost:<port>`; and for a target whose host name contains a dot (for example `https://backend.test:<port>`), resolved to the loopback address through a package-private test resolver seam, the SNI server name the https backend receives in the TLS ClientHello is that host name (the JDK sends no SNI for the dotless name `localhost`, so that name is not the SNI oracle).

A recording `SSLSocketFactory` given to `.sslSocketFactory` receives `createSocket(Socket, String, int, boolean)` with an already connected plain socket, the target host, the target port and `true`, and none of its `createSocket` methods that connect by themselves is called.

With `.connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS).totalTimeout(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`, a backend that accepts the TCP connection and never answers the TLS handshake gives 504 with `kind()` `TOTAL_TIMEOUT` after about 1 second, because the handshake also runs under the total-timeout watchdog.

With the reflective `setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm` path turned off through a package-private test switch, the proxy still verifies the host name through the check it holds — its built-in certificate host name matcher unless a package-private test seam injects another `HostnameVerifier` — calling it once with the target host name and the handshake session after the handshake: an injected recording verifier sees exactly one call with the target host, a verifier answering false gives 502 `CONNECT_FAILED` with no request bytes sent, and a verifier answering true lets the request reach the backend; the JDK's `HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier()`, which rejects every host on a JVM, is never used.

The API 21 animal-sniffer check passes on `NaruServe-proxy` with no `@IgnoreJRERequirement` or other exemption in its main sources, and its main class files hold no direct method reference to `javax/net/ssl/SSLParameters.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm`.

No public method of `Proxy` turns off certificate or host name verification; its only TLS option is `sslSocketFactory(SSLSocketFactory)` (IR-PROXY-001 AC-3), and verification of the host name stays on with it, as AC-2 shows.

The proxy's own host name check runs after every handshake on every runtime, Android or not and whether or not the endpoint identification reads back: with an `.sslSocketFactory` over a private CA whose trust manager is an `X509ExtendedTrustManager` that checks only the chain, one whose `createSocket` completes the handshake before returning, and one whose delegating `SSLSocket` keeps the `SSLParameters` it was given without applying the identification, a backend whose certificate names another host gives 502 `CONNECT_FAILED` with no request bytes sent, while with a delegating private-CA factory a backend whose certificate names the target host is reached.

The built-in host name matcher accepts `localhost` for a certificate with dNSName `localhost` or `LOCALHOST`, `a.example.test` for `*.example.test`, and `127.0.0.1` for iPAddress `127.0.0.1`, and rejects `a.b.example.test` and `example.test` for `*.example.test`, `a.example.test` for `a*.example.test` or `*.test`-style wildcards outside the leftmost whole label, `127.0.0.1` for a dNSName `127.0.0.1`, and any host for a certificate whose only match would be its subject common name.

records.requirement: The system shall make the proxy reach an `https` target by connecting a plain `Socket` with `connect(address, connectTimeout)` and wrapping it with `SSLSocketFactory.createSocket(plain, host, port, true)` — the JDK default factory, or the one given to `.sslSocketFactory` — so that SNI carries the target host name, run the TLS handshake with `SO_TIMEOUT` set to the connect timeout and under the total-timeout watchdog, always verify the certificate chain (through the factory's trust managers) and the target host name, the latter on every runtime by the proxy's own check of the handshake session's peer leaf certificate after the handshake, whatever the factory or socket does with `SSLParameters`, with `SSLParameters.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS")` also set by reflection where that method exists as a second layer, offer no option that turns either check off, send no request byte before both checks pass, and report every TLS handshake or verification failure as `CONNECT_FAILED` except a handshake timeout, which is `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, and a handshake ended by the total-timeout watchdog, which is `TOTAL_TIMEOUT`. The proxy's host name check matches a DNS host name case-insensitively against the certificate's `dNSName` subject alternative names, where `*` is allowed only as the whole leftmost label and matches exactly one non-empty label, matches an IP literal target only against `iPAddress` subject alternative names, and does not fall back to the subject common name.
records.rationale:
AC-1 ← PRD-161, PRD-162, PRD-220, PRD-227; AC-2 ← PRD-165, PRD-220; AC-3 ← PRD-159, PRD-220; AC-4 ← PRD-159; AC-5 ← PRD-160, PRD-112; fills: PRD-160 / hole / for AC-5, the request bounds the handshake with the connect timeout but does not say what bounds a handshake whose bytes keep arriving, so the total-timeout watchdog also covers it (design D-063); AC-6 ← PRD-162, PRD-163; fills: PRD-163 / defect / for AC-6, on the JDK the default `HostnameVerifier` of `HttpsURLConnection` rejects every host, so the Android fallback path is verified through an injected verifier instead of the platform default (feasibility run 2026-11-14.naruserve.0120.v01, probe on OpenJDK 17); AC-7 ← PRD-164 (design D-067); AC-8 ← PRD-161, PRD-165. `createSocket(host, port)` connects at once and cannot apply a connect timeout, hence the plain connect and the layered socket; `SSLSocket` does not verify host names by itself, so the implementation must. `setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm` exists only from Android API 24, and a runtime branch still fails the API 21 signature check, so it is called by reflection rather than exempted (design D-067). Express users set the same through the `agent` and `secure` options of `http-proxy-middleware`; NaruServe offers no `secure: false` counterpart, and a private CA is given through `.sslSocketFactory`.
- [2026-11-14] fills: PRD-220 / defect / for AC-3, the JDK sends no SNI for a dotless host such as localhost (OpenJDK 17 probe, feasibility run 2026-11-14.naruserve.0120.v01), so the SNI clause of the request is observed with a dotted test host resolved through a test seam, and the host handed to createSocket is observed for every target.
records.implementationNotes: - After the handshake, set `SO_TIMEOUT` to the read timeout for the rest of the exchange. Keep a reference to the plain socket: the watchdog closes the plain socket, never the `SSLSocket`, because `SSLSocket.close()` sends `close_notify` and may block behind a writer (watchdog requirement). Map a failure during the handshake or host name verification in this order: first, when the total-timeout watchdog recorded that its deadline fired before it closed the plain socket, the failure is `TOTAL_TIMEOUT` whatever exception the close surfaced as (typically a `SocketException`, not a `SocketTimeoutException`), as AC-5 requires; otherwise a handshake `SocketTimeoutException` is `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`; every other `SSLException` or `IOException` is `CONNECT_FAILED`, which the retry rules never retry. Check the watchdog's recorded deadline before classifying the exception, the same way the body-write path does for `WRITE_TIMEOUT` and `TOTAL_TIMEOUT` (FR-PROXY-017). On an `http` target an `.sslSocketFactory` is accepted and unused (FR-PROXY-002 AC-9).

records.title: Servlet adapter conformance for req.socketAddress(), hop and CIDR proxy trust and isSecure()

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a Servlet request whose `getRemoteAddr()` is `10.0.0.1` and which carries `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7`, `req.socketAddress()` is `10.0.0.1` under the default configuration, under `app.trustProxyHops(1)` and under `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`.

Under `app.trustProxyHops(1)` and under `app.trustProxyCidrs("10.0.0.0/8")`, the same request gives `req.remoteAddress()` = `203.0.113.7`; with `getRemoteAddr()` = `198.51.100.20` and the CIDR setting it gives `198.51.100.20`.

With `isSecure()` = `false`, `app.trustProxyHops(1)` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, `req.isSecure()` is `true`; with `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7` (one entry) and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https, https` (two entries, a count mismatch under the SEC-ENGINE-003 XFP rule) it is `false`.
A shared case table of peer, setting and headers runs on the Servlet adapter and on the in-memory adapter and yields identical `socketAddress()`, `remoteAddress()` and `isSecure()` values.

For every combination of forwarding headers (`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `Forwarded`) in the case table, `ServletExchange.remoteAddress()` and `ServletExchange.isSecure()` equal the `getRemoteAddr()` and `isSecure()` values captured at construction; a recording `HttpServletRequest` proxy shows that the only `getHeaders` calls are the snapshot loop over `getHeaderNames()`, that `getHeader` is never called for those three names, and that `getRemoteHost()` is never called (no reverse DNS); the observed container values are recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md` and `docs/api/en/servlet.md`.

records.rationale: 00 §2 lists Base64Url, HmacSigner and ConstantTime as internal (non-public, not contract-stable) building blocks for JWT, CSRF, device tokens and API key comparison; R8 (kid, derived keys) and R47 (constant-time SHA-256 compare) depend on them. java.util.Base64 is API 26 and cannot be used on API 21.
records.research:
- Decisive facts: java.util.Base64 is API 26+, so base64url is hand-written (01 §2.1). javax.crypto.Mac is not thread-safe: use Mac.getInstance per call or a ThreadLocal (01 §2.1).
- Ground truth: strict decode rejects padding, whitespace and the standard alphabet so one token has exactly one valid encoding (06 AUTH-T03, T04: a signature whose last character is swapped for one decoding to the same bytes must be rejected).
- Pitfall: do not rely on MessageDigest.isEqual; older Android implementations were not constant time. Use an XOR-accumulate loop over the full length (01 §2.1). 04 §2.4.1 still says MessageDigest.isEqual for bcrypt; 00 lists ConstantTime as the primitive, so ConstantTime wins.
- Rejected: exposing these as public API (00 §2 marks internal as no compatibility promise). Reopen only if an app-facing SPI needs them.

records.title: MiniJson strict parser and writer with CLAIMS and FILE profiles

acceptanceCriteria.text: Under CLAIMS, a document nested 3 levels deep is rejected and a document nested 2 levels deep is accepted; under FILE, depth 8 is accepted and depth 9 is rejected

Under CLAIMS, input larger than 8 KB or containing a string longer than 1 KB is rejected before any value is returned; under FILE, input larger than the configured total (default 8 MB) or a string longer than 64 KB is rejected

In both profiles {"alg":"HS256","alg":"none"} (duplicate key) is rejected, NaN and Infinity literals are rejected, an invalid escape such as \x41 is rejected, and any non-whitespace character after the top-level value is rejected

records.research:
- Decisive facts: the JDK has no bcrypt and javax.crypto Blowfish cannot be used because EksBlowfish needs direct control of the key schedule repeated 2^cost times; Blowfish is written from P-array (18), S-boxes (4x256 pi constants, ~4 KB) and 16 rounds; output is "OrpheanBeholderScryDoubt" encrypted 64 times and cut to 23 bytes (04 §2.4.1).
- Pitfall: a planted cost-31 hash in the DB would pin a CPU; hence the cap checked before any work (04 §2.4.1 rule 3).
- Pitfall: $2x$ marks the old crypt_blowfish sign-extension bug; accepting it would verify against wrong hashes (rule 1).
- Licensing: write from the Provos-Mazieres 1999 paper and the OpenBSD spec; do not port jBCrypt (ISC notice would be required).
- Ground truth: bcrypt is a legacy verifier; successful bcrypt login always rehashes to PBKDF2 (R38 upper side). hash() also works but PBKDF2 stays the default (FIPS/NIST).
- Residual risk: a never-logged-in high-cost bcrypt account takes longer than the 1.25T floor and is distinguishable (R38 "remaining risk").
records.implementationNotes: - utils.auth.password.BcryptPasswordHasher, utils.auth.password.PasswordHashers.bcrypt(), utils.auth.internal.Blowfish (int arrays and bit ops only; Java 8 / API 21 safe). Runs inside the hash slot (REL-TOKEN slot requirement). Android cost-10 timing is unmeasured (04 §2.4.1, 00 §12).

records.title: Constant-work login and the 1.25T failure-response floor

acceptanceCriteria.text: For an unknown username, a known PBKDF2 user (stored iteration count equal to the target) with a wrong password, an MD5-legacy user with a wrong password, and a service account or null-hash user, each attempt runs exactly one target-cost PBKDF2 computation and takes exactly one slot (counted through an instrumented hasher); an MD5-legacy user and a bcrypt-legacy user with the correct password each run the legacy verify plus exactly one target-cost PBKDF2 computation inside one slot (00 R38: legacy users run the legacy verify then the dummy PBKDF2), and the rehash runs outside that slot (PERF-TOKEN-002 AC-1)

With HashCost.calibrate(250 ms) (T = 250 ms, PERF-TOKEN-001 AC-6 and AC-7) and a measurement stub, a fast fake hasher and an injected scheduler, a failed login response is scheduled at 312.5 ms plus a jitter value in the range 0-50 ms after the request started, never earlier
A 503 caused by a full slot queue is also delayed to the 1.25T floor; a 429 throttle response is sent without the floor and runs no hash (00 §6.4 R38 x R34)
A successful login is not delayed by the floor
While failure responses are waiting for the floor, the waiting holds no worker thread: 50 delayed failures with 2 worker threads do not block a concurrent non-auth request

Login with a correct password for a PBKDF2 user whose stored iteration count is below the target verifies with the stored count, not the target count, and runs exactly one PBKDF2 computation (R38 edition 8)

Under HashCost.fixed(n), T is the duration of one PBKDF2 computation at n iterations measured once at start (open question Q45, decided 2026-11-02): with HashCost.fixed(n), a measurement stub that reports 200 ms for that start measurement and an injected scheduler, a failed login response is scheduled at 250 ms plus a jitter value in the range 0-50 ms after the request started, never earlier, and no further measurement runs per request.

Delayed responses written from the floor scheduler thread are delivered intact on the real adapters (00 §12 verification limit for the R38 delayed response): with the TinyHttpd adapter and with the Servlet adapter, each started on a local port, a failed login answered after the floor is received by the client with status 401, its JSON body and its headers unchanged, and a concurrent non-auth request on the same server is answered while the failure waits.

records.requirement: Every password login attempt shall take one hash slot (or get the 503 of a full slot queue, REL-TOKEN-001) and run exactly one PBKDF2 computation inside it (the real verify at the stored iteration count for PBKDF2 users, the legacy verify plus a target-cost dummy PBKDF2 for legacy users, a target-cost dummy PBKDF2 for unknown users and users without a password), and every failure response of an attempt, including that 503, shall be sent no earlier than max(1.25T, elapsed) plus 0-50 ms random jitter after the request started, where T is the current calibrated target time, waiting on a scheduler rather than a blocked thread; an attempt is a login request that reached the hash step (④) of SEC-FLOW-012, that is a request with a well-formed JSON body holding a non-empty string password that also passed the login throttle and device-trust checks of SEC-FLOW-012 steps ①–③, so requests rejected earlier by the transport check, the multiple-credential or API-key procedure, the body format (415), the CSRF/Origin check (403), the request shape (400 for a missing, non-string or empty password) or the login throttle (429 too_many_attempts from SEC-FLOW-012 steps ①–③) take no slot, run no hash and are not held to the floor.
records.rationale: 00 §6.3 R38 (all attempts take one slot and run target-cost PBKDF2 once, edition 6 P-13; failure floor 1.25T + 0-50 ms jitter for all failures incl. 503, excluding 429, edition 9 T-3; scheduler wait without a held thread; real verify uses stored iterations, edition 8 S-5); R47 (6)(7) service account password login uses the same timing.
records.research:
- Decisive facts: equal work per attempt makes queue length, 503 rate and duration independent of account type, closing the user-enumeration timing channel (R38).
- Ground truth: the floor 1.25T covers the case where a stored hash is cheaper than the target; legacy fast hashes are padded to it.
- Residual risk (documented, not fixed): never-logged-in high-cost bcrypt accounts and dormant PBKDF2 hashes above 125 percent of target take longer than the floor and are distinguishable; reduce with dormant-account wrapping (04 §2.4).
- Pitfall: 429 responses do no hashing, so applying the floor would only add latency; the limit response does not reveal account existence because unknown names are counted the same (R34).
- Verification limit: whether writing the response from the scheduler thread is safe is to be confirmed at implementation (00 §12, "지연 응답(R38)").
- API key verification is SHA-256 and does not use the slot or the floor (R47 (2)).
- [2026-11-02] Decided (Q45): under HashCost.fixed(n), T is one start-time timing of a hash at n iterations (AC-7; PERF-TOKEN-001 AC-3/AC-6). The 00 §12 scheduler-thread limit is closed by an adapter test on TinyHttpd and Servlet (AC-8). Q39 needed no change: the statement already excludes the request-shape 400 from the floor, because no hash ran. A Lockout refusal does reach step 4, so it is floored (FR-FLOW-009 AC-2).
records.implementationNotes: - Lives in the password Authenticator path used by POST /auth/login (FLOW owns the endpoint, registered with methodAsync("POST", ...)). Dummy hash is a PBKDF2 hash at the current target computed once at build(). Delay via a ScheduledExecutorService daemon thread completing the async response; time via TimeSource/System.nanoTime (no java.time). Uses HashCost T (PERF-TOKEN-001) and the slot pool (REL-TOKEN-001).

completedWork.summary: [req] FR-PROXY-015 - Proxy failures before the response delivered: backend-side failures go to the app error flow as ProxyException with kind and cause (CONNECT_FAILED for refused, unresolvable or TLS failures; INVALID_RESPONSE for malformed or truncated responses) with no proxy-written body or logger entry, the default error page names neither target host nor port (causes printed by class name only), an early backend response after a failed body write is relayed best-effort with no further client body read, and watchdog write/total deadlines keep WRITE_TIMEOUT/TOTAL_TIMEOUT; tests ProxyErrorsTest and ProxyTlsTest; wave-18 merge 94a3c1f with host fix 6c51bda; loop P r2 pass; regression 4627/0

[req] FR-PROXY-017 - Proxy timeouts delivered: four finite per-Proxy timeouts (connect 10 s covering TCP connect and TLS handshake, write 60 s excluding client-body waits, read 60 s, total 5 min including retries), first one reached applies, CONNECT_TIMEOUT/WRITE_TIMEOUT/READ_TIMEOUT/TOTAL_TIMEOUT as 504 before the response and a client abort plus log after it, with a final deadline check before the response status (no backend headers on 504) and the total timeout ending a trickled client body; tests ProxyTimeoutsTest; wave-18 merge 94a3c1f with host fix b6f88f5; loop P r2 pass; regression 4627/0

[req] FR-PROXY-016 - A backend failure after the response was handed to res.relay (body shorter than its Content-Length, malformed chunk, read timeout between body bytes or total timeout) is logged once to the app logger as a ProxyException of its kind through Logger.error(String, Throwable) and then thrown from the package-private relayed body stream as an IOException caused by that ProxyException, so the framework aborts the client connection without the proxy calling res.abort; covered by ProxyMidResponseFailureTest with a recording Response and a recording logger; wave-17 merge 3a6f8e0, loop P r1 pass, regression 4598/0.

[req] FR-PROXY-014 - The proxy hands the backend body to res.relay as a stream with the Content-Length value, -1 for a decoded chunked body and -1 for a body read until close, and treats HEAD, 204 and 304 responses as bodyless before any framing rule, reading no body bytes and passing the single Content-Length value from the shared list parser for HEAD and 304 (else -1) and -1 for 204, so their framing headers never raise INVALID_RESPONSE; covered by ProxyResponseBodyTest with a recording Response; wave-17 merge 3a6f8e0, loop P r1 pass, regression 4598/0.

[req] SEC-PROXY-004 - The proxy's backend response parser reads the status line and headers as ISO-8859-1 within a 64 KiB head bound charged before the status line is parsed, skips 100 and 103 interim responses, decides framing in RFC 9112 §6.3 order with HEAD, 204 and 304 bodyless first, accepts only a single chunked coding, discards chunked trailers within 64 KiB, and maps every malformed status line, obs-fold, bad header name or value, 101, early close or reset, conflicting or invalid framing, Transfer-Encoding on HTTP/1.0 and oversized chunk-size line or trailer to INVALID_RESPONSE (502 or a mid-response abort); covered by BackendResponseParserTest over raw ServerSocket backends; wave-17 merge 3a6f8e0, loop P r1 pass, regression 4598/0.

[req] REL-PROXY-001 - the proxy runs synchronously on the request thread through connect, request write and response header read, takes the concurrency slot and starts the total-timeout watchdog only after every check and req.bodyStream, and releases the slot, the watchdog reservations and the backend socket exactly once at the first of relayed-stream close(), res.onAbort or the middleware exit; a client disconnect during a silent backend is released by the read or total timeout (LP-1 carried to wave-18); tests ProxyExchangeTest and ProxyLifetimeSocketTest; wave-16 merge 917681b; regression 4511/0

[req] FR-PROXY-019 - maxConcurrent(n) gives the proxy a new lock-free AtomicInteger counter shared by reference by objects derived through other option methods (a fresh one on each maxConcurrent call) and across apps; a request at the limit gets 503 CONCURRENCY_LIMIT at once without a backend connection, slots are held until relayed bodies end, and the default stays unlimited; tests ProxyConcurrencyTest; wave-16 merge 917681b; regression 4511/0

[req] FR-PROXY-010 - the proxy runs its checks in one fixed order (WebSocket upgrade to next(), method token, CONNECT and TRACE 405, request-target and path segments, header names, values and Host lines, body framing, req.bodyStream(limit), concurrency slot, watchdog start) so a request failing several gets the first answer, and throws its own 400, 405 and 501 answers into the error flow as plain HttpException with a null message, not ProxyException; tests ProxyCheckOrderTest; wave-16 merge 917681b; regression 4511/0

[req] FR-PROXY-012 - removeResponseHeader(name) skips backend lines of that name while keeping a value the app set, responseHeader(name, value) sets the value with res.header after the header copy and the Location rewrite so it replaces backend and app values, names compare case-insensitively, and the later call for a name wins; tests ProxyFixedResponseHeadersTest; wave-15 merge 7602bee, loop P pass r1, regression 4476/0

[req] FR-PROXY-013 - unless rewriteLocation(false), a backend Location that is a same-origin absolute URL or network-path reference under the target base path becomes an origin-less path with the client-side prefix (req.baseUrl() under stripPrefix), comparing scheme and host case-insensitively with default ports, keeping query and fragment, using / for an empty path, guarding network-path-looking results with a leading /., dropping user information, and leaving relative, foreign and ungrammatical values unchanged; tests ProxyLocationRewriteTest, LocationRewriterTest; wave-15 merge 7602bee, loop P pass r1, regression 4476/0

[req] FR-PROXY-009 - the proxy forwards the received method token unchanged over HTTP/1.1 including extension methods, answers 400 to a non-token method and 405 with Allow to CONNECT and TRACE (case-insensitive) without a backend connection, passes WebSocket upgrades to next() so app.ws routes win in either order, forwards other Upgrade requests without Upgrade and HTTP2-Settings, and never calls next() after forwarding; tests ProxyMethodTest; wave-15 merge 7602bee, loop P pass r1, regression 4476/0

[req] OPS-BUILD-004 - CLAUDE.md module line names NaruServe-proxy as the eleventh module and eighth API 21 check target (reverse proxy on NaruServe-api only, included by no other module), and the Maven-mode full build stays green with the baseline tests kept; tests BuildLayoutTest plus the build command; wave-14 merge 196378f, loop P pass r3, regression 4476/0

[req] CON-BUILD-020 - NaruServe-proxy joins the API 21 animal-sniffer check with no exemption and the javax.servlet class-reference check of the eight Android modules, and its main classes fail the build on any reference to a com/snoworca/naruserve package with an internal or spi segment or to android/, javax/servlet/, com/google/gson/, com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/ or kotlin/ (anchored at the name start); tests BuildChecksTest TestKit probes; wave-14 merge 196378f with fixes ee74726, 4d6e517, loop P pass r3, regression 4476/0

[req] SEC-PROXY-005 - https backends reached by a plain connect under the connect timeout and a TLS layer via createSocket(plain, host, port, true) with SNI, handshake under SO_TIMEOUT and the total-timeout watchdog, certificate chain and host name always verified (own SAN matcher after every handshake plus reflective endpoint identification, API 21 safe), no option to turn verification off, TLS failures as CONNECT_FAILED, handshake timeout as CONNECT_TIMEOUT or TOTAL_TIMEOUT; tests ProxyTlsTest, CertificateHostnamesTest; wave-14 merge 196378f with fixes 32cda82, 98c25ce, loop P pass r3, regression 4476/0

[req] IR-PROXY-002 - public final ProxyException extending HttpException with the nested Kind enum of seven proxy failure kinds, kind() accessor, status derived from the kind (502/504/503), null message, cause kept, and exactly one public constructor (Kind, @Nullable Throwable) usable through next.error to onError; tests ProxyExceptionTest; wave-14 merge 196378f, loop P pass r3, regression 4476/0

[req] FR-PROXY-006 - the proxy forwards the method token, path, query exactly as encoded and body bytes unchanged, building the backend request target as the base path followed by the raw originalUrl() by default or by url() under stripPrefix(true), forwarding the mount path itself as / (or /base/) and answering 400 with no backend connection when the stripped remainder is not a raw suffix of the checked originalUrl(); tests ProxyRequestTargetTest over the in-memory adapter and TinyHttpd; merged at 1c94acb; regression 4369/0

[req] FR-PROXY-004 - the proxy sends the target host as Host (port only off the scheme default, IPv6 in brackets) and the received Host as X-Forwarded-Host, keeps the received Host unchanged under preserveHost(true), sends the target host and no X-Forwarded-Host when no Host or an empty Host value is received, and answers 400 with no backend connection for several Host lines before the framing and https checks; tests ProxyHostHeaderTest over the in-memory adapter and a TinyHttpd socket; merged at 1c94acb; regression 4369/0

[req] FR-PROXY-001 - Proxy.to(url) hand-parses the target URL (package-private TargetUrl) and accepts only an http or https scheme, an ASCII host name of valid labels, an IPv4 literal or a bracketed IPv6 literal without zone id, an optional port 1..65535 and an optional base path whose trailing slashes are removed and which must pass the SEC-PROXY-001 path checks; a query, fragment, user information, other schemes, a missing host, bad literals or ports throw IllegalArgumentException at the call and null throws NullPointerException; the base path prefixes every forwarded path; tests ProxyTargetUrlTest; merged at 1c94acb; regression 4369/0

[req] SEC-PROXY-001 - the proxy checks the raw originalUrl() path and query before any backend connection, whatever stripPrefix says, and answers 400 for dot segments, empty segments, semicolons, encoded unreserved characters, %2f %5c %00 and raw backslash, double encodings, controls, space, 0x7F, non-ASCII, # and bad percent escapes, while the configured target origin stays pinned (absolute-form requests reach only the target or get 421 on TinyHttpd and the servlet adapter); package-private PathChecker reused for the Proxy.to base path; tests ProxyPathChecksTest, PathCheckerTest, ServletProxyAbsoluteFormTest; merged at 1c94acb; regression 4369/0
wave-12: proxy request header forwarding, request body forwarding, request body limit and FR-PROXY-021 landed on the integration branch; FR-PROXY-003 implemented with AC-8 deferred to wave-19

summary.goal: Let apps read the raw request (body stream, header enumeration) and write repeated response headers through the public API, and ship an optional naruserve-proxy module whose Proxy.to(url) forwards requests transparently with safe defaults on Java 8 / Android API 21.
